Liebe strebt nach Objekten; ihre Hauptfunktion, von
der Natur in jeder Weise begünstigt, ist die Erhaltung
der Art. So traten zuerst Ichtriebe und Objekttriebe
einander gegenüber. Für die Energie der letzteren, und
ausschließlich für sie, führte ich den Namen Libido ein;
somit lief der Gegensatz zwischen den Ichtrieben und
den aufs Objekt gerichteten „libidinösen“ "Trieben der
Liebe im weitesten Sinne.

man kam über diese Unstimmigkeit hinweg; der Sadis-

rungen der Libido, ein Kampf, in dem das Ich gesiegt
hatte, aber um den Preis schwerer Leiden und Ver-
zichte.

nicht wie ein längst überwundener Irrtum klingt. Doch

Begriff der Libido geriet in Gefahr.

fassen wolle. Warum das geschehen müsse, wissen wir
nicht; das sei eben das Werk des Eros. Diese Men-
schenmengen sollen lıbidinös aneinander gebunden
werden; die Notwendigkeit allein, die Vorteile der
Arbeitsgemeinschaft werden sie nicht zusammen-
halten. Diesem Programm der Kultur widersetzt sich
aber der natürliche Aggressionstrieb der Menschen, die
Feindseligkeit eines gegen alle und aller gegen einen.

Dieser Aggressionstrieb ist der Abkömmling und
Hauptvertreter des 'I'odestriebes, den wir neben dem
Eros gefunden haben, der sich mit ihm in die Weltherr-
schaft teilt. Und nun, meine ich, ist uns der Sinn der
Kulturentwicklung nicht mehr dunkel. Sie muß uns
den Kampf zwischen Eros und Tod, Lebenstrieb und
Destruktionstrieb zeigen, wie er sich an der Menschen-
art vollzieht. Dieser Kampf ist der wesentliche Inhalt
des Lebens überhaupt und darum ist die Kulturent-
wicklung kurzweg zu bezeichnen als der Lebenskampf

7

[Source scan 101 · printed page 98](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n101/mode/1up)
98 Der Kampf zwischen Eros und Todestrieb

der Menschenart.‘ Und diesen Streit der Giganten
wollen unsere Kinderfrauen beschwichtigen mit dem
„Eiapopeia vom Himmel“ !

ı) Wahrscheinlich mit der näheren Bestimmung: wie er sich
von einem gewissen, noch zu erratenden, Ereignis an gestalten
mußte.
[Source scan 92 · printed page 89](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n92/mode/1up)
VI

In no work have I had so strongly the feeling as this time that I am presenting matters generally known, offering up paper and ink, and, in further consequence, typesetting work and printer's ink, in order to relate things that are actually self-evident. I therefore gladly take it up when the appearance arises that the recognition of a particular, independent aggressive drive signifies a modification of the psychoanalytic theory of drives.

It will become apparent that this is not so, that it is merely a matter of grasping more sharply a turn that has long since been made and pursuing it into its consequences. Of all the slowly developed parts of analytic theory, the theory of drives has groped its way forward with the greatest difficulty. Yet it was so indispensable to the whole that something had to be put in its place. In the complete perplexity of the beginnings, the dictum of the
[Source scan 93 · printed page 90](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n93/mode/1up)
90 The development of the

poet-philosopher Schiller gave me the first foothold, that “Hunger and Love” hold together the machinery of the world. Hunger could count as the representative of those drives that seek to preserve the individual; love strives for objects; its principal function, favoured by nature in every way, is the preservation of the species. Thus ego-drives and object-drives first confronted one another. For the energy of the latter, and exclusively for them, I introduced the name libido; thus the opposition ran between the ego-drives and the “libidinal” drives of love directed toward the object in the widest sense.

One of these object-drives, the sadistic one, admittedly distinguished itself by the fact that its aim was anything but loving; it also evidently aligned itself in some respects with the ego-drives, and could not conceal its close affinity with drives of mastery without libidinal aim, but one got over this inconsistency; sadism evidently belonged to sexual life after all, the cruel game could replace the tender one. Neurosis appeared as the outcome of a struggle between the interest of self-preservation and the demands of libido, a struggle in which the ego had triumphed, but at the cost of severe sufferings and renunciations.
Every analyst will admit that even today this does not sound like a long-surmounted error. Yet
[Source scan 94 · printed page 91](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n94/mode/1up)
psychoanalytic theory of drives 91

a modification became indispensable when our research progressed from the repressed to the repressing, from the object-drives to the ego. Decisive here was the introduction of the concept of narcissism, i.e. the insight that the ego itself is cathected with libido, indeed is libido's original abode and in a certain sense also remains its headquarters. This narcissistic libido turns toward objects, thus becomes object-libido, and can be transformed back into narcissistic libido. The concept of narcissism made it possible to grasp analytically traumatic neurosis, as well as many affections close to the psychoses and the latter themselves. The interpretation of transference neuroses as attempts by the ego to defend itself against sexuality did not have to be abandoned, but the concept of libido came into danger.

Since the ego-drives too were libidinal, for a while it seemed unavoidable to make libido coincide with drive-energy in general, as C. G. Jung had already wished earlier. Yet something remained, like a certainty not yet capable of being grounded, that the drives cannot all be of the same kind. I took the next step in “Beyond the Pleasure Principle” (1920), when the compulsion to repeat and the conservative character of drive-life first struck me. Proceeding from speculations about the beginning of life and from biological parallels, I drew the conclusion that, besides
[Source scan 95 · printed page 92](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n95/mode/1up)
92 The discovery of the death-

the drive to preserve living substance and to gather it together into ever greater unities,¹ there must be another, opposed to it, that strives to dissolve these unities and lead them back to the primordial, inorganic state. Thus, besides Eros, a death drive; from the combined and opposing action of these two, the phenomena of life could be explained. Now it was not easy to demonstrate the activity of this assumed death drive. The manifestations of Eros were conspicuous and noisy enough; one could assume that the death drive worked silently within the living being toward its dissolution, but that was naturally no proof. The idea led further that a portion of the drive turns toward the external world and then comes to light as a drive toward aggression and destruction.

The drive would thus itself be compelled into the service of Eros, in that the living being destroyed other things, animate as well as inanimate, instead of its own self. Conversely, the cessation of this aggression outward would have to increase the self-destruction that is in any case always proceeding. At the same time, one could infer from this example that the

1) The opposition into which the restless tendency of Eros to spread here enters with the generally conservative nature of the drives is striking and may become the starting-point of further questions.
[Source scan 96 · printed page 93](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n96/mode/1up)
or destruction drive 93

two kinds of drive seldom—perhaps never—occur in isolation from one another, but alloy themselves with one another in various, greatly fluctuating proportions and thereby make themselves unrecognizable to our judgment. In sadism, long known as a component drive of sexuality, one would have such a particularly strong alloy of the striving for love with the destruction drive, as in its counterpart, masochism, a union of destruction directed inward with sexuality, through which the otherwise imperceptible tendency becomes conspicuous and palpable.

The assumption of the death or destruction drive has encountered resistance even in analytic circles; I know that there is often an inclination to ascribe everything found dangerous and hostile in love rather to an original bipolarity of its own nature. At first I advanced the views developed here only tentatively, but in the course of time they have gained such power over me that I can no longer think otherwise. I think they are theoretically incomparably more serviceable than all possible others; they produce that simplification without neglect or violation of the facts for which we strive in scientific work. I recognize that in sadism and masochism we have the strongly alloyed with eroticism
[Source scan 97 · printed page 94](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n97/mode/1up)
94 Destruction and aggression

the manifestations of the destructive instinct directed outward and inward always before us, but I no longer understand how we could overlook the ubiquity of non-erotic aggression and destruction and fail to accord it the place due to it in the interpretation of life. (The destructive urge turned inward, if it is not erotically tinged, usually eludes perception.) I recall my own resistance when the idea of the destructive instinct first appeared in psychoanalytic literature, and how long it took before I became receptive to it. That others showed, and still show, the same rejection surprises me less. For children do not like to hear it when man's innate inclination toward “evil,” toward aggression, destruction, and thus also toward cruelty, is mentioned.

After all, God created them in the image of
His own perfection; one does not wish to be reminded
how difficult it is to reconcile the—despite the assur-
ances of Christian Science—undeniable existence of
evil with His omnipotence or His all-goodness. The
Devil would be the best expedient for exculpating God;
in this he would assume the same economically reliev-
ing role as the Jew in the world of the Aryan ideal. But
even then: one can surely demand an accounting from
God just as well
[Source scan 98 · printed page 95](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n98/mode/1up)
The Devil and Evil 95

for the existence of the Devil as for that of the evil
which he embodies. In the face of these difficulties, it
is advisable for everyone, at a suitable point, to make
a deep bow before the profoundly moral nature of man;
it helps one to gain general popularity, and much will
be forgiven one for it.'

The name libido may again be used for the manifesta-
tions of the force of Eros, in order to distinguish them
from the energy of the death instinct.” It is ad-
1) The identification of the evil principle with the destructive instinct is particularly convincing in Goethe's Mephistopheles:

“For all that comes into being
Is worthy that it should perish.
Thus all that you call sin,
Destruction, in short, evil,
Is my proper element.”

As his opponent, the Devil himself does not name the holy,
the good, but rather nature's power of generation, of the increase
of life, thus Eros.

“From air, water, as from earth,
A thousand germs wrest themselves,

In dry, moist, warm, cold!
Had I not reserved the flame for myself,
I should have nothing special of my own.”
2) Our present conception may be expressed approximately in the proposition that libido participates in every manifestation of an instinct, but that not everything in it is libido.
[Source scan 99 · printed page 96](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n99/mode/1up)
96 The independent instinctual disposition

mit that we grasp the latter only with so much greater
difficulty, as it were only guess it from the residue left
behind Eros, and that it eludes us wherever it is not
betrayed by its alloy with Eros. In sadism, where it
bends the erotic aim to suit its own purposes, while
nevertheless fully satisfying the sexual striving, we
obtain the clearest insight into its nature and its rela-
tion to Eros. But even where it appears without sexual
intention, even in the blindest destructive rage, one
cannot fail to recognize that its satisfaction is bound up
with an extraordinarily high narcissistic enjoyment, in
that it shows the ego the fulfilment of its old wishes of
omnipotence. Moderated and tamed, as it were inhib-
ited in aim, the destructive instinct, directed toward
objects, must procure for the ego the satisfaction of its
vital needs and mastery over nature.

Since
its assumption rests essentially on theoretical grounds,
one must admit that it is not completely secured against
theoretical objections either. But this is simply how it
appears to us now, at the present state of our insights;
future research and reflection will surely bring decisive
clarity.

For everything that follows, then, I take the position
that the inclination to aggression is an original, inde-
pendent instinctual disposition of man, and return
[Source scan 100 · printed page 97](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n100/mode/1up)
to aggression | 97

to the point that civilization finds its most powerful
obstacle in it. At some point in the course of this inves-
tigation, the insight has forced itself upon us that civi-
lization is a particular process that takes place over
mankind, and we still remain under the spell of this
idea. We add that it is a process in the service of Eros,
which seeks to unite isolated human individuals, later
families, then tribes, peoples, nations, into one great
unity, mankind. Why this must happen, we do not
know; it is simply the work of Eros. These masses of
men are to be bound to one another libidinally; neces-
sity alone, the advantages of the community of labour,
will not hold them together. But the natural aggressive
instinct of men opposes this programme of civilization,
the hostility of one against all and of all against one.

This aggressive instinct is the descendant and chief
representative of the death instinct, which we have
found alongside Eros and which shares world dominion
with it. And now, I think, the meaning of cultural de-
velopment is no longer obscure to us. It must show us
the struggle between Eros and death, between the life
instinct and the destructive instinct, as it is enacted in
the human species. This struggle is the essential con-
tent of life in general, and therefore cultural develop-
ment is simply to be described as the struggle for life

7

[Source scan 101 · printed page 98](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n101/mode/1up)
98 The struggle between Eros and the death instinct

of the human species.‘ And our nursery nurses seek
to soothe this strife of giants with the “Eiapopeia from
heaven”!

vi

Warum zeigen unsere Verwandten, die Tiere, keinen
solchen Kulturkampf? Oh, wir wissen es nicht. Sehr
wahrscheinlich haben einige unter ihnen, die Bienen,
Ameisen, 'T’ermiten durch Jahrhunderttausende gerungen,
bis sie jene staatlichen Institutionen, jene Verteilung
der Funktionen, jene Einschränkung der Individuen
gefunden haben, die wir heute bei ihnen bewundern.
Kennzeichnend für unseren gegenwärtigen Zustand ist
es, daß unsere Empfindungen uns sagen, in keinem
dieser 'Tierstaaten und in keiner der dort dem Einzel-
wesen zugeteilten Rollen würden wir uns glücklich
schätzen. Bei anderen 'Iierarten mag es zum zeitweili-
gen Ausgleich zwischen den Einflüssen der Umwelt und
den in ihnen sich bekämpfenden Trieben, somit zu einem
Stillstand der Entwicklung gekommen sein. Beim Ur-
menschen mag ein neuer Vorstoß der Libido ein neu-
erliches Sträuben des Destruktionstriebes angefacht haben.
Es ist da sehr viel zu fragen, worauf es noch keine

Antwort gibt.
„*

[Source scan 103 · printed page 100](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n103/mode/1up)

100- +* Die Verinnerlichung der Aggression

Eine andere Frage liegt uns näher. Welcher Mittel
bedient sich die Kultur, um die ihr entgegenstehende
Aggression zu hemmen, unschädlich zu machen, vielleicht
auszuschalten ? Einige solcher Methoden haben wir
bereits kennen gelernt, die anscheinend wichtigste aber
noch nicht. Wir können sie an der Entwicklungs-
geschichte des Einzelnen studieren. Was geht mit ihm
vor, um seine Aggressionslust unschädlich zu machen ?
Etwas sehr merkwürdiges, das wir nicht erraten hätten
und das doch so nahe liegt. Die Aggression wird in-
trojiziert, verinnerlicht, eigentlich aber dorthin zurück-
geschickt, woher sie gekommen ist, also gegen das
eigene Ich gewendet. Dort wird sie von einem Anteil
des Ichs übernommen, das sich als Über-Ich dem übri-
gen entgegenstellt, und nun als „Gewissen“ gegen das
Ich dieselbe strenge Aggressionsbereitschaft ausübt, die
das Ich gerne an anderen fremden Individuen befrie-
digt hätte. Die Spannung zwischen dem gestrengen
Über-Ich und dem ihm unterworfenen Ich heißen wir
Schuldbewußtsein; sie äußert sich als Strafbedürfnis.
Die Kultur bewältigt also die gefährliche Aggressions-
lust des Individuums, indem sie es schwächt, ent-
waffnet und durch eine Instanz in seinem Inneren,
wie durch eine Besatzung in der eroberten Stadt über-
wachen läßt.

Über die Entstehung des Schuldgefühls denkt der
Analytiker anders als sonst die Psychologen ; auch ihm

[Source scan 104 · printed page 101](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n104/mode/1up)

zum Gewissen 101

wird es nicht leicht, darüber Rechenschaft zu geben.
Zunächst, wenn man fragt, wie kommt einer zu einem
Schuldgefühl, erhält man eine Antwort, der man nicht
widersprechen kann: man fühlt sich schuldig (Fromme
sagen: sündig), wenn man etwas getan hat, was man
. als „böse“ erkennt. Dann merkt man, wie wenig diese
Antwort gibt. Vielleicht nach einigem Schwanken wird
man hinzusetzen, auch wer dies Böse nicht getan hat,
sondern bloß die Absicht, es zu tun, bei sich erkennt,
kann sich für schuldig halten, und dann wird man die
Frage aufwerfen, warum hier die Absicht der Aus-
führung gleichgeachtet wird. Beide Fälle setzen aber
voraus, daß man das Böse bereits als verwerflich, als
von der Ausführung auszuschließen erkannt hat. Wie
kommt man zu dieser Entscheidung ? Ein ursprüngliches,
sozusagen natürliches Unterscheidungsvermögen für Gut
und Böse darf man ablehnen. Das Böse ist oft gar nicht
das dem Ich Schädliche oder Gefährliche, im Gegenteil
auch etwas, was ihm erwünscht ist, ihm Vergnügen
bereitet. Darin zeigt sich also fremder Einfluß; dieser
bestimmt, was Gut und Böse heißen soll. Da eigene
Empfindung den Menschen nicht auf denselben Weg
geführt hatte, muß er ein Motiv haben, sich diesem
fremden Einfluß zu unterwerfen. Es ist in seiner Hilf-
losigkeit und Abhängigkeit von anderen leicht zu ent-
decken, kann am besten als Angst vor dem Liebes-
verlust bezeichnet werden. Verliert er die Liebe des

[Source scan 105 · printed page 102](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n105/mode/1up)

102 Das „schlechte Gewissen“

anderen, von dem er abhängig ist, so büßt er auch
den Schutz vor mancherlei Gefahren ein, setzt sich
vor allem der Gefahr aus, daß dieser Übermächtige
ihm in der Form der Bestrafung seine Überlegenheit
erweist. Das Böse ist also anfänglich dasjenige, wo-
für man mit Liebesverlust bedroht wird; aus Angst
vor diesem Verlust muß man es vermeiden. Darum
macht es auch wenig aus, ob man das Böse bereits
getan hat oder es erst tun will; in beiden Fällen
trıtt die Gefahr erst ein, wenn die Autorität es ent-
deckt, und diese würde sich in beiden Fällen ähnlich
benehmen.

Man heißt diesen Zustand „schlechtes Gewissen“,
aber eigentlich verdient er diesen Namen nicht, denn
auf dieser Stufe ist das Schuldbewußtsein offenbar nur
Angst vor dem Liebesverlust, „soziale* Angst. Beim
kleinen Kind kann es niemals etwas anderes sein,
aber auch bei vielen Erwachsenen ändert sich nicht
mehr daran, als daß an Stelle des Vaters oder beider
Eltern die größere menschliche Gemeinschaft tritt. Dar-
um gestatten sie sich regelmäßig, das Böse, das ihnen
Annehmlichkeiten verspricht, auszuführen, wenn sie
nur sicher sind, daß die Autorität nichts davon er-
fährt oder ihnen nichts anhaben kann und ihre
Angst gilt allein der Entdeckung.‘ Mit diesem Zustand

ı) Man denke an Rousseaus berühmten Mandarin !

[Source scan 106 · printed page 103](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n106/mode/1up)

Das Über-Ich 108

hat die Gesellschaft unserer Tage im allgemeinen zu
rechnen.

Eine große Änderung tritt erst ein, wenn die Auto-
rität durch die Aufrichtung eines Über-Ichs verinnerlicht
wird. Damit werden die Gewissensphänomene auf eine
neue Stufe gehoben, im Grunde sollte man erst jetzt
von Gewissen und Schuldgefühl sprechen.‘ Jetzt ent-
fällt auch die Angst vor dem Entdecktwerden und
vollends der Unterschied zwischen Böses Tun und Bö-
ses Wollen, denn vor dem Über-Ich kann sich nichts
verbergen, auch Gedanken nicht. Der reale Ernst der
Situation ist allerdings vergangen, denn die neue
Autorität, das Über-Ich, hat unseres Glaubens kein Mo-
tiv, das Ich, mit dem es innig zusammengehört, zu
mißhandeln. Aber der Einfluß der Genese, der das
Vergangene und Überwundene weiterleben läßt, äußert
sich darin, daß es im Grunde so bleibt, wie es zu
Anfang war. Das Über-Ich peinigt das sündige Ich mit
den nämlichen Angstempfindungen und lauert auf
Gelegenheiten, es von der Außenwelt bestrafen zu
lassen.

ı) Daß in dieser übersichtlichen Darstellung scharf getrennt wird,
was sich in Wirklichkeit in fließenden Übergängen vollzieht, daß
es sich nicht um die Existenz eines Über-Ichs allein, sondern um
dessen relative Stärke und Einflußsphäre handelt, wird jeder Ein-
sichtige verstehen und in Rechnung bringen. Alles Bisherige über
Gewissen und Schuld ist ja allgemein bekannt und nahezu unbe-
stritten.

[Source scan 107 · printed page 104](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n107/mode/1up)

104 Eigentümlichkeiten des Gewissens

Auf dieser zweiten Entwicklungsstufe zeigt das Ge-
wissen eine Eigentümlichkeit, die der ersten fremd war
und die nicht mehr leicht zu erklären ist. Es benimmt
sich nämlich um so strenger und mißtrauischer, je
tugendhafter der Mensch ist, so daß am Ende gerade
die es in der Heiligkeit am weitesten gebracht, sich der
ärgsten Sündhaftigkeit beschuldigen. Die Tugend büßt
dabei ein Stück des ihr zugesagten Lohnes ein, das ge-
fügige und enthaltsame Ich genießt nicht das Vertrauen
seines Mentors, bemüht sich, wie es scheint, vergeblich,
es zu erwerben. Nun wird man bereit sein einzuwen-
den: das seien künstlich zurecht gemachte Schwierig-
keiten. Das strengere und wachsamere Gewissen sei
eben der ihn kennzeichnende Zug des sittlichen Men-
schen, und wenn die Heiligen sich für Sünder aus-
geben, so täten sie es nicht mit Unrecht unter Berufung
auf die Versuchungen zur 'Triebbefriedigung, denen sie
in besonders hohem Maße ausgesetzt sind, da Ver-
suchungen bekanntlich durch beständige Versagung nur
wachsen, während sie bei gelegentlicher Befriedigung
wenigstens zeitweilig nachlassen. Eine andere Tatsache
des an Problemen so reichen Gebiets der Ethik ist die,
daß Mißgeschick, also äußere Versagung die Macht des
Gewissens im Über-Ich so sehr fördert. So lange es dem
Menschen gut geht, ist auch sein Gewissen milde und
läßt dem Ich allerlei angehen; wenn ihn ein Unglück
getroffen hat, hält er Einkehr in sich, erkennt seine

[Source scan 108 · printed page 105](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n108/mode/1up)

Pi



Das Schicksal als Fortsetzung der Elterninstanz 105

Sündhaftigkeit, steigert seine Gewissensansprüche, legt
sich Enthaltungen auf und bestraft sich durch Bußen.'
Ganze Völker haben sich ebenso benommen und be-
nehmen sich noch immer so. Aber dies erklärt sich be-
quem aus der ursprünglichen infantilen Stufe des Ge-
wissens, die also nach der Introjektion ins Über-Ich nicht
verlassen wird, sondern neben und hinter ihr fortbe-
steht. Das Schicksal wird als Ersatz der Elterninstanz
angesehen; wenn man Unglück hat, bedeutet es, daß
man von dieser höchsten Macht nicht mehr geliebt
wird, und von diesem Liebesverlust bedroht, beugt
man sich von neuem vor der Elternvertretung im Über-
Ich, die man im Glück vernachlässigen wollte. Dies
wird besonders deutlich, wenn man in streng religiö-
sem Sinne im Schicksal nur den Ausdruck des gött-
lichen Willens erkennt. Das Volk Israel hatte sich für
Gottes bevorzugtes Kind gehalten, und als der große
Vater Unglück nach Unglück über dies sein Volk
hereinbrechen ließ, wurde es nicht etwa irre an dieser
Beziehung oder zweifelte an Gottes Macht und Ge-
rechtigkeit, sondern erzeugte die Propheten, die ihm

ı) Diese Förderung der Moral durch Mißgeschick behandelt
Mark Twain in einer köstlichen kleinen Geschichte : The first
melon I ever stole. Diese erste Melone ist zufällig unreif. Ich hörte
Mark Twain diese kleine Geschichte selbst vortragen. Nachdem er
ihren Titel ausgesprochen hatte, hielt er inne und fragte sich wie
zweifelnd: „Was it the first“? Damit hatte er alles gesagt.

[Source scan 109 · printed page 106](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n109/mode/1up)

106 Ursprünge des Schuldgefühls

seine Sündhaftigkeit vorhielten und schuf aus seinem
Schuldbewußtsein die überstrengen Vorschriften seiner
Priesterreligion. Es ist merkwürdig, wie anders sich der
Primitive benimmt! Wenn er Unglück gehabt hat, gibt
er nicht sich die Schuld, sondern dem Fetisch, der offen-
bar seine Schuldigkeit nicht getan hat, und verprügelt
ihn, anstatt sich selbst zu bestrafen.

Wir kennen also zwei Ursprünge des Schuklgeihhk,
den aus der Angst vor der Autorität und den späteren
aus der Angst vor dem Über-Ich. Das erstere zwingt
dazu, auf Triebbefriedigungen zu verzichten, das andere
drängt, da man den Fortbestand der verbotenen
Wünsche vor dem Über-Ich nicht verbergen kann, außer-
dem zur Bestrafung. Wir haben auch gehört, wie man
die Strenge des Über-Ichs, also die Gewissensforderung,
verstehen kann. Sie setzt einfach die Strenge der äußeren
Autorität, die von ihr abgelöst und teilweise ersetzt
wird, fort. Wir sehen nun, in welcher Beziehung der
Triebverzicht zum Schuldbewußtsein steht. Ursprünglich
ist ja der Iriebverzicht die Folge der Angst vor der
äußeren Autorität; man verzichtet auf Befriedigungen,
um deren Liebe nicht zu verlieren. Hat man diesen
Verzicht geleistet, so ist man sozusagen mit ihr quitt,
es sollte kein Schuldgefühl erübrigen., Anders ist es im
Falle der Angst vor dem Über-Ich. Hier hilft der Trieb-
verzicht nicht genug, denn der Wunsch bleibt bestehen
und läßt sich vor dem Über-Ich nicht verheimlichen. Es

100- +* The internalization of aggression

Another question lies nearer to us. What means
does civilization employ in order to inhibit the aggression
that opposes it, to render it harmless, perhaps to
eliminate it? We have already become acquainted with
some such methods, but apparently not with the most
important one. We can study it in the developmental
history of the individual. What happens to him in
order to render his desire for aggression harmless?
Something very remarkable, which we should not have
guessed and which nevertheless lies so near at hand.
The aggression is introjected, internalized, but properly
speaking sent back to where it came from, that is,
turned against the subject's own ego.

There it is taken over by a part
of the ego which sets itself against the rest as the
super-ego, and now, as “conscience,” exercises against
the ego the same strict readiness for aggression which
the ego would gladly have satisfied upon other, alien
individuals. We call the tension between the stern
super-ego and the ego subject to it consciousness of
guilt; it manifests itself as a need for punishment.
Thus civilization masters the individual's dangerous
desire for aggression by weakening him, disarming him,
and having him watched by an agency within him,
as by a garrison in the conquered city.

the question why the intention is here treated as
equivalent to the execution. But both cases presuppose
that one has already recognized evil as reprehensible,
as something to be excluded from being carried out. How
does one arrive at this decision? An original, as it
were natural, capacity for distinguishing good and evil
may be rejected.

Evil is often not at all
what is harmful or dangerous to the ego; on the contrary,
it is also something desired by it, something that affords
it pleasure. Thus an alien influence shows itself here;
it determines what good and evil are to mean. Since
his own feeling had not led man along the same path,
he must have a motive for submitting to this alien
influence. It is easy to discover it in his helplessness
and dependence on others; it can best be described as
fear of the loss of love. If he loses the love of the
[Source scan 105 · printed page 102](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n105/mode/1up)
102 The “bad conscience”

other person on whom he depends, he also forfeits
protection against dangers of various kinds; above all,
he exposes himself to the danger that this more powerful
person will demonstrate his superiority to him in the
form of punishment. Thus evil is initially that for
which one is threatened with loss of love; one must
avoid it out of fear of this loss. For this reason it
also makes little difference whether one has already
done the evil or only intends to do it; in both cases
the danger arises only when the authority discovers it,
and in both cases it would behave similarly.

This state is called “bad conscience,”
but it does not properly deserve this name, for at
this stage consciousness of guilt is evidently only
fear of the loss of love, “social” fear. In the small
child it can never be anything else, but in many adults,
too, no more changes than that the larger human
community takes the place of the father or both
parents. Therefore they regularly permit themselves to
carry out the evil which promises them advantages, if
they are only certain that the authority will learn
nothing of it or can do nothing to them, and their
fear concerns discovery alone.¹ With this state
1) Think of Rousseau's famous Mandarin!
[Source scan 106 · printed page 103](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n106/mode/1up)
The super-ego 103
the society of our day generally has to reckon.

A great change occurs only when the authority is
internalized through the erection of a super-ego. Thereby
the phenomena of conscience are raised to a new level;
in truth, only now should one speak of conscience and
a feeling of guilt.¹ Now the fear of being discovered
also falls away, and entirely so does the distinction
between doing evil and willing evil, for nothing can be
concealed from the super-ego, not even thoughts. The
real gravity of the situation has indeed passed away,
for the new authority, the super-ego, in our belief has
no motive to maltreat the ego with which it is intimately
connected. But the influence of the genesis, which lets
the past and the overcome continue to live, manifests
itself in the fact that fundamentally things remain as
they were at the beginning.

The super-ego torments the sinful ego with
the same feelings of anxiety and lies in wait for
opportunities to have it punished by the external world.

1) That, in this schematic presentation, a sharp distinction is made between
what in reality takes place in gradual transitions, that
it is not a matter of the existence of a super-ego alone, but of
its relative strength and sphere of influence, every perceptive
person will understand and take into account. Everything said hitherto about
conscience and guilt is, after all, generally known and almost un-
disputed.
[Source scan 107 · printed page 104](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n107/mode/1up)
104 Peculiarities of conscience

At this second stage of development, con-
science displays a peculiarity that was foreign to the first
and that is no longer easy to explain. It behaves,
namely, all the more strictly and distrustfully the more
virtuous a person is, so that in the end precisely those
who have gone furthest in holiness accuse themselves of
the worst sinfulness. Virtue thereby forfeits a portion of
the reward promised to it; the compliant and abstinent
ego does not enjoy the confidence of its mentor, and,
it seems, strives in vain to acquire it. Now one will be ready to ob-
ject: these are artificially contrived difficul-
ties.

The stricter and more watchful conscience is
indeed the distinguishing trait of the moral per-
son, and if the saints present themselves as sinners,
they do not do so without justification, in view
of the temptations to instinctual satisfaction to which they
are exposed in an especially high degree, since temp-
tations, as is well known, only increase through continual deprivation,
whereas with occasional satisfaction they at least temporarily subside. Another fact
in the field of ethics, so rich in problems, is that
misfortune, that is, external deprivation, so greatly promotes
the power of conscience in the super-ego. So long as a
person is doing well, his conscience too is mild and
allows the ego all manner of things; when misfortune
has befallen him, he examines himself, recognizes his
[Source scan 108 · printed page 105](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n108/mode/1up)
Pi
Fate as a continuation of the parental agency 105

sinfulness, heightens the demands of his conscience, imposes
abstinences upon himself, and punishes himself by penances.'
Entire peoples have behaved, and still behave, in the same way.
But this is readily explained by the original infantile stage of con-
science, which, after introjection into the super-ego,
is not abandoned, but continues to exist alongside and behind it.
Fate is regarded as a substitute for the parental agency;
if one suffers misfortune, it means that one is no longer loved
by this supreme power, and, threatened by this loss
of love, one once again bows before the parental representative in the super-
ego, which one had wished to neglect in good fortune. This
becomes especially clear when, in the strictly religious
sense, one recognizes in fate only the expression of the divine
will.

The people of Israel had regarded itself as
God's favoured child, and when the great
Father caused misfortune upon misfortune to break
upon this people of his, it did not become doubtful of this
relationship or doubt God's power and jus-
tice; rather, it produced the prophets, who reproached it with

1) This promotion of morality through misfortune is treated
by Mark Twain in a delightful little story: The first
melon I ever stole. This first melon happens to be unripe. I heard
Mark Twain himself recite this little story. After he had
pronounced its title, he paused and asked himself, as if in doubt:
“Was it the first?” With that he had said everything.
[Source scan 109 · printed page 106](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n109/mode/1up)
106 Origins of the sense of guilt

its sinfulness and, out of its consciousness of guilt, created
the excessively strict precepts of its priestly religion. It is remarkable how differently the
primitive behaves! When he has suffered misfortune, he does
not blame himself, but the fetish, which evidently
has not done its duty, and beats it instead
of punishing himself.

Thus we know two origins of the sense of guilt,
one arising from fear of authority and the later one
from fear of the super-ego. The former compels one
to renounce instinctual satisfactions; the latter urges one,
since one cannot conceal the continued existence of the forbidden
desires from the super-ego, also toward punishment. We have also heard how one can
understand the severity of the super-ego, that is, the demand of conscience.
It simply continues the severity of the external
authority, from which it has been detached and which it partly replaces.
We now see the relation in which instinctual renunciation stands to consciousness of guilt. Originally,
instinctual renunciation is indeed the consequence of fear of the
external authority; one renounces satisfactions
in order not to lose its love.

Once one has made this
renunciation, one is, so to speak, quits with it;
no sense of guilt ought to remain. It is otherwise in the
case of fear of the super-ego. Here instinctual re-
nunciation does not help enough, for the wish persists
and cannot be concealed from the super-ego. There
[Source scan 110 · printed page 107](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n110/mode/1up)
The role of instinctual renunciation 107

will therefore be a sense of guilt despite the renunciation
that has taken place, and this is a great economic disadvantage of the establishment
of the super-ego, as one may say, of the formation of conscience.
Instinctual renunciation now no longer has any wholly liberating effect;
virtuous abstinence is no longer rewarded
by the assurance of love; for a threatened external misfortune
— loss of love and punishment at the hands of the external
authority — one has exchanged an enduring inner mis-
fortune, the tension of consciousness of guilt.

These relations are so complicated and at the same time
so important that, despite the dangers of repetition,
I should like to approach them once more from another side. The
temporal sequence would thus be: first, instinctual re-
nunciation as a result of fear of the aggression of the external
authority — for that is what fear of loss of love amounts to,
love protects against this aggression of punishment — then the establishment of the inner authority,
instinctual renunciation as a result of fear of it, anxiety of con-
science. In the second case, evil deed and evil intention are treated as equivalent,
hence consciousness of guilt and need for punishment.
The aggression of conscience preserves the aggression of authority.
So far this has presumably become clear; but where is there room
for the influence of misfortune (of renunciation imposed from without)
that strengthens conscience, for the extraordinary severity
[Source scan 111 · printed page 108](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n111/mode/1up)
108 Discussion of the relation

of conscience in the best and most compliant? We
have already explained both peculiarities of conscience, but
have probably left the impression
that these explanations do not reach to the bottom,
leaving a remainder unexplained. And here at last
an idea intervenes that is entirely peculiar to psychoanalysis
and alien to the ordinary thinking of human beings. It is
of such a kind that it enables us to understand
why the subject was bound to appear so confused and opaque to us.
It says, namely, that at first conscience (more correctly: the anxiety
that later becomes conscience) is indeed the cause of instinctual renunciation, but later
the relation is reversed.

Every instinctual renunciation
now becomes a dynamic source of conscience; every new
renunciation increases its severity and intolerance, and
if only we could bring it into better accord with the history of the emergence
of conscience known to us, we should be tempted
to subscribe to the paradoxical proposition: Conscience is the consequence of
instinctual renunciation; or: instinctual renunciation (imposed upon us from without)
creates conscience, which then demands further
instinctual renunciation.

Actually, the contradiction between this proposition and
the given genesis of conscience is not so great,
and we see a way of diminishing it further.
For the sake of easier exposition, let us single out
the example of the aggressive instinct and assume
[Source scan 112 · printed page 109](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n112/mode/1up)
between instinctual renunciation and sense of guilt 109

that in these circumstances we are always dealing
with renunciation of aggression. This is of course
intended only as a provisional assumption. The effect
of instinctual renunciation upon conscience then proceeds
in such a way that every portion of aggression whose
satisfaction we forgo is taken over by the superego and
increases its aggression (against the ego). This does not
accord very well with the fact that the original aggression
of conscience is the continued severity of external
authority, and thus has nothing to do with renunciation.
But we can make this discrepancy disappear if we assume
a different derivation for this first endowment of the
superego with aggression.

Against the authority which
prevents the child from attaining its first, but also most
important satisfactions, a considerable measure of aggres-
sive inclination must have developed in the child, regard-
less of what kind the demanded instinctual renunciations
were. Necessarily the child had to renounce the satisfac-
tion of this vindictive aggression. It extricates itself from
this difficult economic situation by means of familiar
mechanisms, by taking this unassailable authority into
itself through identification; this authority now becomes
the superego and comes into possession of all the aggres-
sion which one would gladly, as a child, have exercised
against it. The child's ego must content itself with the
sad role of the thus humiliated authority—that of the
father. It
[Source scan 113 · printed page 110](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n113/mode/1up)
110 Discussion of the relation

is a reversal of the situation, as so often occurs.
“If I were the father and you the child, I would
treat you badly.” The relation between superego and
ego is the return, distorted by wish, of real relations
between the still undivided ego and an external object.
This too is typical. The essential difference, however,
is that the original severity of the superego is not—or
not so much—that which one has experienced from it
or imputes to it, but represents one's own aggression
against it. If this is correct, one may indeed maintain
that conscience was originally produced by the suppression
of an aggression and that in its further course it is
strengthened by new suppressions of the same kind.

Which of the two views is right, then?
The earlier one, which seemed so genetically unassailable
to us, or the more recent one, which rounds off the
theory in such a welcome manner? Clearly, according
to the testimony of direct observation as well, both are
justified; they do not contradict one another, indeed they
coincide at one point, for the child's vindictive aggression
will be codetermined by the amount of punitive
aggression it expects from its father. Experience, however,
teaches that the severity of the superego which a child
develops by no means reproduces the severity of the
treatment which it has itself experienced.
[Source scan 114 · printed page 111](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n114/mode/1up)
between instinctual renunciation and sense of guilt 111

It appears independent of it; with a very mild upbringing
a child can acquire a very severe conscience. But it would
also be wrong to exaggerate this independence; it is not
difficult to convince oneself that the severity of upbringing
also exerts a strong influence upon the formation of the
child's superego. The result is that, in the formation of
the superego and the emergence of conscience, innate
constitutional factors and influences of the milieu of the
real environment cooperate; and this is by no means
strange, but the general aetiological condition of all such
processes.”

1) As Melanie Klein and other English authors have
rightly emphasized.

2) In “Psychoanalysis of the Total
Personality” (1927), Fr. Alexander has correctly appraised, in con-
nection with Aichhorn's study of neglect, the two principal types
of pathogenic methods of upbringing, excessive severity and
indulgence. The “excessively soft and indulgent” father will give
the child occasion to form an excessively severe superego, because,
under the impression of the love it receives, this child has no
other outlet for its aggression than to turn it inward. In the
neglected child, who has been brought up without love, the tension
between ego and superego is absent; all its aggression can be
directed outwards.

If, then, one disregards
a constitutional factor which must be assumed, one may
say that the severe conscience arises from the cooperation
of two influences of life: instinctual frustration, which
unleashes aggression, and the experience of love, which
turns this aggression inward and transfers it to the
superego.
[Source scan 115 · printed page 112](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n115/mode/1up)
112 The historical origin of the sense of guilt

One may also say that when the child reacts to the first
great instinctual frustrations with excessively strong aggression
and a corresponding severity of the superego, it is following
a phylogenetic model and going beyond the reply justified
by the actual situation; for the primal father was certainly
terrible, and the utmost measure of aggression might be
imputed to him. The differences between the two views
of the genesis of conscience are thus diminished still
further when one passes from individual to phylogenetic
developmental history. In return, a new significant difference
appears in these two processes. We cannot go beyond
the assumption that the sense of guilt of mankind derives
from the Oedipus complex and was acquired at the killing
of the father by the union of brothers.

At that time, an aggression was not sup-
pressed but carried out—the very aggression whose
suppression in the child is supposed to be the source of
the sense of guilt. Now I should not be surprised if a
reader angrily exclaimed: “So it is entirely immaterial
whether one kills one's father or not; one gets a sense of
guilt in any event! One may permit oneself some doubts
about that. Either it is false that the sense of guilt arises
from suppressed aggressions, or the whole story of the
killing of the father is a romance, and the children of
primitive man
[Source scan 116 · printed page 113](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n116/mode/1up)
Remorse 113

did not kill their fathers more often than those of today
are wont to do. Besides, if it is not a romance but
plausible history, then one would have a case in which
what everyone expects takes place—namely, that one
feels guilty because one has really done something that
cannot be justified. And for this case, which after all
occurs every day, psychoanalysis has failed to provide
us with an explanation.” |

That is true and is to be made good. Nor is it any
special secret. If one has a sense of guilt after and
because one has committed some offence, one should
rather call this feeling remorse. It relates only to a
deed, and naturally presupposes that a conscience, the
readiness to feel guilty, already existed before the deed.
Such remorse can therefore never help us to discover
the origin of conscience and of the sense of guilt in
general. The course of these everyday cases is usually
that an instinctual need has acquired the strength to
enforce its satisfaction against conscience, which is itself
limited in strength, and that with the natural weakening
of the need through its satisfaction, the earlier relation
of forces is restored. Psychoanalysis is therefore right
to exclude the case of the sense of guilt arising from
remorse from

these discussions, however frequent it may be
8
[Source scan 117 · printed page 114](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n117/mode/1up)
114 The Origin of the Sense of Guilt

occurs and however great its practical significance
may be.

But if the human sense of guilt goes back to the
killing of the primal father, that was surely a case of
“remorse,” and, according to the assumption, conscience
and a sense of guilt cannot have existed before the
deed at that time? Whence came remorse in this case?
Certainly, this case must elucidate for us the mystery
of the sense of guilt, put an end to our embarrassments.
And I think that it does so. This remorse was the
result of the primordial ambivalence of feeling toward
the father; the sons hated him, but they also loved him;
after the hatred had been satisfied by the aggression,
love came to light in remorse over the deed, through
identification with the father set up the super-ego,
gave it the father’s power as if for the punishment of
the aggression perpetrated against him, created the
restrictions that were to prevent a repetition of the
deed.

And since the inclination to aggression against
the father repeated itself in subsequent generations,
the sense of guilt also persisted and was strengthened
anew by every aggression that was repressed and
transferred to the super-ego. Now, I think, we finally
grasp two things in full clarity: the part played by
love in the origin of conscience and the fateful
inevitability of the sense of guilt
[Source scan 118 · printed page 115](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n118/mode/1up)
from the conflict of ambivalence 115

. It is really not decisive whether one has
killed the father or refrained from the deed; in both
cases one must find oneself guilty, for the sense of
guilt is the expression of the conflict of ambivalence,
of the eternal struggle between Eros and the destructive
or death instinct. This conflict is kindled as soon as
human beings are set the task of living together; so
long as this community knows only the form of the
family, it must express itself in the Oedipus complex,
bring conscience into operation, create the first sense
of guilt. When an extension of this community is
attempted, the same conflict is continued in forms
dependent on the past, intensified, and results in a
further increase of the sense of guilt.

Since civilization obeys an
inner erotic impulse which bids it unite human beings
into an intimately connected mass, it can attain this
goal only by way of an ever-growing intensification
of the sense of guilt. What was begun with the father
is completed with the mass. If civilization is the
necessary course of development from the family to
humanity, then inseparably connected with it, as a
consequence of the inborn conflict of ambivalence, as
a consequence of the eternal strife between love and
the striving for death, is the increase of the sense of
guilt perhaps to heights which the individual

finds hard to bear. One recalls the moving
$*+
[Source scan 119 · printed page 116](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n119/mode/1up)
116 The Inevitability of the Sense of Guilt

accusation of the great poet against the “heavenly
powers”:
“You lead us into life,
You let the poor man become guilty,
Then you abandon him to torment,
For every guilt avenges itself on earth.”'

And one may well sigh at the realization
that it is granted to certain people to draw forth the
deepest insights from the vortex of their own feelings
almost effortlessly, whereas we others

have to make our way toward them through painful
uncertainty and restless groping.
ı) Goethe, Songs of the Harpist in “Wilhelm Meister”.

Am Ende eines solchen Weges angelangt, muß der
Autor seine Leser um Entschuldigung bitten, daß er
ihnen kein geschickter Führer gewesen, ihnen das Er-
lebnis öder Strecken und beschwerlicher Umwege nicht
erspart hat. Es ist kein Zweifel, daß man es besser
machen kann. Ich will versuchen, nachträglich etwas
gutzumachen.

Zunächst vermute ich bei den Lesern den Eindruck,
daß die Erörterungen über das Schuldgefühl den Rah-
men dieses Aufsatzes sprengen, indem sie zuviel Raum
für sich einnehmen und ihren anderen Inhalt, mit dem
sie nicht immer innig zusammenhängen, an den Rand
drängen. Das mag den Aufbau der Abhandlung ge-
stört haben, entspricht aber durchaus der Absicht, das
Schuldgefühl als das wichtigste Problem der Kultur-
entwicklung hinzustellen und darzutun, daß der Preis
für den Kulturfortschritt in der Glückseinbuße durch
die Erhöhung des Schuldgefühls bezahlt wird.” Was an

1) „So macht Gewissen Feige aus uns allen... .“
Daß sie dem jugendlichen Menschen verheimlicht, welche Rolle

die Sexualität in seinem Leben spielen wird, ist nicht der einzige

[Source scan 121 · printed page 118](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n121/mode/1up)

118 Der Preis des Kulturfortschritts

diesem Satz, dem Endergebnis unserer Untersuchung
noch befremdlich klingt, läßt sich wahrscheinlich auf das
ganz sonderbare, noch durchaus unverstandene Verhält-
nis des Schuldgefühls zu unserem Bewußtsein zurück-
führen. In den gemeinen, uns als normal geltenden
Fällen von Reue macht es sich dem Bewußtsein deut-
lich genug wahrnehmbar; wir sind doch gewöhnt, an-
statt Schuldgefühl „Schuldbewußtsein“ zu sagen. Aus
dem Studium der Neurosen, denen wir doch die wert-
vollsten Winke zum Verständnis des Normalen dan-
ken, ergeben sich widerspruchsvolle Verhältnisse. Bei
einer dieser Affektionen, der Zwangsneurose, drängt
sich das Schuldgefühl überlaut dem Bewußtsein auf, es
beherrscht das Krankheitsbild wie das Leben der Kran-

Vorwurf, den man gegen die heutige Erziehung erheben muß. Sie
sündigt außerdem darin, daß sie ihn nicht auf die. Aggression
vorbereitet, deren Objekt er zu werden bestimmt ist. Indem sie
die Jugend mit so unrichtiger psychologischer Orientierung ins
Leben entläßt, benimmt sich die Erziehung nicht anders, als wenn
man Leute, die auf eine Polarexpedition gehen, mit Sommer-
kleidern und Karten der oberitalischen Seen ausrüsten würde.
Dabei wird ein gewisser Mißbrauch der ethischen Forderungen
deutlich. Die Strenge derselben würde nicht viel schaden, wenn
die Erziehung sagte: So sollten die Menschen sein, um glücklich
zu werden und andere glücklich zu machen; aber man muß damit
rechnen, daß sie nicht so sind. Anstatt dessen läßt man den
Jugendlichen glauben, daß alle anderen die ethischen Vorschriften
erfüllen, also tugendhaft sind. Damit begründet man die Forde-
rung, daß er auch so werde.

[Source scan 122 · printed page 119](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n122/mode/1up)

. Das unbewußte Schuldgefühl 119

ken, läßt kaum anderes neben sich aufkommen. Aber
in den meisten anderen Fällen und Formen von Neu-
rose bleibt es völlig unbewußt, ohne darum gering-
fügigere Wirkungen zu äußern. Die Kranken glauben
uns nicht, wenn wir ıhnen ein „unbewußtes Schuld-
gefühl“ zumuten; um nur halbwegs von ihnen ver-
standen zu werden, erzählen wir ihnen von einem un-
bewußten Strafbedürfnis, in dem sich das Schuldgefühl
äußert. Aber die Beziehung zur Neurosenform darf
nicht überschätzt werden; es gibt auch bei der Zwangs-
neurose I'ypen von Kranken, die ihr Schuldgefühl nicht
wahrnehmen oder es als ein quälendes Unbehagen,
eine Art von Angst erst dann empfinden, wenn sie an
der Ausführung gewisser Handlungen verhindert wer-
den. Diese Dinge sollte man endlich einmal verstehen
können, man kann es noch nicht. Vielleicht ist hier die
Bemerkung willkommen, daß das Schuldgefühl im
Grunde nichts ist als eine topische Abart der Angst,
in seinen späteren Phasen fällt es ganz mit der Angst
vor dem Über-Ich zusammen. Und bei der Angst
zeigen sich im Verhältnis zum Bewußtsein dieselben
außerordentlichen Variationen. Irgendwie steckt die
Angst hinter allen Symptomen, aber bald nimmt sie
lärmend das Bewußtsein ganz für sich in Anspruch,
bald verbirgt sie sich so vollkommen, daß wir genötigt
sind, von unbewußter Angst — oder wenn wir ein
reineres psychologisches Gewissen haben wollen, da ja

[Source scan 123 · printed page 120](https://archive.org/details/DasUnbehagenInDerKultur/page/n123/mode/1up)

120 Die Erlösung

die Angst zunächst nur eine Empfindung ist — von
Angstmöglichkeiten zu reden. Und darum ist es sehr
wohl denkbar, daß auch das durch die Kultur erzeugte
Schuldbewußtsein nicht als solches erkannt wird, zum
großen Teil unbewußt bleibt oder als ein Unbehagen,
eine Unzufriedenheit zum Vorschein kommt, für die
man andere Motivierungen sucht. Die Religionen
wenigstens haben die Rolle des Schuldgefühls in der
Kultur nie verkannt. Sie treten ja, was ich an anderer
Stelle nicht gewürdigt hatte,’ auch mit dem Anspruch
auf, die Menschheit von diesem Schuldgefühl, das sie
Sünde heißen, zu erlösen. Aus der Art, wie im Christen-
tum diese Erlösung gewonnen wird, durch den Opfer-
tod eines Einzelnen, der damit eine allen gemeinsame
Schuld auf sich nimmt, haben wir ja einen Schluß darauf
gezogen, welches der erste Anlaß zur Erwerbung dieser
Urschuld, mit der auch die Kultur begann, gewesen
sein mag.”

Es kann nicht sehr wichtig werden, mag aber nicht
überflüssig sein, daß wir die Bedeutung einiger Worte
wie: Über-Ich, Gewissen, Schuldgefühl, Strafbedürfnis,
Reue erläutern, die wir vielleicht oft zu lose und eines
für’s andere gebraucht haben. Alle beziehen sich auf
dasselbe Verhältnis, benennen aber verschiedene Seiten
desselben. Das Über-Ich ist eine von uns erschlossene

2) Totem und Tabu (1912).

Ginge es ohne diese
Bedingung, so wäre es vielleicht besser. Anders aus-

als ein Produkt der Interferenz zweier Strebungen,
des Strebens nach Glück, das wir gewöhnlich „ego-
istisch*, und des Strebens nach Vereinigung mit den
anderen in der Gemeinschaft, das wir „altruistisch“

egoistische oder Glücksstrebung, die andere, „kulturell“

Strebungen die stärkste und reinste, darum oft auch
