The central point is reclassified: from a geometric element it becomes a sign of the earth and the center of cosmic order.
The complete circle is reclassified: from an abstract figure it becomes a sign of Solar dignity.
The Moon is reclassified: from a separate celestial body it becomes a relational form defined by the Sun.
The change of visibility is reclassified: from an isolated variation it becomes an effect of irradiation, turning, and time.
The opposition between motion and form is resolved, because the form of the Moon renders the motion of the Solar relation visible.
Surface: Point, circle, hemicycle, and horned figure refer to the earth, Sun, and Moon.
Structural: The terrestrial center, Solar preeminence, and Lunar subordination constitute a concentric and hierarchical order.
Metastrategic: The hieroglyphic institutes the transition from figure to cosmology, so that geometry renders relations of dignity, motion, and dependence legible.
Ontological/Temporal: Celestial bodies are constituted as relational beings, whose form and visibility are temporally changed through the order of Solar irradiation.
The axioms suffice to restore the movement from the central point to the earth, from the earth to the Sun, and from the Sun to the Moon.
The distinction between the complete Solar circle and the lunar hemicycle is necessary for restoring the geometric hierarchy.
The dependence of light, turning toward the Sun, and temporal change explain the series from visibility to disappearance and horned form.
The relation between the Solar circle and the lunar hemicycle is not fully determined in all geometric terms in the transmitted text.
The system is internally coherent with respect to the primacy of the Sun and the dependence of the Moon, but the exact nexus between motion, form, and irradiation remains partly symbolic.
The strength of the argument consists in its hierarchical and relational structure; its fragility appears in the undemonstrated transition from geometric figure to physical causation.

units.title: T H E O R E M A Iiii.

items.text: Quaestio est quomodo Lunæ hemicyclium, quamvis Solari Circulo quasi superius priusque videatur, ad Solem ordinetur.
Nova constitutio ponit Lunam Solem tamquam Dominum Regemque suum observare.
Fundamentum relationis est forma Solis et eius vicinitas, quibus Luna quasi assimilari videtur.
Probatio procedit per conversionem luminis, irradiationem solarem et apparentem transformationem Lunæ.
Motus concluditur per disparitionem Lunæ e caelo et eius post aliquot dies reditum in figuram corniculatam.
Lunæ hemicyclium Solari Circulo quasi superius priusque apparet.
Sol Lunæ Dominus et Rex observatur.
Luna Solis formam et vicinitatem appetere ac diligere videtur.
Luna magnitudinem Solis in semidiametro æmulatur, saltem vulgaribus apparentem hominibus.
Luna lumen suum semper ad Solem convertit.
Luna radiis solaribus imbui appetit.
Luna, quasi in Solem transformata, toto caelo disparere potest.
Post aliquot dies Luna figura corniculata rursus apparet.
Apparentia Lunæ per successionem figurarum et vicinitatum temporaliter determinatur.
Luna, quamvis quasi superior et prior appareat, non constituitur ut potestas a Sole independens.
Lumen Lunæ non sistitur ut a Solis relatione separatum.
Luna non permanet in una eademque figura apparente.
Transformativa assimilatio ad Solem non terminatur in perpetua praesentia Lunæ in caelo.
Disparitio Lunæ non est eius ultimus status, quia figura corniculata postea restituitur.
Magnitudo hic non definitur ut mensura absoluta, sed ut magnitudo vulgaribus hominibus apparens.
Apparens superioritas Lunæ non tollit eius ordinationem ad Solem.
Forma et vicinitas Solis efficiunt ut Luna non solum lumen recipere, sed etiam Soli assimilari videatur.
Conversio luminis ad Solem significat relationem directionalem, qua Luna per Solem visibiliter determinatur.
Appetitus radiorum solarum ducit ad statum in quo distinctio apparens inter Lunam et Solem maxime attenuatur.
Disparitio caeli et reditus corniculatus constituunt unum motum periodicum potius quam conversionem irrevocabilem.
Figura corniculata post aliquot dies est effectus temporalis relationis Lunæ ad Solem.
Apparens hierarchia cosmica simul continet inversionem ordinum: Luna quasi superior apparet, sed causaliter et simbolice ad Solem subordinatur.
Identitas Lunæ non ut substantia visualiter stabilis, sed ut series relationum ad Solem producitur.
Lumen efficit medium transformationis: per irradiationem Luna a propria figura ad solaris similitudinis limen transit.
Tempus non tantum mutationem observat, sed formas Lunæ in circulum apparentiarum ordinat.
Relatio ad Solem simul est principium visibilitatis, assimilationis et disparitionis Lunæ.
Systema tacite excludit Lunam cuius forma et lumen a relatione Solari plene explicarentur.
Systema excludit oppositionem simplicem inter Lunam activam et Solem passivum, quia Luna ad Solem convertitur et ab eo formatur.
Systema excludit identitatem quæ uno momento et una figura tota stabiliretur.
Systema excludit distinctionem rigidam inter visibilitatem et transformationem, quia idem lumen Lunam ostendit et quasi abscondit.
Systema excludit temporalitatem rectilineam, in qua transformatio ad Solem sine reversione procederet.
Textus circumit ideam luminis Lunaris absolute proprii, quia lumen in directione et radiis Solaribus explicatur.
Textus praecludit Lunam tamquam centrum ultimum ordinis cosmici, quamvis eius species momentanee quasi superior appareat.
Textus relinquit indisponibilem ideam separationis absolutae inter corpora quæ per formam, vicinitatem et lumen definiuntur.
Impossibilis fit figura Lunæ quæ extra vicissitudinem Solarem semel pro semper determinetur.
Absentia constitutiva est autonomia Lunæ: eius apparentia semper aliquid extra Lunam, Solem, supponit.
Apparens superioritas Lunæ → recognitio Solis ut Domini et Regis → subordinatio relationis.
Forma et vicinitas Solis → æmulatio magnitudinis et conversio luminis → assimilatio Lunæ.
Appetitus radiorum → quasi-transformătio in Solem → disparitio e caelo.
Intervallum temporale → reapparitio figuræ corniculatæ → clausura circularis motus.
Species initialis → relatio Solarizata → indistinctio apparens → absentia → species nova.
Hemicyclium Lunæ quasi superius priusque → Solis auctoritas → assimilatio formæ et luminis → disparitio in solarizatione → reditus corniculatus post aliquot dies.
Apparentia Lunæ → relatio ad Solem → transformatio temporalis → restitutio alterius figuræ.
Oppositio inter superioritatem Lunæ et dominationem Solis reclassificatur ut distinctio inter apparentem ordinem et relationalem dependentiam.
Lumen non iam tantum proprietas visualis est, sed agens quod directionem, assimilationem et disparitionem coniungit.
Figura Lunæ mutatur a forma fixa in seriem statuum temporalium: hemicyclium, absentia, corniculata species.
Disparitio non classificatur ut annihilatio, sed ut extrema forma assimilationis ad Solem.
Vicinitas fit principium conceptuale quod hierarchiam, similitudinem et mutationem simul ordinat.
Surface: Luna variis figuris apparet, ad Solem lumen convertit, evanescit et postea corniculata redit.
Structural: Forma Lunæ per vicinitatem, radios et relationem ad Solem determinatur.
Metastrategic: Apparens superioritas ad subordinatam assimilationem convertitur; quod primo quasi prius apparet, postea a relatione ad Dominum explicatur.
Ontological/Temporal: Luna non ut ens visualiter immobile, sed ut corpus per periodicam transformationem et reversionem constitutum ponitur.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam catenam a superioritate apparente ad dominationem Solis, assimilationem, disparitionem et reditum corniculatum.
Cohaerentia interna firma est in eo quod omnes mutationes ad relationem Solarem et ad successionem temporalem referuntur.
Determinatio astronomica exacta non satis stabilitur, quia textus describit apparentias et non explicat mechanismum geometricum completum.
Verba «videtur», «apparente hominibus» et «quasi» limites epistemicos assertionibus imponunt.
Tensionalis commissura manet inter Lunæ quasi-superiorem positionem et eius statum Solariter subordinatum.
Altera tensio manet inter transformationem quasi irrevocabilem in Solem et reversionem ad figuram corniculatam.
Restitutio servat motum verum textus: ab apparentia formali ad relationem dominativam, inde ad solarizationem, absentiam et reappearance temporale.

translations.title: T H E O R E M A IIII.

items.text: The question is how the Moon's semicircle, although it seems as though higher and prior to the Solar Circle, is ordered toward the Sun.
The new constitution holds that the Moon observes the Sun as its Lord and King.
The foundation of the relation is the form of the Sun and its proximity, by which the Moon seems as though to be assimilated.
The proof proceeds through the turning of light, solar irradiation, and the apparent transformation of the Moon.
The movement is concluded through the Moon's disappearance from the sky and its return after some days in a horned figure.
The Moon's semicircle appears as though higher and prior to the Solar Circle.
The Sun is observed as the Moon's Lord and King.
The Moon seems to seek and cherish the Sun's form and proximity.
The Moon emulates the Sun's magnitude in its semidiameter, at least as it appears to ordinary people.
The Moon always turns its light toward the Sun.
The Moon seeks to be imbued with solar rays.
The Moon, as though transformed into the Sun, can disappear from the whole sky.
After some days the Moon appears again in a horned figure.
The Moon's appearance is temporally determined through a succession of figures and proximities.
The Moon, although it appears as though superior and prior, is not constituted as a power independent of the Sun.
The Moon's light is not presented as separated from its relation to the Sun.
The Moon does not remain in one and the same apparent figure.
Transformative assimilation to the Sun does not end in the Moon's perpetual presence in the sky.
The Moon's disappearance is not its final state, because the horned figure is afterward restored.
Magnitude here is not defined as an absolute measure, but as a magnitude apparent to ordinary people.
The Moon's apparent superiority does not remove its ordering toward the Sun.
The form and proximity of the Sun bring it about that the Moon seems not only to receive light, but also to be assimilated to the Sun.
The turning of light toward the Sun signifies a directional relation by which the Moon is visibly determined through the Sun.
The seeking of solar rays leads to a state in which the apparent distinction between the Moon and the Sun is most attenuated.
Disappearance from the sky and horned return constitute one periodic movement rather than an irrevocable conversion.
The horned figure after some days is a temporal effect of the Moon's relation to the Sun.
The apparent cosmic hierarchy simultaneously contains an inversion of orders: the Moon appears as though superior, but is causally and symbolically subordinated to the Sun.
The identity of the Moon is produced not as a visually stable substance, but as a series of relations to the Sun.
Light effects a medium of transformation: through irradiation, the Moon passes from its own figure to the threshold of solar likeness.
Time not only observes change, but orders the Moon's forms into a circle of appearances.
Relation to the Sun is at once the principle of the Moon's visibility, assimilation, and disappearance.
The system tacitly excludes a Moon whose form and light would be fully explained apart from relation to the Sun.
The system excludes a simple opposition between an active Moon and a passive Sun, because the Moon turns toward the Sun and is formed by it.
The system excludes an identity that would be wholly stabilized in one moment and one figure.
The system excludes a rigid distinction between visibility and transformation, because the same light shows and as though conceals the Moon.
The system excludes a rectilinear temporality in which transformation toward the Sun would proceed without return.
The text circumvents the idea of an absolutely proper lunar light, because light is explained in solar direction and rays.
The text precludes the Moon as the ultimate center of cosmic order, although its appearance momentarily seems as though superior.
The text leaves unavailable the idea of absolute separation between bodies defined through form, proximity, and light.
Impossible is a figure of the Moon that is once and for all determined outside solar vicissitude.
The constitutive absence is the Moon's autonomy: its appearance always presupposes something outside the Moon, namely the Sun.
The Moon's apparent superiority → recognition of the Sun as Lord and King → subordination of the relation.
The Sun's form and proximity → emulation of magnitude and turning of light → assimilation of the Moon.
Seeking of rays → quasi-transformation into the Sun → disappearance from the sky.
Temporal interval → reappearance of the horned figure → circular closure of the movement.
Initial appearance → solarized relation → apparent indistinction → absence → new appearance.
The Moon's semicircle as though higher and prior → the Sun's authority → assimilation of form and light → disappearance in solarization → horned return after some days.
The Moon's appearance → relation to the Sun → temporal transformation → restoration of another figure.
The opposition between the Moon's superiority and the Sun's domination is reclassified as a distinction between apparent order and relational dependence.
Light is no longer merely a visual property, but an agent that conjoins direction, assimilation, and disappearance.
The Moon's figure changes from a fixed form into a series of temporal states: semicircle, absence, horned appearance.
Disappearance is not classified as annihilation, but as the extreme form of assimilation to the Sun.
Proximity becomes a conceptual principle that simultaneously orders hierarchy, likeness, and change.
Surface: The Moon appears in various figures, turns its light toward the Sun, vanishes, and later returns horned.
Structural: The Moon's form is determined through proximity, rays, and relation to the Sun.
Metastrategic: Apparent superiority is converted into subordinate assimilation; what first appears as though prior is afterward explained by relation to the Lord.
Ontological/Temporal: The Moon is posited not as a visually immobile being, but as a body constituted through periodic transformation and return.
The axioms suffice to restore the chain from apparent superiority to the Sun's domination, assimilation, disappearance, and horned return.
The internal coherence is firm in that all changes are referred to solar relation and temporal succession.
Exact astronomical determination is not sufficiently established, because the text describes appearances and does not explain the complete geometric mechanism.
The words «videtur», «apparente hominibus» and «quasi» impose epistemic limits upon the assertions.
A tension remains between the Moon's quasi-superior position and its solar-subordinated state.
Another tension remains between quasi-irrevocable transformation into the Sun and return to the horned figure.
The restoration preserves the text's true movement: from formal appearance to dominative relation, thence to solarization, absence, and temporal reappearance.

identity.title: T H E O R E M A Iiii.

units.title: T H E O R E M A V.

items.text: Textus quaerit quomodo relatio inter semicirculum Lunarem et complementum Solare diem constituat.
Semicirculus Lunaris ad complementum Solare perductus unit vesperum et mane in unum diem.
Haec unitas constituit diem primum, non simpliciter continuationem dierum iam datorum.
Dies primus definitur per productionem Lucis et ad ordinem Philosophorum refertur.
Motus argumentationis est: figura complementaria → unificatio temporalium → constitutio principii → designatio philosophica.
Semicirculus Lunaris est figura partialis quae relatione ad aliud complementum determinatur.
Complementum Solare est terminus ad quem Semicirculus Lunaris perducitur.
Perductio semicirculi ad complementum constituit relationem completivam inter Lunam et Solem.
Vesper et mane in hac relatione ad unum diem pertinent.
Unus dies sic constitutus potest esse principium ordinis temporalium.
Dies primus est dies in quo Lux facta est.
Ordo hic ad designationem Philosophorum refertur.
Dies non ex vespera vel mane solitarie constituitur, sed ex eorum coniunctione.
Semicirculus Lunaris non ut figura plena aut iam completa tractatur.
Complementum Solare non est obiectum separatum a figura Lunari, sed eius terminatio constitutiva.
Primus dies non est unus dies inter alios, sed initium ordinis.
Lux non ad eventum posteriorem diei reducitur, sed ad eius constitutionem primariam pertinet.
Per complementum Solare, partialitas Semicirculi Lunaris in unitatem ordinis convertitur.
Si vesper et mane unum diem efficiunt, temporis divisio in formam unam ordinatur.
Dies ex relatione complementaria oritur, non ex sola successione temporali.
Unitas diei primum locum obtinet quia ad productionem Lucis refertur.
Designatio Philosophorum ponitur tamquam interpretatio ordinis primi diei.
Principium temporale producitur per completionem relationis inter figuras, non per positionem unius termini isolati.
Oppositio inter vesperum et mane in unitatem constitutivam reordinatur.
Lux fit principium ordinis, quia dies primus eam continet tamquam eventum originarium.
Philosophicum hic significat ordinem quo figurae cosmicae, tempora et Lux in unum principium legibile coniunguntur.
Falsum esse oportet diem tamquam quantitatem mere mensurabilem sine figura et complemento constitui.
Falsum esse oportet Lunam et Solem ut terminos sine relatione mutua intelligi.
Falsum esse oportet vesperum et mane duas unitates temporales independentes efficere.
Falsum esse oportet originem Lucis a constitutione diei primigenii separari.
Falsum esse oportet designationem Philosophorum ad nomen sine structura ordinis reduci.
Textus excludit tempus quod ante omnem relationem figuralem iam plene constitutum esset.
Textus excludit complementum purum quod terminum suum partialem non transformaret.
Textus excludit principium quod a productione Lucis nullam vim ordinatingem acciperet.
Textus tacite praecludit distinctionem inter sensum cosmologicum et sensum philosophicum tamquam duos ordines prorsus separatos.
Semicirculus Lunaris partialis + complementum Solare → relatio completiva.
Relatio completiva → coniunctio vesperis et matutini.
Coniunctio vesperis et matutini → unus dies.
Unus dies → primus terminus ordinis temporalis.
Primus dies + productio Lucis → principium originarium.
Principium originarium + relatio cosmica → designatio Philosophorum.
Semicirculus Lunaris → complementum Solare → vesper et mane coniunguntur → unus dies constituitur → dies primus instituitur → Lux principium fit → ordo Philosophorum designatur.
Tempus fit visibile tamquam effectus relationis inter figuras cosmicas.
Vesper et mane ex partibus oppositis in membra unius diei reclassificantur.
Dies primus non amplius solum chronologicus, sed ontogeneticus apparet, quia cum productione Lucis coniungitur.
Relatio Lunaris-Solaris denuo describitur ut principium ordinis, non ut mera observatio astrorum.
Philosophicum collocatur in ipsa conversione figurae cosmicae in ordinem temporalem et lucis principium.
**Surface:** Semicirculus Lunaris ad complementum Solare perducitur, et vesper ac mane unum diem efficiunt.
**Structural:** Complementatio figurae mechanismum constitutivum diei praebet.
**Metastrategic:** Textus quaestionem de figura cosmica in quaestionem de productione ordinis convertit.
**Ontological/Temporal:** Dies primus et Lux tamquam origines ordinis temporalis constituuntur.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam seriem a semicirculo Lunari ad diem primum et Lucem.
Cohaerentia interna constat ex motu a partialitate ad complementum, deinde ad unitatem.
Relatio exacta inter verba «Philosophorum» et diem primum non plene determinatur.
Ambiguum manet utrum Philosophorum genitivus originem, proprietatem an interpretationem diei significet.
Systema firmissimum est in unificatione vesperis et matutini per complementum; fragilius est in transitione ad designationem Philosophorum.
Restitutio servat motum verum textus, sed ultimam qualificationem philosophicam non ultra verba fontis determinat.

translations.title: T H E O R E M V.

items.text: The text asks how the relation between the Lunar semicircle and the Solar complement constitutes the day.
The Lunar semicircle brought to the Solar complement unites evening and morning into one day.
This unity constitutes the first day, not merely the continuation of days already given.
The first day is defined through the production of Light and is referred to the order of the Philosophers.
The movement of the argument is: complementary figure → unification of temporal things → constitution of a principle → philosophical designation.
The Lunar semicircle is a partial figure determined by its relation to another complement.
The Solar complement is the term to which the Lunar semicircle is brought.
The bringing of the semicircle to the complement constitutes a completing relation between the Moon and the Sun.
Evening and morning, in this relation, belong to one day.
One day thus constituted can be the principle of the order of temporal things.
The first day is the day on which Light was made.
This order is referred to the designation of the Philosophers.
The day is not constituted from evening or morning in isolation, but from their conjunction.
The Lunar semicircle is not treated as a full or already completed figure.
The Solar complement is not an object separate from the Lunar figure, but its constitutive termination.
The first day is not one day among others, but the beginning of the order.
Light is not reduced to a later event of the day, but pertains to its primary constitution.
Through the Solar complement, the partiality of the Lunar semicircle is converted into the unity of an order.
If evening and morning make one day, the division of time is ordered into one form.
The day arises from a complementary relation, not from temporal succession alone.
The unity of the day holds the first place because it is referred to the production of Light.
The designation of the Philosophers is posited as an interpretation of the order of the first day.
A temporal principle is produced through the completion of the relation between figures, not through the positing of one isolated term.
The opposition between evening and morning is reordered into a constitutive unity.
Light becomes the principle of order because the first day contains it as an originating event.
The philosophical here signifies the order by which cosmic figures, times, and Light are joined into one intelligible principle.
It must be false that the day is constituted as a merely measurable quantity without figure and complement.
It must be false that the Moon and the Sun are understood as terms without mutual relation.
It must be false that evening and morning make two independent temporal unities.
It must be false that the origin of Light is separated from the constitution of the primordial day.
It must be false that the designation of the Philosophers is reduced to a name without a structure of order.
The text excludes a time that would already be fully constituted before every figural relation.
The text excludes a pure complement that would not transform its partial term.
The text excludes a principle that would receive no ordering force from the production of Light.
The text tacitly precludes the distinction between cosmological meaning and philosophical meaning as two altogether separate orders.
Partial Lunar semicircle + Solar complement → completing relation.
Completing relation → conjunction of evening and morning.
Conjunction of evening and morning → one day.
One day → first term of the temporal order.
First day + production of Light → originating principle.
Originating principle + cosmic relation → designation of the Philosophers.
Lunar semicircle → Solar complement → evening and morning are joined → one day is constituted → the first day is established → Light becomes principle → the order of the Philosophers is designated.
Time becomes visible as the effect of a relation between cosmic figures.
Evening and morning are reclassified from opposed parts into members of one day.
The first day appears no longer merely chronological, but ontogenetic, because it is joined with the production of Light.
The Lunar-Solar relation is redescribed as a principle of order, not as a mere observation of the stars.
The philosophical is situated in the very conversion of the cosmic figure into temporal order and the principle of Light.
**Surface:** The Lunar semicircle is brought to the Solar complement, and evening and morning make one day.
**Structural:** The completion of the figure provides the constitutive mechanism of the day.
**Metastrategic:** The text converts the question of cosmic figure into a question of the production of order.
**Ontological/Temporal:** The first day and Light are constituted as origins of temporal order.
The axioms suffice to reconstruct the sequence from the Lunar semicircle to the first day and Light.
The internal coherence consists in the movement from partiality to complement, then to unity.
The exact relation between the word «Philosophorum» and the first day is not fully determined.
It remains ambiguous whether the genitive Philosophorum signifies the origin, property, or interpretation of the day.
The system is strongest in the unification of evening and morning through complement; it is more fragile in the transition to the designation of the Philosophers.
The reconstruction preserves the true movement of the text, but does not determine the final philosophical qualification beyond the words of the source.

identity.title: T H E O R E M A V.

units.title: T H E O R E M A V I.

items.text: Quaestio est quomodo Sol et Luna, Cruci Rectilineae innixi, formas Hieroglyphicas numeris significantes exhibeant.
Figura rectilinea ad ternarium et quaternarium significandum resolvitur.
Ternarius ex duabus rectis et puncto communi, quaternarius ex quattuor rectis et quattuor angulis rectis constituitur.
Repetitio configurationum ad octonarium occulte producit, dum connexio ternarii et quaternarii ad septenarium primarium ducit.
Genus argumentationis est reconstructivum-symbolicum: a figura geometrica ad ordinationem numerorum et deinde ad significationem magicam procedit.
Figura rectilinea potest rationes numericas Hieroglyphice significare.
Duae rectae cum puncto communi ternarium constituunt.
Quattuor rectae quattuor angulos rectos includentes quaternarium constituunt.
Eadem elementa geometrica per repetitionem numerice multiplicari possunt.
Repetitio quaternarii ad octonarium pertinere potest.
Ternarius apud Patres et Sophos magicus est compositio Corporis, Spiritus et Animae.
Ternarius et quaternarius simul rationem septenarii primarii constituunt.
Septenarius ex duabus rectis et puncto communi, deinde ex quattuor rectis ab uno puncto separantibus, intelligitur.
Configuratio geometrica potest simul structuram numericam et significationem symbolicam sustinere.
Ternarius non ex tribus rectis simpliciter, sed ex duabus rectis et puncto communi definitur.
Quaternarius non ad numerum quattuor nudum reducitur, sed quattuor rectas et quattuor angulos rectos requirit.
Significatio Hieroglyphica non a figura qualibet, sed a ratione geometrica apposita procedit.
Octonarius non ut forma primaria, sed ut effectus repetitionis occulte se offert.
Septenarius non ut series numerica abstracta, sed ut compositio configurationum geometricarum instituitur.
Auctor de praedecessoribus Magis non certitudinem, sed dubitationem profert.
Si duae rectae puncto communi copulantur, figura eorum ternariam significationem accipit.
Si quattuor rectae quattuor angulos rectos includunt, figura eorum quaternariam significationem accipit.
Si configuratio quaternaria bis repetitur, octonarius ut effectus eiusdem ordinis manifestari potest.
Si ternarius magicus Corpus, Spiritum et Animam continet, numerus ternarius formam compositionis ontologicae accipit.
Si ternarius et quaternarius coniunguntur, septenarius ut compositio primarium appellari potest.
Punctum commune primum copulationem, punctum unum cum rectis separantibus deinde divisionem contrariarum partium designat.
Numerus in hoc systemate non est quantitas separata a figura, sed relatio inter rectas, puncta, angulos et repetitiones.
Eadem figura potest plures ordines significationis generare, quia geometria simul numerum, compositionem et hieroglyphicum sustinet.
Ternarius et quaternarius in septenario non tantum numeri consecutivi, sed modi copulationis et separationis inter se fiunt.
Repetitio structuram latentem producit quae in prima configuratione nondum tota conspicitur.
Significatio magica oritur cum relatio geometrica ad compositionem Corporis, Spiritus et Animae transfertur.
Systema implicite negat numerum esse significatione carentem mensuram externam figurae.
Systema implicite excludit separationem absolutam inter geometrice descriptum et symbolice significatum.
Systema excludit interpretationem quae repetitionem mechanicam sine novo ordine numerico relinqueret.
Systema non admittit ut copulatio et separatio sint operationes sine numerica aut hieroglyphica consequentia.
Systema implicite negat primarium ordinem numerorum sine configuratione generatrice stabiliri posse.
Textus circumagit possibilitatem figurae purae, quae nec numerum nec significationem ontologicam generaret.
Argumentatio praecludit discretionem inter mathematicam formam et magicam interpretationem.
Absentia regulae completae de repetitione ostendit ordinem octonarii tamquam latentem, non plene formalizatum.
Impossibilis intra systema fit numerus qui a suis relationibus geometricis separari possit.
Rectilinea Crux → relatio rectarum et punctorum → numerica significatio Hieroglyphica.
Duae Rectae + Punctum Commune → Ternarius → Corpus / Spiritus / Anima.
Quattuor Rectae + Quattuor Anguli Recti → Quaternarius → repetitio configurationis.
Quaternarius × repetitio → Octonarius occultus.
Ternarius + Quaternarius → Septenarius Primarius.
Punctum Commune → Copulatio; Punctum Unum + Rectae Separantes → Contrariae Partes.
Geometrica descriptio → relatio numerica → translatio magica → hieroglyphica clausura.

Sol et Luna super Cruce Rectilinea → quaestio de significatione figurae → distinctio ternarii et quaternarii → repetitio ad octonarium → compositio ternarii et quaternarii in septenario → connexio geometriae cum ternario magico.
Figura rectilinea fit tabula in qua punctum, recta, angulus et repetitio simul legi possunt.
Numeri ternarius, quaternarius, septenarius et octonarius ex seriebus abstractis in configurationes visuales convertuntur.
Ternarius a numero simplici in compositionem Corporis, Spiritus et Animae denuo classificatur.
Quaternarius a collectione quattuor elementorum in structuram inclusivam quattuor angulorum rectangulorum mutatur.
Septenarius fit effectus coniunctionis inter copulationem ternariam et separationem quaternariam.
Octonarius fit ordo latentis repetitionis, non prima species figurae.
Surface: Sol et Luna Cruci Rectilineae innituntur, cui figurae geometricae attribuuntur.
Structural: Rectae, puncta et anguli numeros per copulationem, inclusionem, separationem et repetitionem generant.
Metastrategic: Lectio figurae a descriptione geometrica ad ordinationem hieroglyphicam et magicam transfertur.
Ontological/Temporal: Ternarius Corpus, Spiritum et Animam componit; repetitio ordinem latentem posterius manifestat.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad motum principalem a Cruce Rectilinea ad ternarium, quaternarium, octonarium et septenarium restituendum.
Fundamentum significationis Solis et Lunae in figura non ulterius explicatur quam per innixionem Cruci.
Relatio formalis qua ternarius et quaternarius septenarium constituunt indicatur, sed non plene demonstratur.
Status octonarii ambiguus manet, quia repetitio bis et eius exactus numericus effectus non omnino formalizantur.
Systema interne cohaeret, dum geometria tamquam generatrix numerorum et significationum assumitur.
Firmissimum est discrimen inter ternarium ex copulatione et quaternarium ex inclusione angulari.
Restitutio verum textus motum servat, sed clausura numerica et interpretatio latentis octonarii partim vi synthetica nituntur.

translations.title: T H E O R E M V I.

items.text: The question is how the Sun and Moon, resting upon the Rectilinear Cross, display Hieroglyphic forms signifying numbers.
The rectilinear figure is resolved into the signification of the ternary and the quaternary.
The ternary is constituted from two straight lines and a common point, the quaternary from four straight lines and four right angles.
The repetition of configurations covertly produces the octonary, while the connection of the ternary and quaternary leads to the primary septenary.
The kind of argumentation is reconstructive-symbolic: it proceeds from geometric figure to the ordering of numbers and then to magical signification.
A rectilinear figure can signify numerical relations hieroglyphically.
Two straight lines with a common point constitute the ternary.
Four straight lines enclosing four right angles constitute the quaternary.
The same geometric elements can be numerically multiplied through repetition.
The repetition of the quaternary can pertain to the octonary.
Among the Fathers and the Wise, the magical ternary is the composition of Body, Spirit, and Soul.
The ternary and quaternary together constitute the ratio of the primary septenary.
The septenary is understood from two straight lines and a common point, then from four straight lines separating from one point.
A geometric configuration can simultaneously sustain numerical structure and symbolic signification.
The ternary is defined not simply from three straight lines, but from two straight lines and a common point.
The quaternary is not reduced to the bare number four, but requires four straight lines and four right angles.
Hieroglyphic signification proceeds not from any figure whatsoever, but from an applied geometric ratio.
The octonary presents itself not as a primary form, but covertly as an effect of repetition.
The septenary is instituted not as an abstract numerical series, but as a composition of geometric configurations.
Concerning the predecessor Magi, the author advances not certainty, but doubt.
If two straight lines are joined by a common point, their figure receives ternary signification.
If four straight lines enclose four right angles, their figure receives quaternary signification.
If a quaternary configuration is repeated twice, the octonary can manifest as an effect of the same order.
If the magical ternary contains Body, Spirit, and Soul, the ternary number receives the form of an ontological composition.
If the ternary and quaternary are joined, the septenary can be called primary as a composition.
The common point first signifies conjunction, then the one point with separating straight lines signifies the division of contrary parts.
Number in this system is not a quantity separate from figure, but a relation among straight lines, points, angles, and repetitions.
The same figure can generate several orders of signification, because geometry simultaneously sustains number, composition, and the hieroglyphic.
In the septenary, the ternary and quaternary become not merely consecutive numbers, but modes of conjunction and separation in relation to one another.
Repetition produces a latent structure that is not yet wholly visible in the first configuration.
Magical signification arises when a geometric relation is transferred to the composition of Body, Spirit, and Soul.
The system implicitly denies that number is an external measure of figure devoid of signification.
The system implicitly excludes an absolute separation between what is geometrically described and what is symbolically signified.
The system excludes an interpretation that would leave mechanical repetition without a new numerical order.
The system does not admit that conjunction and separation are operations without numerical or hieroglyphic consequence.
The system implicitly denies that the primary order of numbers can be established without a generative configuration.
The text circumscribes the possibility of a pure figure that would generate neither number nor ontological signification.
The argumentation precludes a distinction between mathematical form and magical interpretation.
The absence of a complete rule concerning repetition shows the order of the octonary as latent, not fully formalized.
Within the system, a number that could be separated from its geometric relations becomes impossible.
Rectilinear Cross → relation of straight lines and points → numerical Hieroglyphic signification.
Two Straight Lines + Common Point → Ternary → Body / Spirit / Soul.
Four Straight Lines + Four Right Angles → Quaternary → repetition of configuration.
Quaternary × repetition → covert octonary.
Ternary + Quaternary → Primary Septenary.
Common Point → Conjunction; One Point + Separating Straight Lines → Contrary Parts.
Geometric description → numerical relation → magical translation → hieroglyphic closure.

Sun and Moon upon the Rectilinear Cross → question concerning the signification of the figure → distinction of ternary and quaternary → repetition to the octonary → composition of ternary and quaternary in the septenary → connection of geometry with the magical ternary.
The rectilinear figure becomes a map in which point, straight line, angle, and repetition can be read simultaneously.
The ternary, quaternary, septenary, and octonary numbers are converted from abstract series into visual configurations.
The ternary is reclassified from a simple number into a composition of Body, Spirit, and Soul.
The quaternary is changed from a collection of four elements into an inclusive structure of four right angles.
The septenary becomes the effect of a conjunction between ternary conjunction and quaternary separation.
The octonary becomes an order of latent repetition, not the first appearance of the figure.
Surface: The Sun and Moon rest upon the Rectilinear Cross, to which geometric figure is attributed.
Structural: Straight lines, points, and angles generate numbers through conjunction, inclusion, separation, and repetition.
Metastrategic: The reading of the figure is transferred from geometric description to hieroglyphic and magical ordering.
Ontological/Temporal: The ternary composes Body, Spirit, and Soul; repetition subsequently manifests a latent order.
The axioms suffice to reconstruct the principal movement from the Rectilinear Cross to the ternary, quaternary, octonary, and septenary.
The foundation of the signification of the Sun and Moon in the figure is not further explained than through their resting upon the Cross.
The formal relation by which the ternary and quaternary constitute the septenary is indicated, but not fully demonstrated.
The status of the octonary remains ambiguous, because repetition twice and its exact numerical effect are not wholly formalized.
The system coheres internally, provided that geometry is assumed as the generator of numbers and significations.
Strongest is the distinction between the ternary from conjunction and the quaternary from angular inclusion.
The reconstruction preserves the true movement of the text, but numerical closure and the interpretation of the latent octonary rest partly upon synthetic force.

identity.title: T H E O R E M A V I.

units.title: T H E O R. V I I.

items.text: Dislocatio elementorum quaerit regulam reditus ad sedes naturales.
Experientia reditus per rectas lineas homogenearum partium ostendit.
Ex uno puncto in quattuor contrarias partes ductae rectae mysterium quattuor elementorum innuunt.
Geometrica productio lineae ex puncti fluxu exemplar praebet productioni linearum elementarium.
Stilla, tamquam punctum physicum, per casum continuum fluxum mechanicis Magiae praebet.
Numeratio quaternaria per summationem unitatum ad denarium extenditur et numerorum symbolicae structurae rationem aperit.
Motus argumentationis est: dislocatio → reditus rectilineus → punctum et fluxus → elementa → numeratio → denarium.
Partes homogeneae, extra sedes naturales dimotae, ad easdem sedes naturaliter redeunt.
Reditus naturalis partium dislocatarum per rectas lineas fit.
Elementata singula tandem in quattuor elementa resolvi possunt.
Quattuor lineae ab uno puncto in contrarias partes excurrentes quattuor elementorum mysterium exprimere possunt.
Linea geometrica ex puncti fluxu producitur.
Lineae elementares ex stilla, tamquam puncto physico, per casum continuum producuntur.
Casus continuus stillae in Mechanica Magia fluxui respondet.
Numeratio quaternaria per unum, duo, tria et quattuor ad denarium summatim pervenit.
Quaternarius ad denarium referri potest per signa numerationis priscis philosophis attributa.
Ternarius per relationem ad septenarium numerice determinatur.
Elementa extra sedes naturales non manent.
Dislocatarum partium reditus non est indeterminatus aut sine directione.
Elementata non sunt ultima indivisibilia, quia in elementa resolvi possunt.
Linea non ut res puncto prorsus separata concipitur, sed ex puncti fluxu producitur.
Stilla non est punctum mere geometricum, sed punctum physicum cui casus continuus accedit.
Quaternarius non clauditur in numero quattuor, sed ad denarium summatione extenditur.
Numerorum significatio non reducitur ad appellationes ordinarias, sed per relationes doctrinales constituitur.
Si partes homogeneae ad sedes naturales per rectas redeunt, recta linea mechanismum restitutionis naturalis exhibet.
Si elementata in quattuor elementa resolvuntur, quattuor directiones ex uno puncto structuram compositionis elementaris figurant.
Si linea ex puncti fluxu producitur, punctum principium staticum non est, sed origo cuiusdam productionis.
Si stilla est punctum physicum et casus eius continuus est, productio elementarium linearum est processus, non forma iam completa.
Si unum, duo, tria et quattuor simul numerantur, quaternarius seriem constituit quae in denarium summatim clauditur.
Si quaternarius ad denarium et ternarius ad septenarium referuntur, numeri nexum inter structuram simplicem et extensionem symbolicam efficiunt.
Natura restitutiva et Magia mechanica sub eadem productionis ratione coniunguntur: origo punctiformis per fluxum ordinatum ad figuras pervenit.
Elementorum unitas non simpliciter praesupponitur, sed ex dislocatione, resolutione et directione linearum generatur.
Geometria fit translatio inter physicam observationem et structuram magicam.
Numeratio fit forma ontologicae ordinationis: aggregatio unitatum ad denarium non tantum calculum, sed clausuram structurae indicat.
Punctum, stilla, linea, elementum et numerus in una serie generationis inter se convertuntur.
Falsum esse oportet naturam ut ordinem corporum omnino inertem et sine reditu esse.
Falsum esse oportet lineam ut figuram a puncto et eius motu independentem esse.
Falsum esse oportet elementa ut extrema et irreducibilia corpora sine compositione esse.
Falsum esse oportet casum ut mera perturbatio sine continua productione esse.
Falsum esse oportet numerum ut seriem clausam et a relationibus symbolicis separatam esse.
Falsum esse oportet physicam, geometriam et Magiam tres ordines omnino disiunctos constituere.
Textus excludit mundum in quo formae sine origine punctiformi et sine fluxu producuntur.
Textus excludit materiam cui nulla sedes naturalis, nulla directio et nullus reditus competant.
Textus excludit numerum purum, cui nulla transformatio ontologica vel symbolica respondeat.
Textus excludit separationem principii mathematici a materia physica: punctum geometricum sine stilla physica machinam non absolvit.
Textus tacite praecludit distinctionem inter productionem naturalem et operationem magicam, quam sub communi fluxus ratione ordinat.
Dislocatio partium → observatio reditus → restitutio per rectas → positio sedium naturalium.
Unum punctum → quattuor lineae contrariae → quattuor elementa → resolutio elementatorum.
Punctum geometricum → fluxus → linea producta → analogia cum stilla physica.
Stilla physica → casus continuus → lineae elementares → Mechanica Magia.
Unum + duo + tria + quattuor → quaternarius aggregatus → denarius.
Quaternarius et ternarius → numerationes doctrinales → relatio denarii et septenarii.
Motus universus: perturbatio apparens → ordo naturalis → figura geometrica → processus physicus → significatio magica → clausura numerica.
Elementorum dislocatio → experientia reditus → recta ut via naturalis → quattuor directiones ex uno puncto.
Quattuor directiones → resolutio elementatorum → mysterium quattuor elementorum.
Punctum → fluxus → linea → stilla physica → casus continuus → productio magica.
Quaternarius numericus → summa unitatum → denarius → relatio ad antiquas doctrinas numericas.
Structura quaternaria et ternaria → extensiones denaria et septenaria → ordo numericus symbolicus.
Dislocatio, quae initio perturbatio videtur, denuo classificatur ut condicio restitutionis naturalis.
Recta linea non amplius est figura geometrica tantum, sed index reditus et instrumentum compositionis elementaris.
Punctum transit ab unitate immobili ad principium fluxus et productionis.
Stilla physicam materiam et punctum geometricum coniungit sub una genealogia lineae.
Quattuor elementa non ut inventarium separatum, sed ut quattuor directiones ex communi origine intelliguntur.
Numeri quattuor, decem, tres et septem ordinantur ut transformationes inter diversas amplitudines structurae.
Terminus «Mechanica Magia» agrum naturalis causationis et artis magicae in unam rationem fluxionalem redigit.
Surface: Observantur partes homogeneae dislocatae, rectilineus earum reditus, stilla cadens et series numerica.
Structural: Reditus, fluxus et resolutio constituunt mechanismum quo ex origine punctiformi formae et elementa producuntur.
Metastrategic: Geometria et numeratio adhibentur ut media quibus observatio physica in mysterium magicum et doctrinam symbolicam convertitur.
Ontological/Temporal: Ens non ut forma fixa, sed ut productum fluxus continui, casus, resolutionis et aggregationis concipitur.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam principalem machinam: dislocatio ad sedes redit, reditus per rectas fit, et recta ex puncti fluxu producitur.
Additio stillae physicae et casus continui nexum inter geometriam et Mechanicam Magicam absolvit.
Axiomata numerica quaternarium ad denarium referunt, sed vim exactam relationis ternarii ad septenarium non plene determinant.
Structura interne cohaeret in transitu punctum → fluxus → linea → elementum; cohaerentia minor est in transitu numerationis ad doctrinam philosophicam.
Firmissima est analogia inter reditum naturalem, lineam geometricam et productionem mechanicam.
Fragilior est transitus ab observatione experientiali ad «mysterium» quattuor elementorum, quia analogia sola probationem substituit.
Textus iterat inscriptionem «THEOR. VII» ante doctrinam numerorum; unitas inter duas expositiones formaliter non explicatur.
Restitutio servat verum motum textus, dummodo nexus inter physicam, geometriam, Magiam et numerationem tamquam analogicus, non tamquam demonstratio stricte deductiva, intellegatur.

translations.title: T H E O R Y. V I I.

items.text: The displacement of the elements seeks the rule of return to their natural places.
Experience shows return through straight lines of homogeneous parts.
Straight lines drawn from one point into four opposite directions suggest the mystery of the four elements.
The geometrical production of a line from the flux of a point provides a model for the production of elementary lines.
A drop, as a physical point, through continuous falling provides flux to the mechanics of Magia.
Quaternary counting is extended to ten through the summation of units and discloses the rationale of symbolic structures of numbers.
The movement of the argument is: displacement → rectilinear return → point and flux → elements → counting → ten.
Homogeneous parts, removed outside their natural places, naturally return to those same places.
The natural return of displaced parts occurs through straight lines.
Individual elementata can ultimately be resolved into four elements.
Four lines running out from one point into opposite directions can express the mystery of the four elements.
A geometrical line is produced from the flux of a point.
Elementary lines are produced from a drop, as a physical point, through continuous falling.
The continuous falling of a drop corresponds to flux in Mechanica Magia.
Quaternary counting, through one, two, three, and four, reaches ten by summation.
The quaternary can be referred to ten through signs of counting attributed to ancient philosophers.
The ternary is numerically determined through relation to the septenary.
The elements do not remain outside their natural places.
The return of displaced parts is not indeterminate or without direction.
Elementata are not ultimate indivisibles, because they can be resolved into elements.
A line is not conceived as a thing wholly separate from a point, but is produced from the flux of a point.
A drop is not a merely geometrical point, but a physical point to which continuous falling is added.
The quaternary is not enclosed within the number four, but is extended to ten by summation.
The signification of numbers is not reduced to ordinary appellations, but is constituted through doctrinal relations.
If homogeneous parts return to their natural places by straight lines, the straight line displays the mechanism of natural restoration.
If elementata are resolved into four elements, four directions from one point figure the structure of elementary composition.
If a line is produced from the flux of a point, the point is not a static principle, but the origin of a certain production.
If a drop is a physical point and its falling is continuous, the production of elementary lines is a process, not an already completed form.
If one, two, three, and four are counted together, the quaternary constitutes a series that is summatively closed in ten.
If the quaternary is referred to ten and the ternary to seven, numbers effect a connection between simple structure and symbolic extension.
Restorative nature and mechanical Magia are joined under the same rationale of production: a point-like origin arrives at figures through ordered flux.
The unity of the elements is not simply presupposed, but is generated from displacement, resolution, and the direction of lines.
Geometry becomes a translation between physical observation and magical structure.
Counting becomes a form of ontological ordering: the aggregation of units to ten indicates not only calculation, but the closure of a structure.
Point, drop, line, element, and number are mutually transformed within a single series of generation.
It must be false that nature is an entirely inert order of bodies without return.
It must be false that a line is a figure independent of a point and its motion.
It must be false that the elements are ultimate and irreducible bodies without composition.
It must be false that falling is a mere disturbance without continuous production.
It must be false that number is a closed series separated from symbolic relations.
It must be false that physics, geometry, and Magia constitute three entirely disjoined orders.
The text excludes a world in which forms are produced without a point-like origin and without flux.
The text excludes matter to which no natural place, no direction, and no return belong.
The text excludes pure number, to which no ontological or symbolic transformation corresponds.
The text excludes the separation of mathematical principle from physical matter: a geometrical point without a physical drop does not complete the machine.
The text tacitly precludes a distinction between natural production and magical operation, which it orders under a common rationale of flux.
Displacement of parts → observation of return → restoration through straight lines → positing of natural places.
One point → four opposite lines → four elements → resolution of elementata.
Geometrical point → flux → produced line → analogy with a physical drop.
Physical drop → continuous falling → elementary lines → Mechanica Magia.
One + two + three + four → aggregated quaternary → ten.
Quaternary and ternary → doctrinal countings → relation of ten and seven.
Universal movement: apparent disturbance → natural order → geometrical figure → physical process → magical signification → numerical closure.
Displacement of the elements → experience of return → straight line as natural path → four directions from one point.
Four directions → resolution of elementata → mystery of the four elements.
Point → flux → line → physical drop → continuous falling → magical production.
Numerical quaternary → sum of units → ten → relation to ancient numerical doctrines.
Quaternary and ternary structure → denary and septenary extensions → symbolic numerical order.
Displacement, which at first appears a disturbance, is reclassified as a condition of natural restoration.
The straight line is no longer merely a geometrical figure, but an indication of return and an instrument of elementary composition.
The point passes from an immobile unit to a principle of flux and production.
The drop joins physical matter and the geometrical point under one genealogy of the line.
The four elements are understood not as a separate inventory, but as four directions from a common origin.
The numbers four, ten, three, and seven are ordered as transformations among diverse magnitudes of structure.
The term «Mechanica Magia» reduces the field of natural causation and magical art to a single fluxional rationale.
Surface: Displaced homogeneous parts, their rectilinear return, a falling drop, and a numerical series are observed.
Structural: Return, flux, and resolution constitute the mechanism by which forms and elements are produced from a point-like origin.
Metastrategic: Geometry and counting are employed as means by which physical observation is converted into magical mystery and symbolic doctrine.
Ontological/Temporal: Being is conceived not as a fixed form, but as the product of continuous flux, falling, resolution, and aggregation.
The axioms suffice to reconstruct the principal mechanism: displacement returns to places, return occurs through straight lines, and a straight line is produced from the flux of a point.
The addition of the physical drop and continuous falling completes the connection between geometry and Mechanica Magia.
The numerical axioms refer the quaternary to ten, but do not fully determine the exact force of the relation of the ternary to the septenary.
The structure coheres internally in the transition point → flux → line → element; coherence is less in the transition from counting to philosophical doctrine.
The analogy between natural return, geometrical line, and mechanical production is strongest.
More fragile is the transition from experiential observation to the «mystery» of the four elements, because analogy alone substitutes for proof.
The text repeats the inscription «THEOR. VII» before the doctrine of numbers; the unity between the two expositions is not formally explained.

The reconstruction preserves the true movement of the text, provided that the connection among physics, geometry, Magia, and counting is understood as analogical, not as strictly deductive demonstration.

identity.title: T H E O R. V I I.

items.text: Quaestio centralis est quomodo Quaternarius ad Denarium referatur.
Textus novam quaestionis constitutionem proponit, qua numeratio, figura litteralis et symbolum crucis in una serie considerantur.
Fundamentum est summa numerorum 1, 2, 3 et 4, quae denarium constituit.
Probatio extenditur a structura numerica ad crucem rectilineam ex quattuor rectis compositam.
Argumentatio est reconstructiva et symbolico-genealogica: numerus → figura → littera → Denarium → relatio ternarii ad septenarium.
Quaternarius, secundum expansionem cabalisticam et usitatam numerationis phrasin, Denarium summatim exhibet.
Numeri unus, duo, tria et quatuor simul decem conficiunt.
Pythagorica auctoritas confirmat identitatem numerorum 1, 2, 3 et 4 cum Denario.
Crux rectilinea ex quattuor rectis indicatur.
Crux rectilinea litterae vicesimae primae Romani alphabeti respondet.
Crux rectilinea a philosophis Latinis antiquissimis ad Denarium significandum assumpta est.
Locus crucis in eadem serie definitur ubi Ternarius vim suam per Septenarium ducit.
Numeralis compositio et figura crucis in eodem ordine symbolico cohaerent.
Relatio crucis ad Denarium non est temere constituta.
Crux non tractatur ut figura sine numerali vel alphabetica determinatione.
Denarius non separatur a serie quae per Quaternarium, crucem, Ternarium et Septenarium ordinatur.
Significatio crucis non reducitur ad eius formam geometricam nudam, sed terminatur in functione numerali.
Quaternarius ad Denarium ducit per additionem graduum 1 + 2 + 3 + 4.
Figura quattuor rectarum potest esse vehiculum visibilis eiusdem relationis quam numerus quaternarius arithmeticus exhibet.
Littera Romani alphabeti vicesima prima fit nexus inter figuram crucis et ordinem alphabeticum.
Assumptio crucis a philosophis Latinis antiquis auctoritatem genealogicam significationi Denarii addit.
Positio crucis in serie non est tantum descriptiva, sed a transitu virtutis Ternarii per Septenarium ordinatur.
Numerus, littera et figura efficiunt systema conversionis in quo eadem unitas symbolica per modos arithmeticum, alphabeticum et geometricum producitur.
Significatio Denarii constituitur non per unum signum isolatum, sed per ordinem graduum et relationum inter Quaternarium, Ternarium et Septenarium.
Historia assumptionis a philosophis Latinis convertit correspondentiam numericam in traditionem doctrinalem atque legitimam.
Systema non admittit divisionem absolutam inter arithmeticam, alphabetum et geometriam.
Forma visibilis non potest esse symbolice indifferens, quia quattuor rectae ad numeralem constitutionem referuntur.
Ordo numerorum non est mera enumeratio linearis, sed nexus graduum vim suam inter se transferentium.
Interpretatio non fundatur in arbitraria similitudine, sed in correspondentia inter compositionem numericam, formam et locum.
Textus circumit possibilitatem signi cuius figura, numerus et locus inter se non respondeant.
Excluditur mundus in quo Denarius simpliciter summa arithmetica maneret sine manifestatione figurali et alphabetica.
Indisponibilis fit interpretatio quae symbolum a serie ordinatrice Ternarii et Septenarii abstrahit.
Quaternarius → Expansio cabalistica → Denarius.
Quaternarius numericus → quattuor rectae → crux rectilinea.
Crux rectilinea → littera vicesima prima Romani alphabeti → signum ordinatum.
Signum crucis → assumptio philosophica Latina → significatio Denarii.
Ternarius → Septenarius → locus definitus crucis in serie.
Numerus + figura + littera + locus → unitas symbolica Denarii.
Quaternarius → summa 1, 2, 3, 4 → Denarius → figura quattuor rectarum → crux rectilinea → littera vicesima prima → assumptio Latina → locus per Ternarium et Septenarium definitus.
Quaternarius fit principium transitus inter numerum arithmeticum et signum figurale.
Crux denuo classificatur ut nexus geometricus, alphabeticus et numeralis, non ut figura tantum.
Denarius fit effectus ordinis compositi, non solum terminus additionis.
Relatio inter Ternarium et Septenarium constituit locum symboli intra seriem, ita ut positio ipsa vim significativam accipiat.
Surface: Quattuor numeri summati denarium efficiunt, et crux ex quattuor rectis componitur.
Structural: Eadem quaternaria forma numerum, figuram crucis et litteram alphabeticam colligat.
Metastrategic: Interpretatio operatur per translationem inter ordines arithmeticum, geometricum, alphabeticum et doctrinalem.
Ontological/Temporal: Signum habet locum in ordine graduum, ubi vis Ternarii per Septenarium ad manifestationem crucis pervenit.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam productionem Denarii ex Quaternario et ad explicandam crucem ut eius signum.
Nexus inter litteram vicesimam primam et numerum Denarium in textu affirmatur, sed eius mechanismus ulterior non explicatur.
Relatio qua Ternarius vim suam per Septenarium ducit indicatur, non formaliter demonstratur.
Systema interne cohaeret dum numerus, figura et locus eandem symbolicam seriem sustinent.
Firmitas maxima est in additione 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10; commissura fragilior est transitus ab arithmetica ad auctoritatem traditionis Latinae.
Restitutio servat verum motum textus: a Quaternario numerico ad Denarium, a Denario ad crucem, et a cruce ad locum eius in serie symbolica.
The central question is how the Quaternary is related to the Denary.
The text proposes a new formulation of the question, in which numbering, literal figure, and the symbol of the cross are considered in a single series.
The foundation is the sum of the numbers 1, 2, 3, and 4, which constitutes the Denary.
The proof extends from numerical structure to the rectilinear cross composed of four straight lines.
The argumentation is reconstructive and symbolic-genealogical: number → figure → letter → Denary → relation of the Ternary to the Septenary.
The Quaternary, according to the cabalistic expansion and the customary phrasing of numeration, summarily displays the Denary.
The numbers one, two, three, and four together make ten.
Pythagorean authority confirms the identity of the numbers 1, 2, 3, and 4 with the Denary.
The rectilinear cross is indicated by four straight lines.
The rectilinear cross corresponds to the twenty-first letter of the Roman alphabet.
The rectilinear cross was adopted by the most ancient Latin philosophers to signify the Denary.
The place of the cross in the same series is defined where the Ternary conducts its power through the Septenary.
Numerical composition and the figure of the cross cohere in the same symbolic order.
The relation of the cross to the Denary is not established at random.
The cross is not treated as a figure without numerical or alphabetical determination.
The Denary is not separated from the series ordered through the Quaternary, the cross, the Ternary, and the Septenary.
The significance of the cross is not reduced to its bare geometrical form, but is delimited in numerical function.
The Quaternary leads to the Denary through the addition of the degrees 1 + 2 + 3 + 4.
The figure of four straight lines can be the visible vehicle of the same relation that the arithmetical quaternary number displays.
The twenty-first letter of the Roman alphabet becomes the link between the figure of the cross and alphabetical order.
The adoption of the cross by ancient Latin philosophers adds genealogical authority to the significance of the Denary.
The position of the cross in the series is not merely descriptive, but is ordered by the passage of the power of the Ternary through the Septenary.
Number, letter, and figure produce a system of conversion in which the same symbolic unity is produced through arithmetical, alphabetical, and geometrical modes.
The significance of the Denary is constituted not by one isolated sign, but by an order of degrees and relations among the Quaternary, Ternary, and Septenary.
The history of adoption by Latin philosophers converts numerical correspondence into a doctrinal and legitimate tradition.
The system does not admit an absolute division between arithmetic, alphabet, and geometry.
Visible form cannot be symbolically indifferent, because four straight lines refer to numerical constitution.
The order of numbers is not a mere linear enumeration, but a nexus of degrees transferring their power among themselves.
Interpretation is founded not on arbitrary resemblance, but on correspondence among numerical composition, form, and place.
The text precludes the possibility of a sign whose figure, number, and place do not correspond to one another.
A world is excluded in which the Denary would remain simply an arithmetical sum without figural and alphabetical manifestation.
An interpretation that abstracts the symbol from the ordering series of the Ternary and Septenary becomes unavailable.
Quaternary → Cabalistic expansion → Denary.
Numerical Quaternary → four straight lines → rectilinear cross.
Rectilinear cross → twenty-first letter of the Roman alphabet → ordered sign.
Sign of the cross → Latin philosophical adoption → significance of the Denary.
Ternary → Septenary → defined place of the cross in the series.
Number + figure + letter + place → symbolic unity of the Denary.
Quaternary → sum of 1, 2, 3, 4 → Denary → figure of four straight lines → rectilinear cross → twenty-first letter → Latin adoption → place defined through the Ternary and Septenary.
The Quaternary becomes the principle of transition between arithmetical number and figural sign.
The cross is reclassified as a geometrical, alphabetical, and numerical nexus, not as a figure alone.
The Denary becomes the effect of a composite order, not merely the term of an addition.
The relation between the Ternary and the Septenary constitutes the place of the symbol within the series, such that position itself acquires significative force.
Surface: Four numbers added together produce the Denary, and the cross is composed of four straight lines.
Structural: The same quaternary form binds together number, the figure of the cross, and the alphabetical letter.
Metastrategic: Interpretation operates through translation among arithmetical, geometrical, alphabetical, and doctrinal orders.
Ontological/Temporal: The sign has a place in an order of degrees, where the power of the Ternary reaches the manifestation of the cross through the Septenary.
The axioms suffice to reconstruct the production of the Denary from the Quaternary and to explain the cross as its sign.
The link between the twenty-first letter and the Denary number is affirmed in the text, but its further mechanism is not explained.
The relation by which the Ternary conducts its power through the Septenary is indicated, not formally demonstrated.
The system coheres internally so long as number, figure, and place sustain the same symbolic series.
The greatest firmness lies in the addition 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10; the more fragile joint is the transition from arithmetic to the authority of Latin tradition.
The reconstruction preserves the true movement of the text: from the numerical Quaternary to the Denary, from the Denary to the cross, and from the cross to its place in the symbolic series.

items.text: Quaestio centralis est quomodo MONAS, SOL et LVNA per separationem linearum et coniunctionem circularem inter se congruere possint.
Textus proponit congruentiam horum terminorum per operationem geometricam elementorum Magiae.
Fundamentum operationis est separatio exactissima in proprias Lineas.
Probatio procedit per circulos ex peripheriis linearum descriptos et in complemento SOLARI coniunctos.
Argumentatio est demonstrativa-reconstructiva: separationem geometricam in coniunctionem proportionatam convertit.
Conclusio est quod proportio Crucis DENARIA huiusmodi coniunctioni inserviat et quantitatem congruentiae patefaciat.
MONAS, SOL et LVNA sunt termini quorum congruentia demonstranda est.
Quattuor Elementorum Magia materiam operationis geometricam praebet.
Quaevis magnitudo data in Lineas separari potest.
Lineae possunt per leges Geometriae in circulos describi.
Peripheriae linearum ad coniunctionem circularem ordinari possunt.
Coniunctio circularis in complemento SOLARI institui potest.
Separatio et coniunctio simul proportionem inter MONADEM, SOLEM et LVNAM constituunt.
Crux DENARIA est forma proportionis quae huic relationi inservit.
Quantitas proportionis ex ipsa coniunctione circulari cognosci potest.
Congruentia MONADIS, SOLIS et LVNAE non per similitudinem indefinitam, sed per separationem in Lineas constituitur.
Separatio non est dissolutio sine ordine, sed separatio exactissima in partes determinatas.
Coniunctio non praecedit separationem, sed post eam per peripherias linearum efficitur.
Proportio non relinquitur absque mensura, quia per Crucem DENARIAM determinatur.
Operatio non excedit leges Geometriae, quia descriptio circuli eis explicite innititur.
Si MONAS, SOL et LVNA per quattuor Elementorum Magiam in Lineas separantur et Linearum peripheriae circulos efficiunt, tunc eorum coniunctio circularis fieri potest.
Si coniunctio circularis in complemento SOLARI fit, tunc separatio linearum ad ordinem solarem refertur.
Cum separatio et coniunctio in una operatione componantur, proportio MONADIS, SOLIS et LVNAE fit demonstrabilis.
Si Crux DENARIA huic coniunctioni inservit, proportio non solum exsistit sed etiam quantificari potest.
Geometria hic non est mera descriptio formarum, sed medium quo separatio et coniunctio in unam proportionem convertuntur.

Congruentia inter MONADEM, SOLEM et LVNAM producitur per seriem transformationum: materia Elementorum in Lineas, Lineae in circulos, circuli in coniunctionem solarem, coniunctio in proportionem denariam.
Crux DENARIA obtinet munus clausurae formalis, quia relationem inter terminos post operationem geometricam stabilit.
Systema tacite excludit congruentiam quae sine separatione praevia aut sine mediis geometricis immediate assereretur.
Systema excludit oppositionem absolutam inter MONADEM, SOLEM et LVNAM, quia differentia eorum in ordinem coniunctionis transformatur.
Systema excludit proportionem pure symbolicam quae a constructione circulari et a mensura DENARIA separata esset.
Argumentatio impossibilem reddit statum in quo separatio et coniunctio sibi opponuntur ut operationes incompatibiles.
Argumentatio non admittit relationem inter MONADEM, SOLEM et LVNAM quae neque in circularem ordinem neque in proportionem formalem reduci possit.
Quattuor Elementorum Magia → separatio exactissima in Lineas → determinatio partium ordinatarum.
Lineae datae → peripheriae linearum → circuli secundum leges Geometriae.
Circuli linearum → coniunctio circularis → complementum SOLARE.
Coniunctio circularis → proportio MONADIS, SOLIS et LVNAE → servitium Crucis DENARIAE.
Proportio constructa → quantitas congruentiae → cognitio ordinis inter tres terminos.
Congruentia quaerenda → materia quattuor Elementorum → separatio in Lineas → circuli ex peripheriis → coniunctio in complemento SOLARI → proportio Crucis DENARIA → quantitas congruentiae.
Differentia inter MONADEM, SOLEM et LVNAM → ordinatio geometrica differentiae → coniunctio circularis → relatio proportionalis.
MONAS, SOL et LVNA e terminis separatis in seriem unius constructionis geometricae reclassificantur.
Separatio et coniunctio apparent ut gradus complementarii eiusdem operationis, non ut processus contrarii.
Proportio fit obiectum constructibile et mensurabile, quia a Lineis, circulis et Cruce DENARIA derivatur.
Ager solaris non est tantum locus coniunctionis, sed complementum quod ordinem circularem recipit et stabilit.
Surface: Textus separat MONADEM, SOLEM et LVNAM in Lineas earumque peripherias circulis describit.
Structural: Separatio linearum et coniunctio circularis mechanismum constituunt quo termini diversi in proportionem communem rediguntur.
Metastrategic: Argumentatio quaestionem de congruentia transfert ad quaestionem de ordine operationum geometricarum.
Ontological/Temporal: Relatio inter tres terminos tamquam processus successivus constituitur, in quo separatio praecedit coniunctionem et coniunctio proportionem efficit.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam minimam machinam: separatio linearum, constructio circulorum, coniunctio solaris et proportio denaria.
Systema interne cohaeret, quia omnis gradus posterior ex operatione priore pendet.
Firmitas maxima est in transitu a Lineis ad circulos, quem leges Geometriae directe sustentant.
Minus determinatum manet quomodo singulae MONADIS, SOLIS et LVNAE Lineae construantur et quomodo Crux DENARIA exacte mensuretur.
Commissura fragilis est transitus a coniunctione circulari ad assertionem de quantitate proportionis, quia regula huius quantificationis non explicatur.
Restitutio servat verum motum textus, sed vim conclusionis de quantitate partim ex designatione Crucis DENARIAE, non ex demonstratione numerica explicita, accipit.

translations.title: T H E O R. I X.

items.text: The central question is how MONAS, SOL, and LVNA can correspond with one another through the separation of lines and circular conjunction.
The text proposes the congruence of these terms through the geometric operation of the elements of Magic.
The foundation of the operation is the most exact separation into proper Lines.
The proof proceeds through circles described from the peripheries of lines and joined in the SOLAR complement.
The argumentation is demonstrative-reconstructive: it converts geometric separation into proportionate conjunction.
The conclusion is that the DENARY Cross serves such conjunction and discloses the quantity of congruence.
MONAS, SOL, and LVNA are terms whose congruence is to be demonstrated.
The Magic of the Four Elements supplies the geometric material of the operation.
Any given magnitude can be separated into Lines.
Lines can be described into circles according to the laws of Geometry.
The peripheries of lines can be ordered toward circular conjunction.
Circular conjunction can be instituted in the SOLAR complement.
Separation and conjunction together establish the proportion among MONAS, SOL, and LVNA.
The DENARY Cross is a form of proportion that serves this relation.
The quantity of proportion can be known from circular conjunction itself.
The congruence of MONAS, SOL, and LVNA is established not through indefinite similarity, but through separation into Lines.
Separation is not dissolution without order, but the most exact separation into determinate parts.
Conjunction does not precede separation, but is effected after it through the peripheries of lines.
Proportion is not left without measure, because it is determined through the DENARY Cross.
The operation does not exceed the laws of Geometry, because the description of the circle explicitly rests upon them.
If MONAS, SOL, and LVNA are separated into Lines through the Magic of the Four Elements, and the peripheries of the Lines produce circles, then their circular conjunction can occur.
If circular conjunction occurs in the SOLAR complement, then the separation of lines is referred to solar order.
When separation and conjunction are combined in one operation, the proportion of MONAS, SOL, and LVNA becomes demonstrable.
If the DENARY Cross serves this conjunction, proportion not only exists but can also be quantified.
Geometry here is not a mere description of forms, but the means by which separation and conjunction are converted into one proportion.

Congruence among MONAS, SOL, and LVNA is produced through a series of transformations: the material of the Elements into Lines, Lines into circles, circles into solar conjunction, conjunction into denary proportion.
The DENARY Cross assumes the function of formal closure, because it stabilizes the relation among the terms after the geometric operation.
The system tacitly excludes a congruence that would be asserted immediately without prior separation or without geometric means.
The system excludes absolute opposition among MONAS, SOL, and LVNA, because their difference is transformed into an order of conjunction.
The system excludes a purely symbolic proportion that would be separated from circular construction and from DENARY measure.
The argumentation renders impossible a state in which separation and conjunction oppose one another as incompatible operations.
The argumentation does not admit a relation among MONAS, SOL, and LVNA that could be reduced neither to circular order nor to formal proportion.
Magic of the Four Elements → most exact separation into Lines → determination of ordered parts.
Given Lines → peripheries of lines → circles according to the laws of Geometry.
Circles of lines → circular conjunction → SOLAR complement.
Circular conjunction → proportion of MONAS, SOL, and LVNA → service of the DENARY Cross.
Constructed proportion → quantity of congruence → knowledge of the order among the three terms.

Congruence to be sought → material of the four Elements → separation into Lines → circles from peripheries → conjunction in the SOLAR complement → proportion of the DENARY Cross → quantity of congruence.
Difference among MONAS, SOL, and LVNA → geometric ordering of difference → circular conjunction → proportional relation.
MONAS, SOL, and LVNA are reclassified from separate terms into a series of one geometric construction.
Separation and conjunction appear as complementary stages of the same operation, not as contrary processes.
Proportion becomes a constructible and measurable object, because it is derived from Lines, circles, and the DENARY Cross.
The solar field is not merely the place of conjunction, but the complement that receives and stabilizes circular order.
Surface: The text separates MONAS, SOL, and LVNA into Lines and describes their peripheries by circles.
Structural: The separation of lines and circular conjunction constitute the mechanism by which diverse terms are reduced to a common proportion.
Metastrategic: The argumentation transfers the question of congruence to the question of the order of geometric operations.
Ontological/Temporal: The relation among the three terms is established as a successive process, in which separation precedes conjunction and conjunction effects proportion.
The axioms suffice to restore the minimal mechanism: separation of lines, construction of circles, solar conjunction, and denary proportion.
The system coheres internally, because every later stage depends on the prior operation.
The greatest firmness lies in the transition from Lines to circles, which the laws of Geometry directly support.
It remains less determined how the individual Lines of MONAS, SOL, and LVNA are constructed and how the DENARY Cross is exactly measured.
The fragile joint is the transition from circular conjunction to the assertion concerning the quantity of proportion, because the rule of this quantification is not explained.

The reconstruction preserves the true movement of the text, but receives the force of the conclusion concerning quantity partly from the designation of the DENARY Cross, not from an explicit numerical demonstration.
