items.text: Quaestio est quomodo Aries, ut initium Triplicitatis Igneæ, in praxi MONADIS significationem habeat.
Signum astronomicum Arietis ad ministerium ignis intra praxim Monadis additur.
MONAS per unum contextum hieroglyphicum comprehenditur, non per signa separatim dispersa.
In hac Monade Luna et Sol elementa sua separare volunt, dum proportio denaria constituitur.
Separatio elementorum fit ministerio ignis, qui simul principium operativum et transitus inter partes est.
Aries ex loco cæli designato exordium Triplicitatis Igneæ notat.
Nota astronomica Arietis in praxi Monadis ad ministerium ignis significandum adhibetur.
Monadis una consideratio hieroglyphica per unum contextum hieroglyphicum proferri debet.
MONAS Luna et Solem tamquam elementa coniuncta continet.
Luna et Sol elementa sua separari volunt.
Separatio elementorum intra Monadem non est simplex dissolutio, sed operatio ordinata.
Proportio denaria in elementis separatis viget.
Ignis ministerium separationis perficit.
Figura hieroglyphica relationes inter Lunam, Solem, elementa et ignem simul exhibet.
Significatio Arietis derivatur ex coordinatione loci astronomici, ignis et structurae Monadis.
Monadis non tamquam compositio signorum independentium, sed tamquam unus contextus hieroglyphicus tractanda est.
Separatio Lunae et Solis non significat annihilationem eorum communis ordinis in Monade.
Proportio elementorum non relinquitur indefinita, sed denaria ratione circumscribitur.
Ignis non est elementum passive adiectum, sed ministerium eius separationem constituit.
Aries non est ornamentum graphicum sine munere, quia ad significationem ignis et exordii refertur.
Figura non est mera imago astronomica, quia relationes operativas inter partes significat.
Aries locum initialem ignis intra ordinem Monadis designat.
Nota astronomica Arietis fit signum operationis, quia ministerium ignis per eam introducitur.
Unitas contextus hieroglyphici permittit ut Luna, Sol, elementa et ignis tamquam systema relationale legantur.
Separatio elementorum necessario postulat proportionem quae relationem partium conservet.
Ignis est medium quo unitas Monadis in distinctiones ordinatas convertitur.
Significatio Monadis generatur ex simultanea retentione unitatis, separationis et proportionis.
Unitas Monadis non opponitur differentiationi, sed eam continet tamquam processum internum.
Separatio fit intelligibilis tantum si per proportionem et ministerium ignis in ordinem convertitur.
Astronomia, geometria symbolica et operatio alchemica in uno signo hieroglyphico coniunguntur.
Ignis constituit transitum ontologicum a Monade indivisa ad elementa distincta sine ruptura totalis unitatis.
Exordium astronomicum simul initium processus transformationis internæ Monadis evadit.
Systema excludit conceptionem Monadis ut unitatis omnino immobilis et sine differentiatione.
Systema excludit separationem quae sine proportione, mensura vel relatione fieret.
Systema excludit interpretationem ignis ut materiae tantum inter elementa collocatae.
Systema excludit disiunctionem inter signum astronomicum et operationem hieroglyphicam.
Systema excludit ideam quod sensus unius signi ex sola figura visibili sine contextu relationum oriatur.
Textus circumit possibilitatem ut unitas et divisio sint principia inter se absolute incompatibilia.
Textus praecludit cosmologiam in qua partes separatae nullam proportionem communem retinent.
Textus tacite removet ordinem in quo ignis nihil intermedii vel transformativi efficit.
Textus non admittit significationem quae inter astronomiam, symbolum et praxim nullum nexum causalem vel formativum agnoscat.
Locus astronomicus Arietis → Exordium Triplicitatis Igneæ → Requisitio ministerii ignis.
Nota astronomica Arietis + praxis Monadis → Significatio ignis ut operationis internæ.
MONAS una → Luna et Sol in communi contextu → Elementorum distinctio.
Elementorum distinctio + proportio denaria → Separatio ordinata.
Separatio ordinata + ministerium ignis → Contextus hieroglyphicus completus.
Contextus hieroglyphicus → Unitas quae differentiationem continet → Interpretatio Monadis tamquam processus.
Locus Arietis → Exordium ignis → Additio notæ astronomicæ → Praxi Monadis applicatio.
Unitas Monadis → Coniunctio Lunae et Solis → Voluntas separationis → Proportio denaria.
Proportio denaria → Ministerium ignis → Separatio ordinata → Unus contextus hieroglyphicus.
Figura composita → Relatio astronomica, elementaris et operativa → Reconstitutio Monadis ut unitatis differentiantis.
Aries fit non solum initium zodiacale, sed index processus quo ignis distinctionem internam Monadis producit.
Luna et Sol reclassificantur ab imaginibus caelestibus ad elementa intra operationem proportionatam.
Separatio et unitas desinunt esse oppositiones simplices, quia separatio tamquam actus internus unitatis describitur.
Ignis reponitur in categoria mediationis operativæ, non in categoria elementi tantum descripti.
Figura hieroglyphica ordinat simul locum, substantias, proportionem et operationem, ita ut lectio linearis singulorum signorum insufficiens fiat.
Surface: Aries, Luna, Sol, elementa et ignis in contextu hieroglyphico coniunguntur.
Structural: Monadis unitas per separationem elementorum et proportionem denariam operatur.
Metastrategic: Signum astronomicum convertitur in instrumentum quo relatio inter caelum, figuram et praxim legitur.
Ontological/Temporal: Exordium Arietis initium temporale simul et transitum ontologicum ab unitate ad distinctionem constituit.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam catenam ab Ariete et exordio ignis ad separationem Lunae et Solis.
Unitas contextus, separatio elementorum, proportio denaria et ministerium ignis sunt nuclei sine quibus argumentatio deficit.
Structura interne cohaeret, quia divisio non extra Monadem ponitur, sed ab eius operatione generatur.
Relatio exacta proportionis denariae non plene determinatur: textus eam statuit, sed modum eius numerice explicatum non tradit.
Status ignis inter elementum, signum et ministerium operativum non omnino disambiguatur.
Figura relationes principales exhibet, sed sola inspectio eius non sufficit ad omnem ordinem transformationis deducendum.
Restitutio servat verum motum textus: locus astronomicus → ministerium ignis → separatio proportionata → contextus hieroglyphicus unificatus.

translations.title: T H E O R. X.

items.text: The question is how Aries, as the beginning of the Fiery Triplicity, has significance in the practice of the MONAD.
The astronomical sign of Aries is added for the service of fire within the practice of the Monad.
The MONAD is comprehended through one hieroglyphic context, not through signs separately scattered.
In this Monad the Moon and the Sun wish to separate their elements, while a tenfold proportion is established.
The separation of the elements occurs through the service of fire, which is at once the operative principle and the passage between the parts.
Aries, from its designated place in heaven, marks the beginning of the Fiery Triplicity.
The astronomical mark of Aries is employed in the practice of the Monad to signify the service of fire.
A single hieroglyphic consideration of the Monad must be set forth through one hieroglyphic context.
The MONAD contains the Moon and the Sun as conjoined elements.
The Moon and the Sun wish for their elements to be separated.
The separation of the elements within the Monad is not a simple dissolution, but an ordered operation.
A tenfold proportion prevails in the separated elements.
Fire accomplishes the service of separation.
The hieroglyphic figure simultaneously displays the relations among the Moon, the Sun, the elements, and fire.
The significance of Aries is derived from the coordination of astronomical place, fire, and the structure of the Monad.
The Monad is to be treated not as a composition of independent signs, but as one hieroglyphic context.
The separation of the Moon and the Sun does not signify the annihilation of their common order in the Monad.
The proportion of the elements is not left indefinite, but is delimited by a tenfold ratio.
Fire is not an element passively added, but its service constitutes separation.
Aries is not a graphic ornament without function, because it refers to the significance of fire and of beginning.
The figure is not a mere astronomical image, because it signifies operative relations among the parts.
Aries designates the initial place of fire within the order of the Monad.
The astronomical mark of Aries becomes a sign of operation, because through it the service of fire is introduced.
The unity of the hieroglyphic context allows the Moon, the Sun, the elements, and fire to be read as a relational system.
The separation of the elements necessarily requires a proportion that preserves the relation of the parts.
Fire is the means by which the unity of the Monad is converted into ordered distinctions.
The significance of the Monad is generated from the simultaneous retention of unity, separation, and proportion.
The unity of the Monad is not opposed to differentiation, but contains it as an internal process.
Separation becomes intelligible only if it is converted into order through proportion and the service of fire.
Astronomy, symbolic geometry, and alchemical operation are joined in one hieroglyphic sign.
Fire constitutes the ontological passage from the undivided Monad to distinct elements without rupture of total unity.
The astronomical beginning simultaneously becomes the beginning of the process of the Monad's internal transformation.
The system excludes the conception of the Monad as a unity wholly immobile and without differentiation.
The system excludes a separation that would occur without proportion, measure, or relation.
The system excludes an interpretation of fire as merely matter placed among the elements.
The system excludes a disjunction between the astronomical sign and the hieroglyphic operation.
The system excludes the idea that the meaning of one sign arises from visible figure alone, without a context of relations.
The text avoids the possibility that unity and division are principles absolutely incompatible with one another.
The text precludes a cosmology in which separated parts retain no common proportion.
The text tacitly removes an order in which fire effects nothing intermediary or transformative.
The text does not admit a significance that acknowledges no causal or formative connection among astronomy, symbol, and practice.
Astronomical place of Aries → Beginning of the Fiery Triplicity → Requirement of the service of fire.
Astronomical mark of Aries + practice of the Monad → Significance of fire as an internal operation.
One MONAD → Moon and Sun in a common context → Distinction of the elements.
Distinction of the elements + tenfold proportion → Ordered separation.
Ordered separation + service of fire → Complete hieroglyphic context.
Hieroglyphic context → Unity that contains differentiation → Interpretation of the Monad as process.
Place of Aries → Beginning of fire → Addition of the astronomical mark → Application to the practice of the Monad.
Unity of the Monad → Conjunction of the Moon and the Sun → Will to separation → Tenfold proportion.
Tenfold proportion → Service of fire → Ordered separation → One hieroglyphic context.
Composite figure → Astronomical, elemental, and operative relation → Reconstitution of the Monad as differentiating unity.
Aries becomes not only a zodiacal beginning, but an index of the process by which fire produces the Monad's internal distinction.
The Moon and the Sun are reclassified from celestial images into elements within a proportionate operation.
Separation and unity cease to be simple oppositions, because separation is described as an internal act of unity.
Fire is repositioned in the category of operative mediation, not in the category of a merely described element.
The hieroglyphic figure orders place, substances, proportion, and operation simultaneously, so that a linear reading of individual signs becomes insufficient.
Surface: Aries, the Moon, the Sun, the elements, and fire are joined in a hieroglyphic context.
Structural: The unity of the Monad operates through the separation of the elements and tenfold proportion.
Metastrategic: The astronomical sign is converted into an instrument through which the relation among heaven, figure, and practice is read.
Ontological/Temporal: The beginning of Aries constitutes at once a temporal beginning and an ontological passage from unity to distinction.
The axioms suffice to reconstruct the chain from Aries and the beginning of fire to the separation of the Moon and the Sun.
The unity of the context, the separation of the elements, tenfold proportion, and the service of fire are the nuclei without which the argument fails.
The structure coheres internally, because division is not placed outside the Monad, but is generated by its operation.
The exact relation of the tenfold proportion is not fully determined: the text establishes it, but does not provide its numerically explained mode.
The status of fire between element, sign, and operative service is not wholly disambiguated.
The figure displays the principal relations, but inspection of it alone does not suffice to deduce the entire order of transformation.
The reconstruction preserves the true movement of the text: astronomical place → service of fire → proportionate separation → unified hieroglyphic context.

items.text: Quaestio centralis est quomodo nota mystica Arietis in ordine nycthemerae collocanda sit.
Figura duobus semicirculis in puncto communi connexis constituta locum aequinoctialem nycthemerae aptissime significat.
Fundamentum probationis est analogia inter formam signi et distributionem temporis per viginti quattuor horas.
Distributio aequinoctialis temporis occultas proportiones indicat.
Motus argumenti procedit a figura → ad locum temporalem → ad proportionem occultam → ad relationem cum Terra.
Nota mystica Arietis ex duobus semicirculis constituitur.
Semicirculi in puncto communi connexi sunt.
Nota Arietis ad locum aequinoctialem nycthemerae assignatur.
Nycthemera tempus viginti quattuor horarum continet.
Tempus nycthemerae modo aequinoctiali distribuitur.
Distributio aequinoctialis occultas proportiones denotat.
Proportiones dictae ad Terram referuntur.
Nota Arietis non ut figura libera, sed ut compositio duorum semicirculorum connexorum definitur.
Locus notae non extra ordinem aequinoctialem quaeritur.
Tempus nycthemerae non ut continuum indifferens, sed ut distributum et proportionale accipitur.
Proportiones indicatae non ad caelum solum, sed ad Terram referuntur.
Figura duorum semicirculorum et puncti communis formam temporaliter divisam repraesentare potest.
Assignatio ad locum aequinoctialem figuram in ordinem nycthemerae constituit.
Divisio aequinoctialis viginti quattuor horarum fit signum proportionis, non mera designatio temporis.
Nota Arietis relationem symbolicam inter configurationem figurae, ordinem temporis et Terram instituit.
Significatio hieroglyphica ex analogia ordinum provenit: forma signi ordinem temporalem reddit, ordo temporalis proportionem occultam manifestat.
Tempus terrestre intra symbolum caelesti specie constitutum theoretice ordinatur.
Nota mystica non solum obiectum caeleste designat, sed proportionem inter signum, tempus et locum terrestre producit.
Secretum signi in quantificabili distributione temporis positum est, quamquam ipsa proportio ulterius non determinatur.
Systema non admittit significationem quae a forma materiali notae et ab eius connexione interna seiungatur.
Systema non admittit tempus sine partitione aequinoctiali tamquam fundamentum huius significationis.
Systema non admittit proportionem occultam quae a relatione ad Terram omnino abstrahatur.
Systema tacite excludit interpretationem quae notam Arietis ad unam rem isolatam reducat.
Argumentatio circumit, quin explicite constituat, quomodo figura geometrica horas singulas aut partes temporis repraesentet.
Possibilitas signum esse meram conventionem arbitrariam praeclusa est.
Absens manet definitio formalis vocis «proportiones»; haec absentia efficit ut secretum interpretationis retineatur.
Non datur schema explicitum quo relatio inter «nostras» proportiones et Terram verificari possit.
Compositio duorum semicirculorum + connexio in puncto communi → unitas formalis notae.
Unitas formalis + assignatio ad locum aequinoctialem → insertio notae in ordine nycthemerico.
Nycthemera viginti quattuor horarum + distributio aequinoctialis → structura temporalis proportionata.
Structura temporalis proportionata → denotatio proportionum occultarum.
Proportiones occultae + relatio ad Terram → significatio terrestris notae mysticae.
Figura connexa → locus aequinoctialis → nycthemera viginti quattuor horarum → distributio aequinoctialis → proportiones occultae → relatio ad Terram.
Nota Arietis ex figura isolata in nodum relationis inter formam, tempus et Terram reclassificatur.
Nycthemera fit tabula proportionum, non tantum mensura horarum.
Aequinoctium fit principium ordinationis quo figura hieroglyphica temporaliter legibilis redditur.
«Occultum» non extra ordinem numerabilem ponitur, sed in distributione temporis iam constituitur.
**Surface:** Nota Arietis duobus semicirculis connexis describitur et ad locum aequinoctialem assignatur.
**Structural:** Viginti quattuor horae per modum aequinoctialem distribuuntur et in proportiones convertuntur.
**Metastrategic:** Lectio signi a designatione astrologica ad interpretationem hieroglyphicam relationum transit.
**Ontological/Temporal:** Tempus terrestre tamquam ordo occultas proportiones continens concipitur, non tamquam series neutra momentorum.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam transitionem a figura notae ad locum aequinoctialem et ad tempus distributum.
Restitutio servat motum a forma ad proportionem et a proportione ad Terram.
Interna cohaerentia pendet ex aequatione implicita inter formam semicirculorum et distributionem temporis.
Nondum satis determinatur quae proportiones «secretissimae» sint aut quomodo singulis partibus figurae respondeant.
Relatio vocis «nostras» ad Terram ambigua manet et argumentationem non plene claudit.
The central question is how the mystical sign of Aries is to be situated within the order of the nycthemeron.
A figure constituted by two semicircles joined at a common point most fittingly signifies the equinoctial position of the nycthemeron.
The foundation of the proof is the analogy between the form of the sign and the distribution of time over twenty-four hours.
The equinoctial distribution of time indicates hidden proportions.
The movement of the argument proceeds from figure → to temporal position → to hidden proportion → to relation with the Earth.
The mystical sign of Aries is constituted from two semicircles.
The semicircles are joined at a common point.
The sign of Aries is assigned to the equinoctial position of the nycthemeron.
The nycthemeron contains a span of twenty-four hours.
The time of the nycthemeron is distributed in an equinoctial manner.
The equinoctial distribution denotes hidden proportions.
The stated proportions refer to the Earth.
The sign of Aries is defined not as a free figure, but as a composition of two connected semicircles.
The position of the sign is not sought outside the equinoctial order.
The time of the nycthemeron is understood not as an indifferent continuum, but as distributed and proportional.
The indicated proportions are referred not to heaven alone, but to the Earth.
The figure of two semicircles and a common point can represent a temporally divided form.
Assignment to the equinoctial position places the figure within the order of the nycthemeron.
The equinoctial division of twenty-four hours becomes a sign of proportion, not a mere designation of time.
The sign of Aries establishes a symbolic relation between the configuration of the figure, the order of time, and the Earth.
Hieroglyphic significance arises from an analogy of orders: the form of the sign renders the temporal order, and the temporal order manifests hidden proportion.
Terrestrial time is theoretically ordered within a symbol constituted under a celestial aspect.
The mystical sign not only designates a celestial object, but produces a proportion between sign, time, and terrestrial place.
The secret of the sign lies in the quantifiable distribution of time, although the proportion itself is not further determined.
The system does not admit a meaning that is separated from the material form of the sign and from its internal connection.
The system does not admit time without equinoctial partition as the foundation of this meaning.
The system does not admit a hidden proportion that is wholly abstracted from relation to the Earth.
The system tacitly excludes an interpretation that reduces the sign of Aries to a single isolated thing.
The argument bypasses, without explicitly establishing, how the geometric figure represents individual hours or portions of time.
The possibility that the sign is a mere arbitrary convention is precluded.
A formal definition of the term «proportions» remains absent; this absence causes the secret of the interpretation to be retained.
No explicit schema is given by which the relation between «our» proportions and the Earth can be verified.
Composition of two semicircles + connection at a common point → formal unity of the sign.
Formal unity + assignment to the equinoctial position → insertion of the sign into the order of the nycthemeron.
Nycthemeron of twenty-four hours + equinoctial distribution → proportioned temporal structure.
Proportioned temporal structure → denotation of hidden proportions.
Hidden proportions + relation to the Earth → terrestrial significance of the mystical sign.
Connected figure → equinoctial position → nycthemeron of twenty-four hours → equinoctial distribution → hidden proportions → relation to the Earth.
The sign of Aries is reclassified from an isolated figure into a node of relation among form, time, and the Earth.
The nycthemeron becomes a table of proportions, not merely a measure of hours.
The equinox becomes a principle of ordering through which the hieroglyphic figure is rendered temporally legible.
«Hidden» is not placed outside numerical order, but is already constituted in the distribution of time.
**Surface:** The sign of Aries is described by two connected semicircles and assigned to the equinoctial position.
**Structural:** Twenty-four hours are distributed in an equinoctial manner and converted into proportions.
**Metastrategic:** The reading of the sign passes from astrological designation to a hieroglyphic interpretation of relations.
**Ontological/Temporal:** Terrestrial time is conceived as an order containing hidden proportions, not as a neutral series of moments.
The axioms suffice to reconstruct the transition from the figure of the sign to the equinoctial position and to distributed time.
The reconstruction preserves the movement from form to proportion and from proportion to the Earth.
Internal coherence depends on the implicit equation between the form of the semicircles and the distribution of time.
It is not yet sufficiently determined what the «most secret» proportions are or how they correspond to the individual parts of the figure.
The relation of the word «our» to the Earth remains ambiguous and does not fully close the argument.

units.title: T H E O R. Xii.

items.text: Quaestio est quomodo Notae Hieroglyphicae planetarum ex characteribus Lunae vel Solis cum signo Elementorum aut Arietis componantur et explicentur.
Quaestio in structuram processualem convertitur, quia signum Lunare per successiones elementatas ac revolutiones naturae interpretandum est.
Fundamentum expositionis est systema prius iactis Fundamentis, quo singulae figurae hieroglyphicae explicabiles redduntur.
Probatio procedit a natura Lunari ad Saturnum, Iovem et Mercurium, deinde ad substitutionem operativam Spiritus Magici et Solis.
Motus argumentationis est: compositio signorum → interpretatio Lunaris → successiones elementatae → mediazione Spiritus et Solis → impressio figurarum in Terram praeparatam.
Notae Hieroglyphicae quinque Planetarum a Sapientibus Magis traditae sunt.
Notae planetariae componuntur ex Characteribus Lunae vel Solis et signo Elementorum aut Arietis.
Signorum compositio per fundamenta iam posita explicari potest.
Natura Lunaris per scientiam Elementorum circa Terram revolvitur.
Eadem Natura Lunaris diversis gradibus vel vicibus elementatis sub nominibus Saturni, Iovis et Mercurii significatur.
Mercurius, quamvis Lunaris sit, quarta Revolutione produci potest.
Opus secretum non impugnatur si alii Sophi Mercurium quarta Revolutione productum esse volunt.
Spiritus Purissimus Magicus locum Lunae in opere λευκώσεως obtinere potest.
Virtus spiritualis potest cum Solo per quandam Mediam Naturalem sine verbis hieroglyphice operari.
Terra praeparata et simplicissima potest figuras geogamicas suscipere.
Spiritus Magicus figuras in Terram introducit atque imprimit.
Significatio planetaria non in nomine solo, sed in ordine compositivo et processu productionis figurarum consistit.
Notae Hieroglyphicae non sunt characteres simplices, sed compositiones ex pluribus signis.
Interpretatio signorum non separatur a fundamentis antea positis.
Productio Mercurii quarta Revolutione non excluditur propter opinionem aliorum Sophorum.
Operatio spiritualis non requirit verba vocalia, quia Sol hieroglyphice per Mediam Naturalem loqui potest.
Luna non est unica forma operativa operis, quia Spiritus Magicus eius locum administrare potest.
Cum Notae ex Luna vel Sole et signo Elementorum componantur, figura hieroglyphica simul originem astralem et determinationem elementarem exhibet.
Cum Natura Lunaris per plures vicissitudines elementatas describatur, nomina Saturni, Iovis et Mercurii gradus eiusdem processualis indicant.
Quarta Revolutio non delet ordinem Lunarem Mercurii, sed eum ad ulteriorem gradum productionis refert.
Substitutio Lunae per Spiritum Magicum mutat medium operis, non finem eius, qui est administratio λευκώσεως.
Operatio Solis fit translatio spiritualis in medium naturale, quo signa sine locutione materiali exprimuntur.
Impressio figurarum in Terram facit ut hieroglyphicum non solum interpretetur, sed materialiter producatur.
Systema planetarium ordinatur tamquam series transformationum unius naturae, non tamquam collectio entitatum astralium separatarum.
Hieroglyphicum fit machina transitus inter ordinem cosmologicum, processum magicum et inscriptionem materialem.
Nomina planetarum funguntur ut indices occultorum graduum operationis, quorum sensus plene non datur nisi per successionem et compositionem.
Spiritus Magicus instituit mediatorem inter Lunam, Solem, Elementa et Terram, ita ut operis unitas per substitutionem servetur.
Auctoritas tradita et interpretatio operativa simul sustentant systema: traditio praebet formas, fundamenta praebent regulas productionis.
Falsum esse oportet hieroglyphicum signum esse meram designationem planetariae sine compositione elementorum.
Falsum esse oportet successiones Saturni, Iovis et Mercurii esse nominum disiunctas potius quam gradus unius Naturae Lunaris.
Falsum esse oportet productionem magicam consistere in passiva receptione signorum, cum opus ad inscriptionem activam figurarum procedat.
Falsum esse oportet substitutionem Lunae per Spiritum Magicum continuitatem operis tollere.
Falsum esse oportet communicationem hieroglyphicam a voce, sermone vel locutione materiali pendere.
Textus excludit chaos signorum in quo figurae sine ordine genealogico vel processuali exsisterent.
Textus excludit dualismum absolutum inter operationem caelestem et operationem terrestrem.
Textus excludit ideam unius instrumenti cosmici immutabilis, quia Luna per Spiritum Magicum substitui potest.
Textus circumit sed plene non nominat regulam quae determinat quomodo singulae figurae ex quattuor vicibus elementatis producantur.
Textus tacite praecludit distinctionem inter significationem hieroglyphicam et efficaciam materialem: figura simul loquitur et agit.
Character Lunae vel Solis + signum Elementorum aut Arietis → Nota Hieroglyphica composita.
Nota Lunaris → Natura Lunaris → revolutio circa Terram → vicissitudines elementatae → indices Saturni, Iovis et Mercurii.
Quarta Revolutio + admissio doctrinae Sophorum → productio Mercurii sine contradictione cum proposito secreto.
Spiritus Purissimus Magicus pro Luna → administratio λευκώσεως → virtus spiritualis cum Solo.
Sol + Media Naturalis + silentium verborum → locutio hieroglyphica → Terra pura et simplex → introductio et impressio figurarum.

Notae planetariae compositae → explicabilitas per fundamenta priora → interpretatio signorum Lunarium → series revolutionum elementatarum → Mercurius quarta Revolutione → substitutio Lunae per Spiritum Magicum → actio Solis per Mediam Naturalem → impressio figurarum in Terram.
Diversitas nominum planetariorum → unitas Naturae Lunaris → gradatio processualis → translatio cosmica in operationem magicam → materialis effectus hieroglyphicus.
Signum planetarium fit obiectum quod simul secundum originem astralem, compositionem elementarem et gradum operationis classificatur.
Oppositio inter Lunae et Solis characteres reordinatur tamquam differentia inter principium, medium et complementum operis.
Nomina Saturni, Iovis et Mercurii reclassificantur ut stationes transformationis Naturae Lunaris.
Terra non amplius apparet ut finis passivus, sed ut superficies receptiva et productiva figurarum.
Silentium verborum fit condicio communicationis hieroglyphicae, non defectus communicationis.
Surface — Signa Lunae vel Solis cum Elementorum aut Arietis signo componuntur et figurae in Terram imprimuntur.
Structural — Una Natura Lunaris per revolutiones et vicissitudines elementatas in gradus Saturni, Iovis et Mercurii ordinatur.
Metastrategic — Interpretatio ex nominibus planetariis ad mechanismum productionis transfertur, ita ut controversia de quarta Revolutione systema non dissolvat.
Ontological/Temporal — Res magicae constituuntur ut series transformationum inter Lunam, Spiritum, Solem, Elementa et Terram, quarum tempora per revolutiones definiuntur.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam lineam principalem a compositione signorum ad inscriptionem figurarum.
Systema interne cohaeret, quia substitutio Lunae per Spiritum Magicum explicatur ut mutatio medii intra idem opus.
Firmitas maxima consistit in connexione inter compositionem signorum, successionem elementatam et effectum materialem.
Determinatio exacta quattuor revolutionum et relationis inter singulas figuras in textu excerpto nondum plena est.
Productio Mercurii quarta Revolutione admittitur, sed regula formalis huius productionis non explicatur.
Restitutio nititur aliquantum in terminis arcanis et in transitione a figura visibili ad processum invisibilem.
Schema servat verum motum textus: a forma composita ad ordinem processualem, inde ad mediationem spiritualem et ad effectum terrestre.

translations.title: T H E O R. XII.

items.text: The question is how the Hieroglyphic Notes of the planets are composed from the characters of the Moon or the Sun together with the sign of the Elements or of Aries, and how they are to be explained.
The question is converted into a processual structure, because the Lunar sign must be interpreted through elemental successions and revolutions of nature.
The foundation of the exposition is the system of Foundations previously laid down, by which the individual hieroglyphic figures are rendered explicable.
The demonstration proceeds from Lunar nature to Saturn, Jupiter, and Mercury, then to the operative substitution of the Magical Spirit and the Sun.
The movement of the argument is: composition of signs → Lunar interpretation → elemental successions → mediation of Spirit and Sun → impression of figures upon prepared Earth.
The Hieroglyphic Notes of the five Planets were handed down by the Magi Sages.
Planetary Notes are composed from the Characters of the Moon or the Sun and the sign of the Elements or of Aries.
The composition of signs can be explained through foundations already laid down.
Lunar Nature revolves around the Earth through knowledge of the Elements.
The same Lunar Nature is signified at different elemental degrees or turns under the names of Saturn, Jupiter, and Mercury.
Mercury, although Lunar, can be produced by the fourth Revolution.
The secret work is not impugned if other Sages hold that Mercury is produced by the fourth Revolution.
The Most Pure Magical Spirit can occupy the place of the Moon in the work of λευκώσεως.
Spiritual power can operate hieroglyphically with the Sun through a certain Natural Medium without words.
Prepared and most simple Earth can receive geogamic figures.
The Magical Spirit introduces and impresses figures into the Earth.
Planetary signification consists not in the name alone, but in the compositional order and the process of producing figures.
Hieroglyphic Notes are not simple characters, but compositions from several signs.
The interpretation of signs is not separated from the foundations previously laid down.
The production of Mercury by the fourth Revolution is not excluded on account of the opinion of other Sages.
Spiritual operation does not require spoken words, because the Sun can speak hieroglyphically through the Natural Medium.
The Moon is not the sole operative form of the work, because the Magical Spirit can administer its place.
Since the Notes are composed from the Moon or Sun and the sign of the Elements, the hieroglyphic figure displays at once an astral origin and an elemental determination.
Since Lunar Nature is described through several elemental vicissitudes, the names Saturn, Jupiter, and Mercury indicate stages of the same process.
The fourth Revolution does not erase Mercury's Lunar order, but refers it to a further stage of production.
The substitution of the Moon by the Magical Spirit changes the medium of the work, not its end, which is the administration of λευκώσεως.
The operation of the Sun is a spiritual transmission into a natural medium, whereby signs are expressed without material utterance.
The impression of figures upon Earth makes the hieroglyphic not only interpreted, but materially produced.
The planetary system is ordered as a series of transformations of one nature, not as a collection of separate astral entities.
The hieroglyphic becomes a machine of passage between cosmological order, magical process, and material inscription.
The names of the planets function as indices of hidden stages of operation, whose meaning is not fully given except through succession and composition.
The Magical Spirit establishes a mediator between Moon, Sun, Elements, and Earth, so that the unity of the work is preserved through substitution.
Handed-down authority and operative interpretation jointly sustain the system: tradition supplies the forms, the foundations supply the rules of production.
It must be false that a hieroglyphic sign is a mere designation of the planetary without a composition of elements.
It must be false that the successions of Saturn, Jupiter, and Mercury are disjoined names rather than stages of one Lunar Nature.
It must be false that magical production consists in the passive reception of signs, since the work proceeds to the active inscription of figures.
It must be false that the substitution of the Moon by the Magical Spirit removes the continuity of the work.
It must be false that hieroglyphic communication depends on voice, speech, or material utterance.
The text excludes a chaos of signs in which figures would exist without genealogical or processual order.
The text excludes an absolute dualism between celestial operation and terrestrial operation.
The text excludes the idea of one immutable cosmic instrument, because the Moon can be substituted by the Magical Spirit.
The text skirts around but does not fully name the rule that determines how individual figures are produced from four elemental turns.
The text tacitly forecloses the distinction between hieroglyphic signification and material efficacy: the figure speaks and acts simultaneously.
Character of the Moon or Sun + sign of the Elements or of Aries → composite Hieroglyphic Note.
Lunar Note → Lunar Nature → revolution around the Earth → elemental vicissitudes → indices of Saturn, Jupiter, and Mercury.
Fourth Revolution + acceptance of the doctrine of the Sages → production of Mercury without contradiction with the secret purpose.
Most Pure Magical Spirit in place of the Moon → administration of λευκώσεως → spiritual power with the Sun.
Sun + Natural Medium + silence of words → hieroglyphic speech → pure and simple Earth → introduction and impression of figures.

Composite planetary Notes → explicability through prior foundations → interpretation of Lunar signs → series of elemental revolutions → Mercury by the fourth Revolution → substitution of the Moon by the Magical Spirit → action of the Sun through the Natural Medium → impression of figures upon Earth.
Diversity of planetary names → unity of Lunar Nature → processual gradation → cosmic translation into magical operation → material hieroglyphic effect.
The planetary sign becomes an object classified simultaneously according to astral origin, elemental composition, and stage of operation.
The opposition between the characters of the Moon and Sun is reordered as a difference between the principle, medium, and completion of the work.
The names Saturn, Jupiter, and Mercury are reclassified as stations of the transformation of Lunar Nature.
Earth no longer appears as a passive end, but as a receptive and productive surface for figures.
The silence of words becomes a condition of hieroglyphic communication, not a failure of communication.
Surface — Signs of the Moon or Sun are composed with the sign of the Elements or of Aries, and figures are impressed upon Earth.
Structural — One Lunar Nature is ordered through revolutions and elemental vicissitudes into the stages of Saturn, Jupiter, and Mercury.
Metastrategic — Interpretation is transferred from planetary names to the mechanism of production, so that the controversy concerning the fourth Revolution does not dissolve the system.
Ontological/Temporal — Magical things are constituted as a series of transformations among Moon, Spirit, Sun, Elements, and Earth, whose times are defined by revolutions.
The axioms suffice to reconstruct the principal line from the composition of signs to the inscription of figures.
The system coheres internally, because the substitution of the Moon by the Magical Spirit is explained as a change of medium within the same work.
Its greatest strength consists in the connection between the composition of signs, elemental succession, and material effect.
The exact determination of the four revolutions and of the relation among the individual figures is not yet complete in the excerpted text.
The production of Mercury by the fourth Revolution is admitted, but the formal rule of this production is not explained.
The reconstruction relies to some extent on arcane terms and on the transition from visible figure to invisible process.
The schema preserves the true movement of the text: from composite form to processual order, thence to spiritual mediation and terrestrial effect.

identity.title: T H E O R. Xii.

items.text: Quaestio centralis est utrum character Martis ex Solis et Arietis hieroglyphicis, elementali magia interveniente, conflatus sit, atque utrum character Veneris ex Solis et pleniore Elementorum explicatione procedat.
Quaestio ita constituitur ut planetae non simpliciter denotentur, sed motum Solaris περιφορά et opus Ἀναζωπυρήσεως exprimant.
Fundamentum argumenti est progressus quo, perfecta lunari solarique Elementorum magia, Mercurius conspicuus emergit.
Probatio fit per identificationem Mercurii cum Philosoporum Mercurio, Microcosmo et Adamo, atque per correspondentiam huius ordinis cum anatomia Monadis Hieroglyphicae.
Motus argumentationis est: compositio hieroglyphica → circulatio Solaris → regeneratio → apparitio Mercurii → operatio animae separatae → ordinatio planetarum → confirmatio anatomiae Monadicae.
Genus argumentationis est reconstructivum, analogicum et alchemicum, quia signorum ordinem in processum cosmologicum et operativum restituit.
Character hieroglyphicus potest ex aliis characteribus hieroglyphicis componi.
Solis character principium constitutivum Martis et Veneris esse potest.
Elementale Magisterium compositionem hieroglyphicam mediat.
Planetae ad Solaris περιφοράν respiciunt.
Opus Ἀναζωπυρήσεως motum transformationis planetariae constituit.
Lunaris et Solaris Elementorum magia perfecta Mercurium conspicuum producit.
Mercurius Philosophorum est Microcosmus et Adam.
Anima a corpore arte Pyronomica separata operi Χρυσοκολλίνῳ praefici potest.
Anima separata Lunam, vel saltem Mercurium, Luciferum et Pyroenta ligare potest.
Sol Philosophorum potest tertius locus esse quo septenarius numerus completur.
Anatomia Monadis Hieroglyphicae arcana duorum Theorematum exacte et aperte respondet.
Correspondentia inter characteres planetarios et anatomiam Monadis potest significationem arcanorum exhibere.
Mars non ut figura isolata, sed ut compositio Solis, Arietis et Magisterii elementalis accipitur.
Venus non ad solam formam Solis reducitur, sed Elementorum pleniorem explicationem requirit.
Mercurius hic non est tantum planeta astronomicus, sed Mercurius Philosophorum, Microcosmus et Adam.
Sol non necessario locum Mercurii obtinet, quamvis quidam Expertissimi eum eodem gradu posuerint.
Opus non fit sine mediatione animae, si Sol Philosophorum loco Mercurii substituatur.
Operatio animae separatae non est facilis neque sine periculo.
Interpretatio non clauditur in singulis figuris, sed ad septenarii et totius anatomiae ordinem extenditur.
Si Mars ex Sole et Ariete per Magisterium elementale componitur, character Martis Solaris ordinis effectus fit.
Si Venus Solis et Elementorum pleniorem explicationem coniungit, eius character gradum ampliorem explicationis magicae designat.
Si planetae Solaris περιφοράν respiciunt et opus Ἀναζωπυρήσεως efficiunt, eorum series processus transformationis potius quam catalogum corporum indicat.
Perfecta Elementorum magia, lunari solarique coniuncta, condicionem constituit qua Mercurius conspicuus appareat.
Cum Mercurius Philosophorum Microcosmus et Adam sit, eius apparitio transitum ad hominis cosmici constitutionem significat.
Cum anima separata ad corpora planetaria vincula indissolubilia conferre possit, operatio planetaria ab animae mediatione pendet.
Cum Sol Philosophorum tertium locum implere possit, septenarius planetarum per duplicem ordinationem Mercurii et Solis completur.
Correspondentia Monadis cum duobus Theorematibus facit ut anatomia eius figurae non ornamentum, sed index arcanorum sit.
Signa planetaria in systema genealogicum convertuntur, in quo unum character ex altero per elementarem et solarem transformationem producitur.
Cosmologia, alchimia et anthropologia in eodem processu coalescunt, quia Mercurius simul est planeta, operativum medium, Microcosmus et Adam.
Anima separata fit nexus ontologicus inter corpus, planetas et opus alchemicum.
Septenarius non ex sola numeratione planetarum, sed ex gradibus transformationis et substitutionis constituitur.
Anatomia Monadis Hieroglyphicae se praebet ut compendium internum ordinis cosmici, non ut descriptionem externam figurae.
Systema excludit notionem characterum planetariorum ut signorum arbitrariorum et inter se independentium.
Systema excludit separationem rigidam inter astronomiam, alchemiam et anthropologiam.
Systema excludit regenerationem ut eventum puramente naturalem sine arte, magia et mediatione animae.
Systema excludit Microcosmum ut imaginem passivam mundi; Microcosmus hic est effectus transformationis operativae.
Systema excludit univocam identitatem Solis et Mercurii, quia utriusque locus variari potest secundum ordinem interpretativum.
Systema excludit operationem omnino tutam et immediatam, cum halitus ignei sulphureique periculum constituant.
Impossibilis fit interpretatio quae symbolum a processu formationis separat.
Indisponibilis fit cognitio quae ad visum superficiei hieroglyphicae sistit nec eius correspondentias operativas quaerit.
Praecluditur mundus in quo anima, elementa et planetae ordines prorsus heterogenei sunt.
Vetatur clausura uniuscuiusque signi in identitate fixa, quia characteres per circulationem, compositionem et substitutionem definiuntur.
Abest distinctio absoluta inter opus cosmologicum et opus humanum: idem processus a planetis ad animam et a figura ad anatomiam transit.
Character Solar principium → Character Martis et Arietis → Magisterium elementale → compositio Martis.
Sol + Elementorum explicatio plenior → character Veneris → gradus ampliatus magicae.
Circulatio Solaris → Opus Ἀναζωπυρήσεως → perfectio magia lunaris et Solaris → Mercurius conspicuus.
Mercurius conspicuus → Mercurius Philosophorum → Microcosmus et Adam.
Anima a corpore separata → praefectura operis Χρυσοκολλίνου → ligatio Lunae, Mercurii, Luciferi et Pyroentae.
Locus tertius Solis → completio septenarii → translatio ordinis planetarii in ordinem Monadis.
Duo Theoremata → arcana significata → correspondentia cum anatomia Monadis Hieroglyphicae.
Compositio Martis et Veneris → Solaris ordo planetarum → Ἀναζωπύρησις → Mercurius conspicuus.
Mercurius conspicuus → Mercurius Philosophorum → Microcosmus et Adam.
Limitatio substitutionis Solis → necessitas animae separatae → operatio difficilis et periculosa.
Anima operans → ligatio corporum planetariorum → completio septenarii per Solis locum.
Completio ordinis planetarii → arcana duorum Theorematum → confirmatio anatomiae Monadis Hieroglyphicae.
Characteres planetarii e signis separatis in seriem geneticam et transformativam reordinantur.
Mercurius denuo classificatur ut nodus communis cosmologiae, alchemiae et anthropologiae.
Anima separata fit obiectum operativum quod corpora planetaria coniungere potest, non tantum principium cognitionis.
Sol et Mercurius non amplius oppositionem simplicem constituunt, sed loca alternantia intra eundem ordinem septenarium.
Anatomia Monadis fit tabula compressionis qua ordo planetarius et arcana Theorematum simul leguntur.
Oppositio inter figuram et operationem corruit: figura ipsa processus magici et cosmici vestigium fit.
Surface: Characteres Martis, Veneris, Solis, Arietis, Lunae et Mercurii ut figurae hieroglyphicae inter se componuntur.
Structural: Elementale Magisterium, Solaris περιφορά et Ἀναζωπύρησις ordinem compositionis et regenerationis instituunt.

Ontological/Temporal: Realitas exhibetur ut processus graduum, substitutionum et transformationum, in quo Microcosmus per perfectam Elementorum magiam emergit.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam principalem catenam a compositione characterum ad correspondentiam Monadis.
Systema interne cohaeret dum signa planetaria ut gradus unius processus transformativi tractat.
Relatio inter duas formas Mercurii, Mercurium conspicuum et Mercurium Philosophorum, non omnino formaliter determinatur.

Vis argumenti firmissima est in correspondentia inter ordinem planetarium et anatomiam Monadis; fragilior est in probatione ipsius correspondentiae, quae praecipue ex assertione exactae et apertae responsionis pendet.
Restitutio servat motum fontis, sed non aufert eius quaestionalem et conditionalem formam.

The central question is whether the character of Mars was compounded from the hieroglyphics of the Sun and Aries, with elemental magic intervening, and whether the character of Venus proceeds from the Sun and a fuller explication of the Elements.
The question is thus framed so that the planets are not simply denoted, but express the Solar περιφορά and the work of Ἀναζωπυρήσεως.
The foundation of the argument is the progression by which, lunar and solar magic of the Elements having been perfected, conspicuous Mercury emerges.

The proof is made through the identification of Mercury with the Mercury of the Philosophers, the Microcosm, and Adam, and through the correspondence of this order with the anatomy of the Hieroglyphic Monad.

The movement of the argument is: hieroglyphic composition → Solar circulation → regeneration → appearance of Mercury → operation of the separated soul → ordering of the planets → confirmation of the Monadic anatomy.
The kind of argumentation is reconstructive, analogical, and alchemical, because it restores the order of signs to a cosmological and operative process.
A hieroglyphic character can be composed from other hieroglyphic characters.
The character of the Sun can be the constitutive principle of Mars and Venus.
The Elemental Magisterium mediates hieroglyphic composition.
The planets refer to the Solar περιφορά.
The work of Ἀναζωπυρήσεως constitutes the movement of planetary transformation.
Perfected lunar and solar magic of the Elements produces conspicuous Mercury.
The Mercury of the Philosophers is the Microcosm and Adam.
A soul separated from the body by the Pyronomic art can be set over the Χρυσοκολλίνῳ work.
The separated soul can bind the Moon, or at least Mercury, Lucifer, and Pyroenta.
The Sun of the Philosophers can be the third place by which the septenary number is completed.
The anatomy of the Hieroglyphic Monad corresponds exactly and openly to the arcana of the two Theorems.
The correspondence between planetary characters and the anatomy of the Monad can display the meaning of the arcana.
Mars is understood not as an isolated figure, but as a composition of the Sun, Aries, and the elemental Magisterium.
Venus is not reduced to the form of the Sun alone, but requires a fuller explication of the Elements.
Mercury here is not merely an astronomical planet, but the Mercury of the Philosophers, the Microcosm, and Adam.
The Sun does not necessarily occupy the place of Mercury, although certain most expert persons have placed it at the same rank.
The work is not accomplished without the mediation of the soul, if the Sun of the Philosophers is substituted in place of Mercury.
The operation of the separated soul is neither easy nor without danger.
The interpretation is not enclosed within individual figures, but extends to the order of the septenary and of the whole anatomy.
If Mars is composed from the Sun and Aries through the elemental Magisterium, the character of Mars becomes an effect of the Solar order.
If Venus joins the Sun and a fuller explication of the Elements, its character designates a more extensive degree of magical explication.
If the planets refer to the Solar περιφορά and effect the work of Ἀναζωπυρήσεως, their series indicates a process of transformation rather than a catalogue of bodies.
Perfected magic of the Elements, conjoined with the lunar and solar, constitutes the condition under which conspicuous Mercury may appear.
Since the Mercury of the Philosophers is the Microcosm and Adam, its appearance signifies a transition to the constitution of the cosmic human being.
Since the separated soul can confer indissoluble bonds upon planetary bodies, planetary operation depends upon the mediation of the soul.
Since the Sun of the Philosophers can fill the third place, the planetary septenary is completed through the double ordering of Mercury and the Sun.
The correspondence of the Monad with the two Theorems makes the anatomy of its figure not an ornament, but an index of arcana.
Planetary signs are converted into a genealogical system, in which one character is produced from another through elemental and solar transformation.
Cosmology, alchemy, and anthropology coalesce in the same process, because Mercury is simultaneously a planet, an operative medium, the Microcosm, and Adam.
The separated soul becomes an ontological nexus between body, planets, and the alchemical work.
The septenary is constituted not by the enumeration of planets alone, but by degrees of transformation and substitution.
The anatomy of the Hieroglyphic Monad presents itself as an internal compendium of the cosmic order, not as an external description of the figure.
The system excludes the notion of planetary characters as arbitrary and mutually independent signs.
The system excludes a rigid separation between astronomy, alchemy, and anthropology.
The system excludes regeneration as a purely natural event without art, magic, and the mediation of the soul.
The system excludes the Microcosm as a passive image of the world; the Microcosm here is the effect of operative transformation.
The system excludes a univocal identity of the Sun and Mercury, because the place of each can vary according to the interpretive order.
The system excludes an operation wholly safe and immediate, since fiery and sulphurous vapours constitute a danger.
An interpretation that separates the symbol from the process of formation becomes impossible.
Knowledge that halts at the sight of the hieroglyphic surface and does not seek its operative correspondences becomes unavailable.
A world is precluded in which soul, elements, and planets are orders wholly heterogeneous.
The confinement of each sign within a fixed identity is forbidden, because characters are defined through circulation, composition, and substitution.
The absolute distinction between cosmic work and human work is absent: the same process passes from planets to soul and from figure to anatomy.

Two Theorems → signified arcana → correspondence with the anatomy of the Hieroglyphic Monad.

Planetary characters are reordered from separate signs into a genetic and transformative series.
Mercury is reclassified as a common node of cosmology, alchemy, and anthropology.
The separated soul becomes an operative object that can join planetary bodies, not merely a principle of knowledge.
The Sun and Mercury no longer constitute a simple opposition, but alternating places within the same septenary order.
The anatomy of the Monad becomes a compression map by which the planetary order and the arcana of the Theorems are read together.
The opposition between figure and operation collapses: the figure itself becomes a trace of the magical and cosmic process.
Surface: The characters of Mars, Venus, the Sun, Aries, the Moon, and Mercury are composed together as hieroglyphic figures.
Structural: The Elemental Magisterium, Solar περιφορά, and Ἀναζωπύρησις establish the order of composition and regeneration.
Metastrategic: The reading of signs is transformed into a restoration of the order by which the planets, the soul, and the anatomy of the Monad explicate the same machine.
Ontological/Temporal: Reality is presented as a process of degrees, substitutions, and transformations, in which the Microcosm emerges through perfected magic of the Elements.
The axioms suffice to restore the principal chain from the composition of characters to the correspondence of the Monad.
The system coheres internally while it treats planetary signs as stages of a single transformative process.
The relation between the two forms of Mercury, conspicuous Mercury and the Mercury of the Philosophers, is not wholly formally determined.
The substitution of the Sun for Mercury remains conditional, because the text attributes it to certain most expert persons and denies it to the author's age.
The status of the separated soul oscillates between instrument, operative principle, and ontological subject.

The force of the argument is strongest in the correspondence between the planetary order and the anatomy of the Monad; it is weaker in the proof of the correspondence itself, which depends chiefly on the assertion of an exact and open correspondence.
The reconstruction preserves the movement of the source, but does not remove its interrogative and conditional form.

The central question is on what the whole Magisterium depends and how its influence is constituted.
The text frames the question within a triadic structure of the Sun, Moon, and Lemnian Earth.
The principal assertion is that the Magisterium depends on the Sun and Moon, while Lemnian Earth provides its nourishment.
It establishes the authority of this structure through the testimony of Hermes and through the operation of Solar and Lunar rays.
The movement of the argument is: dependence → symbolic genealogy → terrestrial receptacle → radial influence.
This whole Magisterium depends on the Sun and Moon.
The Sun is the paternal principle of the Magisterium.
The Moon is the maternal principle of the Magisterium.
Lemnian Earth provides the place of nourishment for the Magisterium.
Lunar and Solar rays exert a singular Influence around Lemnian Earth.
Hermes confirms this genealogical relation by his authority.
The Magisterium is constituted not from one principle alone, but from the conjunction of celestial principles and a terrestrial receptacle.
The Magisterium is not an autonomous principle separated from the Sun and Moon.
Lemnian Earth is not the father or mother of the Magisterium, but the place of its nourishment.
The Sun and Moon are not reduced to mere static presence, because their rays exert Influence.
The Magisterium is not defined by celestial origin without terrestrial mediation.
Testimony concerning origin is not separated from the authority of Hermes.
The Magisterium is formed through the relation between celestial generation and terrestrial nourishment.
The Sun and Moon constitute active principles, whereas Lemnian Earth constitutes a receptive and nutritive condition.
The influential force of the Magisterium passes through rays, not through causality abstracted from the celestial bodies.
The triadic arrangement of father, mother, and earth establishes an order of generation, reception, and nourishment.
Hermetic confirmation transfers the celestial-terrestrial relation into a doctrinally legitimized order.
The Magisterium is the effect of a circulation between celestial sources and terrestrial matter, not a thing enclosed in one place.
The distinction between origin and nourishment separates two forms of causality: the celestial constitutes, the terrestrial sustains.
Rays constitute the medium through which the symbolic genealogy of the Sun and Moon is converted into physical or cosmological operation.
Hermetic authority and radial relation together cause the Magisterium to be understood as both a transmitted order and an operative influence.
The system tacitly excludes the notion of a Magisterium that could subsist without celestial influence or without a material foundation.
The system excludes univocal causality, whether solely celestial or solely terrestrial.
Paternity and maternity here designate not human persons, but distinct functions within cosmological generation.
Lemnian Earth is not passive matter wholly separated from influence, but a condition without which the nourishment of the Magisterium cannot be explained.
Ancient authority alone would not suffice to constitute the system unless radial influence added a mechanism to it.
The text avoids the conception of the Magisterium as the contrivance of an autonomous human being, because it locates its origin outside human action.
The possibility that heaven and earth are merely metaphorical images without influential efficacy is foreclosed.
The absolute separation between symbolic genealogy and natural operation is foreclosed.
The system renders unavailable a single and simple origin: the Magisterium cannot be derived solely from the Sun, solely from the Moon, or solely from the Earth.
Sun + Moon → paternal and maternal principles → constitutive dependence of the Magisterium.
Lemnian Earth → reception and nourishment → terrestrial continuation of that which is constituted celestially.
Lunar rays + Solar rays → singular influence around Lemnian Earth → conjoint operation of the Magisterium.
Hermetic testimony + order of influence → genealogical and cosmological legitimation.
Celestial and terrestrial conjunction → the Magisterium as a dependent, nourished, and influential process.
Dependence of the Magisterium → constitution of the Sun and Moon as parents → Lemnian Earth as nourishment → rays as the medium of influence → operative unity of the three terms.
The origin of the Magisterium is reclassified from a singular source to a relation between two celestial principles and one terrestrial place.
Lemnian Earth becomes not a material end, but a receptive node where the influences of the Sun and Moon operate.
Paternity, maternity, and nourishment are ordered as distinct causal functions, not as merely poetic terms.
Rays are reordered as the common medium through which the Hermetic symbol passes into a mechanism of influence.
The heaven/earth opposition is dissolved into a schema of circulation: heaven influences; earth receives and nourishes.
Surface — The Magisterium is asserted to depend on the Sun, Moon, and Lemnian Earth.
Structural — The system distributes functions among celestial generative principles, a terrestrial receptacle, and mediating rays.
Metastrategic — Hermetic authority and radial influence are conjoined so that symbolic genealogy acquires doctrinal and operative force.

Ontological/Temporal — The reality of the Magisterium is a process of generation, reception, and nourishment under the influence of celestial bodies; it is neither an immobile substance nor an origin simply local.
The axioms suffice to reconstruct the minimal mechanism: two celestial principles, one terrestrial receptacle, radial influence, and Hermetic confirmation.
The text is internally coherent with respect to the order of father, mother, nourishment, and influence.
The greatest firmness lies in the triadic structure and in the opposition between celestial origin and terrestrial nourishment.
Determination remains incomplete concerning the exact sense of the Magisterium, Lemnian Earth, and singular Influence.
The fragile juncture is the transition from Hermetic testimony to radial efficacy: authority confirms the relation, but does not explain its mechanism.
The reconstruction preserves the true movement of the text, although the causality of the rays and the ontological status of Lemnian Earth can no longer be further demonstrated in the source.
