Structural — Figura per situm, numerum, litteram et divisionem in elementa significationes successive generat.
Metastrategic — Interpretatio ab una lectione ad plures rationes productionis movetur, ita ut compendium numericum ad lectionem verbalem transitus fiat.
Ontological/Temporal — Verbum, Lux et Unitas non tamquam data immediata quam tamquam terminus compositionis, conspirationis et consensus producuntur.
Axiomata de quattuor angulis, significatione quinariali et conversione hieroglyphica sufficiunt ad primam machinam derivationis restituendam.
Axiomata de denario, littera vicesima prima et potestate generali sufficiunt ad multiplicem identitatem crucis explicandam.
Axiomata compositionis numericae sufficiunt ad 252 producendum, sed duas alias rationes a textu promissas non determinant.
Transitus a divisione in duas litteras ad Lux et Verbum formaliter minus explicitus manet quam transitus numericus.
Systema interne cohaeret quatenus omnes gradus ad conversionem unius signi referuntur.
Firmissimum est in compositione numerorum et in pluralitate notarum; fragilius est in identitate litterarum et in necessitate conclusionis verbalium.
Restitutio servat motum verum: figura → numerus → nota → littera → Lux → Verbum, quamquam clausura magistralis innititur praemissis non plene explicatis.
From the Sixth Theorem, the cross is constituted as a figure of four right angles, to each of which a quinary signification can be attributed.
The same structure of quinquagenary, denary, alphabetic, and unitary numbers can be converted into hieroglyphic signs.
Through these conversions, the cross can simultaneously signify number, letter, and a sign of any power.
From the composition of these significations, the number 252 is elicited, which the cross can signify compendiously to the initiated.
The cross, distributed into two letters and compared with their verbal force, brings it about that Light and the final and masterful Word are understood.
Our cross contains four right angles.
A quinary signification can be attributed to each angle.
The position of the angles can determine their signification.
The same rationale of the theorem permits quinquagenary numbers to be converted into hieroglyphic signs.
The cross can commonly denote the denary.
The cross, according to the order of the Latin alphabet, can signify the twenty-first letter.
One sign can have any and however great power.
Four fives, four fifties, ten, twenty-one, and one can be composed into one number.
The number thus composed is 252.
The cross can be distributed into two other letters.
The numerical force of letters and their verbal force can be assessed separately.
The conspiring and agreement of the ternary in the unity of the Word can lead to a masterful signification.
The cross is not restricted to only one numerical signification.
The signification of the cross is not defined by one disposition of the angles alone.
The cross is not merely a geometric figure, because it can also signify number, letter, and sign.
A sign is not limited to one power or to one quantity.
The number 252 is not the sole way by which the signification of the cross is constituted, because two other omitted methods are mentioned.
The final Word is not reduced to numerical force alone, but arises from numerical and verbal force together.
The four angles of the cross, each endowed with quinary signification, produce a series of numerical compositions.
By the same operation, the cross can signify the denary, the twenty-first letter, and general power.
The composition of four fives, four fifties, the denary, twenty-one, and unity produces 252.
The number 252 becomes a compendium in which several orders of the signification of the cross are simultaneously preserved.
The division of the cross into two letters transfers the analysis from the whole figure to the elements constituting the word.
The comparison of the numerical and verbal forces of letters produces the signification of light.
Light, joined with the unity of the Word and the agreement of the ternary, brings about the final and masterful Word.
The cross becomes a machine of translation among geometry, arithmetic, alphabet, word, and hieroglyphic theology.
The identity of the sign is constituted not by one code, but by the superposition of several interpretative orders.
The number 252 does not close interpretation, but opens it to further productions and to masterful reading.
The unity of the Word is generated from the coordination of diverse powers, not from the simple identity of one element.
Hieroglyphic cognition passes from the calculation of the sign to the ontological-verbal production of Light and Word.
An isolated geometric figure is not sufficient to explain the meaning of the cross.
The sign does not possess a proper univocal force that exhausts all its significations.
Numerical reduction cannot abolish the verbal and masterful path.
A letter separated from its numerical force does not retain the fullness of its signification.
Interpretation cannot stop at the first derivation if the same figure admits several modes of production.
The closure of the sign within one genus, whether geometric, numerical, or alphabetic, is held to be impossible.
The opposition between material figure and Word is precluded, because the figure itself can be transfigured into the Word.
There is absent an idea of signification obtained without conversion, composition, and agreement.
An explanation that separates the unity of the Word from the plurality of forms remains inaccessible.
Figure of the cross → four right angles → distribution of quinary significations.
Significations of the angles → series of numbers and signs → hieroglyphic translation.
Cross → denary + twenty-first letter + general sign → multiplicity of powers of signifying.
Four fives + four fifties + ten + twenty-one + one → 252 → cabalistic compendium.
Whole cross → division into two letters → numerical and verbal comparison.
Comparison of letters → Light → final and masterful Word → unity through ternary, conspiring, and agreement.
The preceding theorem concerning angles and quinary signification → the cross is constituted as four-angled.
Four-angled cross → quinquagenary numbers and hieroglyphic signs are derived.
Hieroglyphic sign → the denary, the twenty-first letter, and general power coalesce.
Numerical compositions → 252 is produced as a masterful compendium.
Numerical compendium → division into two letters → numerical and verbal force.
Force of letters → Light → final and masterful Word in the unity of the ternary.
From a figure to be contemplated, the cross becomes a nexus among four orders: space, number, alphabet, and word.
Number and letter no longer act as separate systems, but as conversions of the same sign.
The multiplicity of significations is not confused with error, but is ordered through hieroglyphic composition.
The number 252 transfers the center of gravity from one utterance to a structure of production that admits several paths.
The division of the cross into letters reclassifies meaning as a process proceeding from numerical power to verbal light.
The final Word appears as an effect of coordination, not as the immediate beginning of interpretation.
Surface — The cross contains four right angles and admits various numerical and alphabetic notations.
Structural — Through position, number, letter, and division into elements, the figure successively generates significations.
Metastrategic — Interpretation moves from one reading to several modes of production, so that the numerical compendium becomes a transition to verbal reading.
Ontological/Temporal — Word, Light, and Unity are produced not as immediate givens so much as as the terminus of composition, conspiring, and agreement.
The axioms concerning four angles, quinary signification, and hieroglyphic conversion suffice to reconstruct the first machine of derivation.
The axioms concerning the denary, the twenty-first letter, and general power suffice to explain the multiple identity of the cross.
The axioms of numerical composition suffice to produce 252, but do not determine the two other methods promised by the text.
The transition from division into two letters to Light and Word remains formally less explicit than the numerical transition.
The system coheres internally insofar as all stages are referred to the conversion of one sign.
It is strongest in the composition of numbers and in the plurality of signs; it is more fragile in the identity of letters and in the necessity of the verbal conclusion.
The reconstruction preserves the true movement: figure → number → sign → letter → Light → Word, although the masterful closure rests on premises not fully explained.
Textus quaerit quomodo caelestis astronomia structuram et anatomiam Monadis in natura manifestet.
Quaestio a descriptione corporum caelestium ad interpretationem hieroglyphicam relationis inter caelum, naturam et artem transfertur.
Ex Theorematibus XII et XIII caelestis astronomia inferioris quasi Parens et Magistra constituitur.
Contemplatio caelestium motuum et figurae ovalis praebet formam qua proportio naturalis et anatomia ovi legi possunt.
Haec structura ab ovo aquilino et conflictu Scarabei cum Aquila ad operationem artificialem et metamorphosin ovi derivatur.
Argumentatio est hieroglyphice analogica, reconstructiva et polemica: fabula naturae in schema physicum, alchymicum et medicinale convertitur.
Theoremata XII et XIII caelestem Astronomiam quasi Parentem et Magistram inferioris constituunt.
Oculi Cabalistici, praedictorum mysteriorum theorica illuminati, anatomiam Monadis in lumine Naturae et Vitae percipere possunt.
Contemplatio caelestium nunciorum et gestuum doctrinam de forma et ordine caelesti praebet.
Cursus corporis caelestis figuram ovalem et circuitionem repraesentat.
Interpretationes hieroglyphicae consilium caeleste cum praedictis theorematibus consentaneum reddunt.
Natura proportiones ordinatas continet quae fere totum ordinem rei naturalis comprehendunt.
In ovo albumen aquae, vitellus olei et calx ovi correspondent.
Aquila hominibus timidis et brutis violentiam infert, qua iniuria vindictam Scarabei motivat.
Scarabeus per vim et subtilissimam artem ovum aquilinum in terram praecipitat atque disrumpit.
Iupiter, malum tantum praecavens, impedit ne Scarabeus totam Aquilinam speciem e terris deleat.
Textus Heliocantharos certis temporum curriculis latitantes ponit, quorum indicia contra inimicum adhiberi possunt.
Quidam, quos auctor se nosse dicit, ovum aquilinum dissolutum calce et albumine temperant, deinde temperamento liquorem vitelli ordine artificioso superinducunt.
Volutatio et revolutio artificiosa, ad modum Scarabei pilas conglomerantis, metamorphosin ovi producunt.
In metamorphosi albumen evanescit et in ipso vitellinoso liquore absorbetur.
Tale artificium a gravissimis et antiquissimis philosophis celebratum atque certissimum et utilissimum traditur.
Anaxagoras ex hoc magisterio medicinam excellentissimam fecisse affirmatur.
Nihil horum extra virtutem hieroglyphicam Monadis ponitur.
Anatomia Monadis non per simplicem visum, sed per oculos Cabalisticos et theorica mysteriorum illuminatos apprehenditur.
Textus se non Aesopum, sed Oedipum agere declarat.
Fabulari superficialiter de summis Naturae mysteriis non sufficit ad eorum intellectum.
Confugium ad antrum Scarabei auxilium petentibus liberationem non praestat.
Vindicta Scarabei non ad solam vim brutam reducitur, sed subtili arte efficitur.
Metamorphosis artificialis non per mixtionem indeterminatam, sed per temperationem et ordinem operationum procedit.
Virtus hieroglyphica Monadis extra hunc ordinem caelestem, naturalem et artificialem non extenditur.
Motus caelestis formam formalem praebet qua processus physicus describi potest.
Circulatio ovalis a figura astronomica in principium coordinationis naturae et operationis artificialis convertitur.
Ovum constituitur microstructura proportionata cuius partes materiales significationes hieroglyphicas suscipiunt.
Certamen inter Scarabeum et Aquilam in processum materialem iniuriae, disruptionis et restitutionis transponitur.
Tempus, latitatio et indicia animalium antagonisticorum in cognitionem strategicam convertuntur.
Operatio artificialis motum Scarabei imitatur, ita ut volutatio ipsa fiat instrumentum metamorphoseos.
Disruptio ovi non in annihilatione terminatur, sed in transpositione albuminis ad liquorem vitellinum.
Praecedens philosophicum et medicinale operationem alchymicam intra ordinem scientiae legitimat, quamvis textus hanc auctoritate tradita affirmet.
Signum hieroglyphicum fit mediatio unica inter ordinem caelestem, anatomiam naturalem et artem operativam.
Natura et ars non constituunt ordines oppositos, quia ars motus et proportionem naturae imitari potest.
Fabula animalium, processus physicus et operatio alchymica sunt tres gradus eiusdem structurae hieroglyphicae.
Destructio in hoc systemate formam mutationis habet, quia dissolutio materiam in novum ordinem disponit.
Cognitio non consistit in observatione separata, sed in interpretatione signorum, motuum et temporum.
Monas totalizat astronomiam, physicam, mythum, alchymiam et medicinam sub una virtute hieroglyphica.
Systema excludit separationem absolutam inter caelum et naturam inferiorem.
Systema excludit naturam quae formis, proportionibus et signis non iam ordinetur.
Systema excludit mythum qui ad fabulam moralem vel ad narrationem sine physico mysterio reducatur.
Systema excludit oppositionem simplicem inter artificium et Naturam.
Systema excludit destructionem tamquam terminum ultimum, quia disruptio ad metamorphosin transit.
Systema excludit cognitionem quae a signis, motibus et temporalibus circulis seiungi possit.
Systema excludit materiam isolatam, cuius partes sine proportione et correspondence inter se intelligantur.
Textus praecludit possibilitatem ordinis naturalis qui extra analogiam caelestem et hieroglyphicam maneat.
Textus circumit possibilitatem sermonis neutri qui naturam sine figura, signo aut interpretatione describat.
Textus praecludit eventum naturalem omnino fortuitum et significatione carentem.
Textus praecludit abolitionem totalem ordinis aquilini, quia interventus Iovis extinctionem universalem impedit.
Textus praecludit aliquod magisterium alchymicum quod extra virtutem hieroglyphicam Monadis subsistat.
Theoremata XII et XIII → Astronomia caelestis ut Parens et Magistra → oculi Cabalistici → anatomia Monadis in Natura et Vita.
Contemplatio nunciorum et gestuum caelestium → cursus ovalis → figura circuitionis → concordantia interpretationum hieroglyphicarum.
Proportio a Natura → ovum ut microstructura → albumen/aqua, vitellus/oleum, calx → materia apta ad hieroglyphicam translationem.
Iniuria Aquilae → vindicta Scarabei → praecipitatio ovi → disruptio → imminens deletio speciei.
Interventus Iovis → conservatio limitata Aquilae → cura ovorum certis anni temporibus → indicia Heliocantharorum → possibilitas responsionis.
Ovum dissolutum + calx + albumen → temperatio → liquor vitelli → oblitio ordinata → volutatio et revolutio → metamorphosis ovi.
Metamorphosis → transitus albuminis in liquorem vitellinum → signum hieroglyphicum Naturae → auctoritas philosophica et medicina → clausura in virtute Monadis.

Theoremata XII–XIII → Astronomia ut Parens et Magistra → visus Cabalisticus → motus ovalis → concordantia hieroglyphica → proportio Naturae → anatomia ovi → antagonismus Aquilae et Scarabei → metamorphosis artificialis → inclusio in virtute Monadis.
Caelum ↔ figura → figura ↔ natura → natura ↔ fabula animalis → fabula ↔ operatio alchymica → operatio ↔ medicina philosophica.
Argumentatio caelum, naturam et artem in unam tabulam continuorum ordinum reponit.
Ovum, motus ovalis, Scarabeus et Aquila non amplius ut res separatae, sed ut variantes eiusdem formae proportionatae classificari possunt.
Oppositio inter naturale et artificiale corruit, quia artificium motum naturalem repetendo metamorphosin producit.
Oppositio inter destructionem et generationem denuo classificatur: disruptio fit conditio mutationis materiae.
Tempus et signa animalium ex circumstantia narrativa in instrumenta cognitionis et responsionis convertuntur.
Monas fit tabula totalizans in qua astronomia, physica, mythus, alchymia et medicina eadem structura hieroglyphica participant.
Figurae adiunctae motum caelestem per formam ovalem et dispositiones circulares ostendunt, quamvis singulae correspondentiae signorum non plene glossentur.
**Surface:** Textus ovum aquilinum, Scarabeum, Aquilam, Iovem et operationem temperationis proponit ut obiecta immediata significationis.
**Structural:** Haec obiecta in ordinem proportionis, circuitionis, compositionis et dissolutionis materialis ordinantur.
**Metastrategic:** Interpretatio hieroglyphica certamen inter adversarios et cognitionem alchymicam denuo constituit, ita ut indicia et motus ad responsionem adhiberi possint.
**Ontological/Temporal:** Caelum, natura, ars et mythus unum continuum realitatis formant, cuius motus per circulos, tempora et metamorphoses ordinantur.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad motum principalem a theorematibus caelestibus ad anatomiam ovi et metamorphosin artificialem restituendum.
Cohaerentia firmissima est ubi circulatio caelestis, volutatio Scarabei et revolutio artificialis eandem formam motus repetunt.
Transitus a Theorematibus XII et XIII ad compositionem ovi nititur potius concordantia hieroglyphica quam demonstratione formali.
Correspondentiae inter albumen, vitellum, calcem, caelestes figuras et virtutem Monadis non omnibus gradibus explicite determinantur.
Textus inter historiam animalium, fabulam hieroglyphicam et instructionem alchymicam transit, sed regulas translationis inter hos gradus non plene formalizat.
Interventus Iovis limitat potentiam totalizantem Scarabei et in systemate tensionem inter vindictam, conservationem et deletionem relinquit.
Auctoritas Anaxagorae et philosophorum antiquorum operationem confirmat testimonialiter, non per probationem internam eius efficaciae.
Restitutio servat verum motum textus, sed exacta relatio inter signa figurarum adiunctarum et omnia elementa doctrinalia ex sola expositione non prorsus determinatur.
The text asks how celestial astronomy manifests the structure and anatomy of the Monad in nature.
The question is transferred from the description of celestial bodies to the hieroglyphic interpretation of the relation among heaven, nature, and art.
From Theorems XII and XIII, celestial astronomy is established as the Parent and Mistress, as it were, of the lower realm.
Contemplation of celestial motions and of the oval figure provides the form by which natural proportion and the anatomy of the egg can be read.
This structure is derived from the eagle's egg and from the conflict of Scarabeus with Aquila to artificial operation and the metamorphosis of the egg.
The argumentation is hieroglyphically analogical, reconstructive, and polemical: the fable of nature is converted into a physical, alchemical, and medical schema.
Theorems XII and XIII establish celestial Astronomy as the Parent and Mistress, as it were, of the lower realm.
Cabalistic eyes, illuminated by the theory of the aforesaid mysteries, can perceive the anatomy of the Monad in the light of Nature and Life.
Contemplation of celestial messengers and gestures provides doctrine concerning celestial form and order.
The course of a celestial body represents an oval figure and circulation.
Hieroglyphic interpretations render the celestial design consonant with the aforesaid theorems.
Nature contains ordered proportions which encompass almost the whole order of the natural thing.
In the egg, albumen, yolk, and eggshell correspond respectively to water, oil, and lime.
Aquila inflicts violence upon timid and brutish human beings, by which injury the vengeance of Scarabeus is motivated.
By force and most subtle art, Scarabeus casts the eagle's egg to the ground and breaks it apart.
Iupiter, guarding against so great an evil, prevents Scarabeus from destroying the entire Aquiline species from the earth.
The text places Heliocanthari in hiding during certain courses of time, whose signs may be employed against the enemy.
Certain persons, whom the author says he knows, temper a dissolved eagle's egg with lime and albumen, then by tempering lay the liquid of the yolk over it in an artificial order.
Artificial rolling and revolving, after the manner of Scarabeus conglomerating balls, produce the metamorphosis of the egg.
In the metamorphosis, the albumen vanishes and is absorbed into the very yolk-liquid.
Such an artifice is celebrated by the most weighty and most ancient philosophers and is handed down as most certain and most useful.
Anaxagoras is affirmed to have made an exceptionally excellent medicine from this teaching.
None of these things is placed outside the hieroglyphic virtue of the Monad.
The anatomy of the Monad is apprehended not through simple sight, but through Cabalistic eyes illuminated by the theory of the mysteries.
The text declares that it plays not Aesop, but Oedipus.
To speak fabulously in a superficial manner about the highest mysteries of Nature does not suffice for their understanding.
Flight to the cave of Scarabeus does not provide liberation to those seeking aid.
The vengeance of Scarabeus is not reduced to brute force alone, but is effected by subtle art.
Artificial metamorphosis proceeds not through indeterminate mixture, but through tempering and the order of operations.
The hieroglyphic virtue of the Monad does not extend outside this celestial, natural, and artificial order.
Celestial motion provides a formal form by which a physical process can be described.
Oval circulation is converted from an astronomical figure into a principle of coordinating nature and artificial operation.
The egg consists as a proportioned microstructure whose material parts assume hieroglyphic significations.
The contest between Scarabeus and Aquila is transposed into a material process of injury, disruption, and restoration.
Time, concealment, and the signs of antagonistic animals are converted into strategic knowledge.
Artificial operation imitates the motion of Scarabeus, such that rolling itself becomes an instrument of metamorphosis.
The disruption of the egg ends not in annihilation, but in the transposition of albumen into yolk-liquid.
Philosophical and medical precedent legitimates the alchemical operation within the order of knowledge, although the text affirms this by received authority.
The hieroglyphic sign becomes the sole mediation between celestial order, natural anatomy, and operative art.
Nature and art do not constitute opposed orders, because art can imitate the motion and proportion of nature.
The fable of animals, the physical process, and the alchemical operation are three levels of the same hieroglyphic structure.
Destruction in this system has the form of change, because dissolution disposes matter into a new order.
Knowledge consists not in separate observation, but in the interpretation of signs, motions, and times.
The Monad totalizes astronomy, physics, myth, alchemy, and medicine under one hieroglyphic virtue.
The system excludes an absolute separation between heaven and lower nature.
The system excludes a nature no longer ordered by forms, proportions, and signs.
The system excludes a myth reduced to a moral fable or to a narrative without physical mystery.
The system excludes a simple opposition between artifice and Nature.
The system excludes destruction as an ultimate end, because disruption passes into metamorphosis.
The system excludes knowledge that could be separated from signs, motions, and temporal cycles.
The system excludes isolated matter, whose parts are understood without proportion and correspondence among themselves.
The text forecloses the possibility of a natural order that remains outside celestial and hieroglyphic analogy.
The text circumvents the possibility of a neutral discourse that describes nature without figure, sign, or interpretation.
The text forecloses a natural event wholly accidental and lacking signification.
The text forecloses the total abolition of the Aquiline order, because the intervention of Iupiter prevents universal extinction.
The text forecloses any alchemical teaching that subsists outside the hieroglyphic virtue of the Monad.
Theorems XII and XIII → celestial Astronomy as Parent and Mistress → Cabalistic eyes → anatomy of the Monad in Nature and Life.
Contemplation of celestial messengers and gestures → oval course → figure of circulation → concordance of hieroglyphic interpretations.
Proportion from Nature → egg as microstructure → albumen/water, yolk/oil, lime → matter suited to hieroglyphic translation.
Injury by Aquila → vengeance of Scarabeus → casting down of the egg → disruption → impending destruction of the species.
Intervention of Iupiter → limited preservation of Aquila → care for eggs at certain times of the year → signs of Heliocanthari → possibility of response.
Dissolved egg + lime + albumen → tempering → liquid of yolk → ordered coating → rolling and revolving → metamorphosis of the egg.
Metamorphosis → passage of albumen into yolk-liquid → hieroglyphic sign of Nature → philosophical authority and medicine → closure in the virtue of the Monad.

Theorems XII–XIII → Astronomy as Parent and Mistress → Cabalistic vision → oval motion → hieroglyphic concordance → proportion of Nature → anatomy of the egg → antagonism of Aquila and Scarabeus → artificial metamorphosis → inclusion in the virtue of the Monad.
Heaven ↔ figure → figure ↔ nature → nature ↔ animal fable → fable ↔ alchemical operation → operation ↔ philosophical medicine.
The argumentation places heaven, nature, and art upon a single map of continuous orders.
The egg, oval motion, Scarabeus, and Aquila can no longer be classified as separate things, but as variants of the same proportioned form.
The opposition between the natural and the artificial collapses, because artifice produces metamorphosis by repeating natural motion.
The opposition between destruction and generation is reclassified: disruption becomes the condition of the change of matter.
Time and animal signs are converted from narrative circumstance into instruments of knowledge and response.
The Monad becomes a totalizing map in which astronomy, physics, myth, alchemy, and medicine participate in the same hieroglyphic structure.
The accompanying figures display celestial motion through the oval form and circular dispositions, although the individual correspondences of the signs are not fully glossed.
**Surface:** The text presents the eagle's egg, Scarabeus, Aquila, Iupiter, and the operation of tempering as immediate objects of signification.
**Structural:** These objects are ordered into an order of proportion, circulation, composition, and material dissolution.
**Metastrategic:** Hieroglyphic interpretation reconstitutes the contest between adversaries and alchemical knowledge, such that signs and motions can be employed for response.
**Ontological/Temporal:** Heaven, nature, art, and myth form one continuum of reality, whose motions are ordered through cycles, times, and metamorphoses.
The axioms suffice to reconstruct the principal movement from the celestial theorems to the anatomy of the egg and artificial metamorphosis.
The strongest coherence is where celestial circulation, the rolling of Scarabeus, and artificial revolution repeat the same form of motion.
The transition from Theorems XII and XIII to the composition of the egg rests more upon hieroglyphic concordance than upon formal demonstration.
The correspondences among albumen, yolk, lime, celestial figures, and the virtue of the Monad are not explicitly determined at every level.
The text passes among animal history, hieroglyphic fable, and alchemical instruction, but does not fully formalize the rules of translation among these levels.
The intervention of Iupiter limits the totalizing power of Scarabeus and leaves in the system a tension among vengeance, preservation, and destruction.
The authority of Anaxagoras and of ancient philosophers confirms the operation testimonialy, not through internal proof of its efficacy.

The reconstruction preserves the true movement of the text, but the exact relation between the signs of the accompanying figures and all doctrinal elements is not wholly determined from the exposition alone.

units.title: T H E Ò R. X I X.

items.text: Quaestio est quomodo corpora Elementata inferiora vires suas corporales accipiant.
Nova quaestionis constitutio ponit Solem et Lunam, non cetera Planeta, principales influxus corporales esse.
Fundamentum est quod *Omnium rerum Corporatarum Analysis Pyronomica* hanc differentiam effectu demonstrat.
Probatio distribuit influxum Lunae in Humorem Aqueum et influxum Solis in Liquorem Igneum.
Motus argumentationis procedit ab inaequali vi caelesti ad constitutionem corporeitatis terrestris mortalium.
Sol et Luna omnibus ceteris Planetis fortiores sunt in inferiora Elementata Corpora.
Corpora caelestia suas vires corporales in corpora inferiora infundunt.
*Analysis Pyronomica* effectibus rerum corporatarum influxus corporales demonstrat.
Luna Humorem Aqueum refundit.
Sol Liquorem Igneum refundit.
Humore Aqueo et Liquore Igneo sustentatur corporeitas terrestris rerum mortalium.
Effectus caelestes in corporibus inferioribus per formas materiales determinatas manifestantur.
Corporeitas rerum mortalium terrestrium a coniunctione influxuum solaris et lunaris dependet.
Influxus corporalis Solis et Lunae non aequalis influxui omnium ceterorum Planetarum ponitur.
Corpora inferiora non tamquam a seipsis sufficientia describuntur.
Humores et liquores terrestres non sine origine caelesti explicantur.
*Analysis Pyronomica* non mera descriptio corporum, sed demonstratio effectuum corporalis habetur.
Sustentatio rerum mortalium non ad unam causam caelestem reducitur.
Sol et Luna structuram materialem corporum inferiorum causaliter participant.
Lunae influxus ad dimensionem aqueam corporeitatis refertur.
Solis influxus ad dimensionem igneam corporeitatis refertur.
Corporeitas terrestris ex differentiata distributione elementorum materialium constituitur.
Mortalia corpora sunt effectus sustentati, non simpliciter data, influxuum caelestium.
Ordo corporeus terrestris in hierarchia caelesti fundatur, quia vis corporalis superiorum corporum conditionem inferiorum determinat.
Distinctio Solis et Lunae efficit ut generatio corporeitatis non una sed bipolaris intelligatur.
*Analysis Pyronomica* fit nexus inter observationem effectuum et hypothesim cosmologicam de causis materialibus.
Corpora mortalia ontologice dependent ab circulatione virium inter corpora caelestia et elementa inferiora.
Falsum esse debet corpora terrestria clausam et autonomam materiam constituere.
Falsum esse debet influxum caelestem ad metaphoram vel significationem non-materialem reduci.
Falsum esse debet omnes Planetas eandem vim in corpora inferiora exercere.
Falsum esse debet corporeitatem mortalium explicari posse sine relatione inter Humorem Aqueum et Liquorem Igneum.
Falsum esse debet effectus corporales a principiis cosmologicis separari posse.
Textus excludit mundum materialem sine mediatione caelesti sufficienter intelligibilem.
Textus praecludit aequalitatem causalem inter corpora caelestia.
Textus circumit sed non explicite resolvit quomodo influxus caelestes in substantiam terrestrem transmutentur.
Textus inadmissibilem reddit notionem vitae mortalis a sustentatione cosmica abstractae.
Inaequalitas virium caelestium → praecipua potestas Solis et Lunae → influxus corporalis in Elementata Corpora.
Influxus Lunae → Humoris Aquei refunditio; influxus Solis → Liquoris Ignei refunditio.
Humor Aqueus + Liquor Igneus → sustentatio Corpulentiae Terrestris → conservatio rerum mortalium.
Effectus corporales observati → Analysis Pyronomica → confirmatio ordinis causalitatis caelestis.

Corporum mortalium sustentatio → investigatio causarum materialium → comparatio virium Planetarum → privilegium Solis et Lunae → distinctio influxuum aquei et ignei → constitutio corporeitatis terrestris.
Corpora inferiora ex obiectis passivis in nodos relationis inter influxus caelestes et materias elementares reclassificantur.
Sol et Luna ex corporibus caelestibus inter alia enumeratis in fontes materiales distinctos elevantur.
Oppositio inter causam caelestem et materiam terrestrem dissolvitur, quia corporeitas terrestris per influxum caelestem describitur.
Humidum et igneum fiunt principia coordinata, quibus ager corporeitatis mortalium ordinatur.
Surface — Sol et Luna vires corporales in corpora inferiora infundunt; Luna Humorem Aqueum, Sol Liquorem Igneum refundit.
Structural — Corporeitas terrestris ex influxuum caelestium distributione materiali sustentatur.
Metastrategic — Effectus observabiles per *Analysim Pyronomicam* convertuntur in probationem ordinis causalitatis cosmici.
Ontological/Temporal — Res mortales dependent ab continuo nexu inter corpora caelestia, elementa inferiora et sustentationem corporeitatis.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam catenam a superioritate Solis et Lunae ad sustentationem corporeitatis terrestris.
Distinctio inter influxum Lunae aqueum et influxum Solis igneum est necessaria ad structuram argumenti.
Mechanismus quo Humor Aqueus et Liquor Igneus corporeitatem sustentant nondum satis determinatur.
Vis argumenti firmissima est in distributione bipartita influxuum et in conversione effectus in probationem.
Systema nititur praesuppositione quod *Analysis Pyronomica* revera influxus caelestes demonstrat, quamquam modus demonstrationis hic non explicatur.
Restitutio servat motum fontis: effectus corporales → demonstratio pyronomica → privilegium Solis et Lunae → formas materiales → corporeitas terrestris.

translations.title: T H E O R. X I X.

items.text: The question is how lower Elementated bodies receive their corporeal powers.
The new formulation of the question posits that the Sun and Moon, not the other Planets, are the principal corporeal influences.
The foundation is that the *Pyronomic Analysis of All Corporeal Things* demonstrates this difference by effect.
The proof distributes the Moon's influence into Aqueous Moisture and the Sun's influence into Fiery Liquid.
The movement of the argument proceeds from unequal celestial power to the constitution of the terrestrial corporeity of mortal things.
The Sun and Moon are stronger than all the other Planets upon lower Elementated Bodies.
Celestial bodies pour their corporeal powers into lower bodies.
*Pyronomic Analysis* demonstrates corporeal influences through the effects of corporeal things.
The Moon pours forth Aqueous Moisture.
The Sun pours forth Fiery Liquid.
The terrestrial corporeity of mortal things is sustained by Aqueous Moisture and Fiery Liquid.
Celestial effects are manifested in lower bodies through determinate material forms.
The corporeity of terrestrial mortal things depends upon the conjunction of solar and lunar influences.
The corporeal influence of the Sun and Moon is not posited as equal to the influence of all the other Planets.
Lower bodies are not described as self-sufficient in themselves.
Terrestrial moistures and liquids are not explained without a celestial origin.
*Pyronomic Analysis* is regarded not as a mere description of bodies, but as a demonstration of corporeal effects.
The sustenance of mortal things is not reduced to one celestial cause.
The Sun and Moon causally participate in the material structure of lower bodies.
The Moon's influence is referred to the aqueous dimension of corporeity.
The Sun's influence is referred to the fiery dimension of corporeity.
Terrestrial corporeity is constituted from the differentiated distribution of material elements.
Mortal bodies are sustained effects, not simply given, of celestial influences.
The terrestrial corporeal order is founded in a celestial hierarchy, because the corporeal power of higher bodies determines the condition of lower ones.
The distinction of Sun and Moon causes the generation of corporeity to be understood as not one but bipolar.
*Pyronomic Analysis* becomes the nexus between the observation of effects and the cosmological hypothesis concerning material causes.
Mortal bodies depend ontologically on the circulation of powers between celestial bodies and lower elements.
It must be false that terrestrial bodies constitute closed and autonomous matter.
It must be false that celestial influence is reduced to metaphor or non-material signification.
It must be false that all Planets exert the same power upon lower bodies.
It must be false that the corporeity of mortals can be explained without a relation between Aqueous Moisture and Fiery Liquid.
It must be false that corporeal effects can be separated from cosmological principles.
The text excludes a material world sufficiently intelligible without celestial mediation.
The text precludes causal equality among celestial bodies.
The text skirts but does not explicitly resolve how celestial influences are transformed into terrestrial substance.
The text renders inadmissible the notion of mortal life abstracted from cosmic sustenance.
Inequality of celestial powers → preeminent power of the Sun and Moon → corporeal influence into Elementated Bodies.
Influence of the Moon → pouring forth of Aqueous Moisture; influence of the Sun → pouring forth of Fiery Liquid.
Aqueous Moisture + Fiery Liquid → sustenance of Terrestrial Corporeity → preservation of mortal things.
Observed corporeal effects → Pyronomic Analysis → confirmation of the order of celestial causality.

Sustenance of mortal bodies → investigation of material causes → comparison of the powers of the Planets → privilege of the Sun and Moon → distinction of aqueous and fiery influences → constitution of terrestrial corporeity.
Lower bodies are reclassified from passive objects into nodes of relation between celestial influences and elemental materials.
The Sun and Moon are elevated from celestial bodies enumerated among others into distinct material sources.
The opposition between celestial cause and terrestrial matter is dissolved, because terrestrial corporeity is described through celestial influence.
The moist and the fiery become coordinated principles by which the field of mortal corporeity is ordered.
Surface — The Sun and Moon pour corporeal powers into lower bodies; the Moon pours forth Aqueous Moisture, the Sun Fiery Liquid.
Structural — Terrestrial corporeity is sustained by the material distribution of celestial influences.
Metastrategic — Observable effects are converted through *Pyronomic Analysis* into proof of the order of cosmic causality.
Ontological/Temporal — Mortal things depend upon a continuous nexus between celestial bodies, lower elements, and the sustenance of corporeity.
The axioms suffice to restore the chain from the superiority of the Sun and Moon to the sustenance of terrestrial corporeity.
The distinction between the Moon's aqueous influence and the Sun's fiery influence is necessary to the structure of the argument.
The mechanism by which Aqueous Moisture and Fiery Liquid sustain corporeity is not yet sufficiently determined.
The argument's greatest force lies in the bipartite distribution of influences and in the conversion of effect into proof.
The system relies upon the presupposition that *Pyronomic Analysis* truly demonstrates celestial influences, although the mode of demonstration is not explained here.
The reconstruction preserves the movement of the source: corporeal effects → pyronomic demonstration → privilege of the Sun and Moon → material forms → terrestrial corporeity.

units.title: T H E O R. X X.

items.text: Quaestio est utrum punctum centrale crucis sit necessarium ternario ex binario constituto, an sine detrimento removeri possit.
Argumentatio demonstrativa et mystagogica absentiam puncti redigit ad dissolutionem unitatis linearum atque ad mutationem binarii in quaternarium.
Punctum ternarii ut necessarium statuitur, dum eiusdem puncti in quaternario remotio ut purgatio superfluitatis exhibetur.
Eadem figura geometrica in distinctionem ontologicam convertitur: punctum ternarii est principium copulativum, punctum quaternarii est impedimentum confusionis.
Monas per binarium et ternarium ad quaternarium purificatum procedere dicitur, ut proportione aequalitatis ad unitatem et materiam propriam redeat.
Lineae rectae elementa significant.
Binarium linearum unitatem praesupponit quae puncto communi servatur.
Sublato puncto communi, unitas linearum discontinuatur et binarium in quaternarium emergit.
Punctum quod binario adest ad ternarium constituendum necessario adesse debet et substitui non potest.
Punctum centrale non est pars binarii, quia partes linearum lineae sunt, punctum autem linea non est.
Punctum propriam hypostasim habet, quamvis in longitudinibus linearibus binarii contineatur.
Quaternarium ex puncto remoto non substantiam linearum amittit, sed distinctionem et claritatem consequitur.
In ternario punctum nullatenus superfluum est; in regno quattuor elementorum idem punctum superfluum, confusivum et corruptibile censetur.
Monas nullas unitates aut numeros externos admittit, quia suis numeris sibi sufficienter absoluta est.
Reditus Monae ad materiam propriam requirit retentionem proportionis genuinae et resectionem eorum quae ad eam non pertinent.
Punctum ternarii non potest abesse, quia absentia eius binarium destrueret.
Punctum necessarium non est pars linearis neque proprietas hypostatica binarii.
Quaternarium purificatum non retinet punctum centrale, quia illud ibi non est principium unitatis substantialis.
Claritas quaternarii non per additionem obtinetur, sed per remotionem puncti superflui et confusionis.
Via Monae non recipit numeros vel unitates extrinsecas.
Materia propria Monae non includit elementa quae eius proportionem hereditariam non servant.
Ternarium non est mera aggregatio binarii et puncti, sed unitas cuius punctum est conditio constitutiva.
Punctum idem secundum situm numeralem contrarias functiones suscipit: ternarium copulat, quaternarium separat.
Puncti remotio a quaternario non imminutio est, sed manifestatio linearum distinctarum sine detrimento ipsarum.
Purificatio definitur ut exclusio eius quod structuram non constituit sed proportionem obscurat.
Aequalitas proportionis permitit Monae, per formas suas internas transitum facienti, ad unitatem propriam restitui.
Ordo numeralis non est scalaris: idem elementum fit necessarium aut noxium prout unitatem constituit aut eam iam constitutam confundit.
Integritas non per conservationem omnium partium definitur, sed per conservationem solius proportionis propriae; purgatio igitur forma restitutionis est.
Monas systema clausum est quod internis numeris expanditur, artificio transformatur, et tamen ad primam materiam suam redit.
Valorizatio luminis et tenebrarum super operationem geometricam imponitur, ita ut puritas formalis in ordinem spiritualem transferatur.
Falsum esse debet punctum semper eandem essentiam functionemque servare, quia punctum ternarii et punctum quaternarii oppositis valoribus ordinantur.
Falsa est identitas inter contineri in lineis et esse pars linearum; punctum continetur sine compositione lineari.
Falsum esse debet quod imminutio numerica necessario sit imminutio substantialis, quia sublatio puncti quaternarium clarius distinguit.
Externa additio non potest Monae perfectionem conferre, quia eius sufficientia et restitutio ex numeris propriis pendent.
Argumentatio excludit omnem unitatem quae sine medio copulativo immediate inter lineas ponitur.
Argumentatio excludit plenitudinem indiscriminatam, in qua retinere omne datum praeferatur distinctioni proportionatae.
Systema non admittit principium extrinsecum quod Monae ordinem fundet, quia Monas ad se ipsam et ad materiam suam propriam reducitur.
Binarium linearum + punctum commune → ternarium unitum; remotio puncti → discontinuatio unitatis → quaternarium.
Examen situs puncti → distinctio puncti necessarii et puncti superflui → conservatio primi, reiectio secundi.
Quaternarium purificatum + proportio aequalitatis → restitutio Monae ad unitatem et materiam propriam.
Exclusio externorum numerorum → autarkia numeralis → expansio interna et reditus proportionalis.
Dubium de absentia puncti → suppositio subtractionis → binarii conversio in quaternarium → impossibilitas binarii simul remanentis et dissoluti.
Necessitas puncti ternarii → negatio partis linearis → affirmatio hypostasis propriae intra binarium contentae.
Transitus ad crucem quaternariam → remotio mathematice possibilis → quaternarii distinctio et purificatio.
Figura A punctum necessarium exhibens / figura B vacuitatem puncti remoti exhibens → Monas per ternarium ad quaternarium purificatum restituta.
Punctum reclassificatur non ut res simpliciter data, sed ut operator cuius necessitas a configuratione numerali pendet.
Oppositio inter additionem et subtractionem dissolvitur: additio puncti potest unitatem constituere, subtractio puncti potest claritatem producere.
Quaternarium non describitur ut mera multiplicatio binarii, sed ut effectus discontinuatae unitatis et locus purificationis.
Proportio transfertur a relatione quantitativa ad criterium inclusionis, purificationis, identitatis et reditus.
Surface — Cruces duarum linearum et punctum earum commune vel remotum examinantur.
Structural — Unitas, discontinuatio, pars, hypostasis, proportio et purificatio relationem inter binarium, ternarium et quaternarium ordinant.
Metastrategic — Demonstratio mathematica adhibetur ut discriminet quid intra figuram retinendum sit et quid tanquam superfluum reiciendum.
Ontological/Temporal — Monas ex numero proprio evolvitur, in amplitudinem diffunditur, et per resectionem ad materiam primam propriam restituitur.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam necessitatem puncti in ternario, conversionem eius subtractione in quaternarium, et purificationem quaternarii.
Commissura principalis manet in transitu a demonstratione geometrica ad iudicium spirituale, quia corruptibilitas et tenebrositas puncti quaternarii geometrice non inferuntur.
Systema cohaeret dum differentia inter punctum constitutivum et punctum confusivum situ numerali regitur; criterium huius mutationis ultra ipsam configurationem non plene determinatur.
Tensionem efficit quod punctum propriam hypostasim habet et tamen in longitudinibus linearibus contineri dicitur, sine expositione modi huius continentiae.
Tensionem secundariam efficit quod Monas sibi sufficiens dicitur, sed simul artificis industria ad expansionem et restitutionem indigere describitur.

translations.title: T H E O R. X X.

items.text: The question is whether the central point of the cross is necessary to the ternary constituted from the binary, or whether it can be removed without loss.
Demonstrative and mystagogical argumentation reduces the absence of the point to the dissolution of the unity of the lines and to the transformation of the binary into the quaternary.
The point of the ternary is established as necessary, while the removal of that same point in the quaternary is presented as a purgation of superfluity.
The same geometric figure is converted into an ontological distinction: the point of the ternary is a copulative principle, the point of the quaternary is an impediment of confusion.
The Monad is said to proceed through the binary and the ternary to the purified quaternary, so that by the proportion of equality it may return to unity and to its own matter.
Straight lines signify elements.
The binary of lines presupposes a unity that is preserved by a common point.
When the common point is removed, the unity of the lines is interrupted and a quaternary emerges from the binary.
The point that is present to the binary in order to constitute the ternary must necessarily be present and cannot be substituted.
The central point is not a part of the binary, because the parts of lines are lines, whereas a point is not a line.
The point has its own hypostasis, although it is contained within the linear extensions of the binary.
The quaternary resulting from the removed point does not lose the substance of the lines, but attains distinction and clarity.
In the ternary the point is by no means superfluous; in the realm of the four elements, the same point is considered superfluous, confusive, and corruptible.
The Monad admits no external units or numbers, because it is sufficiently absolute in itself through its own numbers.
The return of the Monad to its own matter requires the retention of genuine proportion and the cutting away of those things that do not pertain to it.
The point of the ternary cannot be absent, because its absence would destroy the binary.
The necessary point is neither a linear part nor a hypostatic property of the binary.
The purified quaternary does not retain the central point, because there it is not a principle of substantial unity.
The clarity of the quaternary is not attained through addition, but through the removal of the superfluous point and of confusion.
The path of the Monad admits no extrinsic numbers or units.
The proper matter of the Monad does not include elements that do not preserve its inherited proportion.
The ternary is not a mere aggregation of the binary and the point, but a unity of which the point is a constitutive condition.
The same point, according to its numerical position, assumes contrary functions: it couples the ternary and separates the quaternary.
The removal of the point from the quaternary is not a diminution, but a manifestation of distinct lines without loss of the lines themselves.
Purgation is defined as the exclusion of that which does not constitute the structure but obscures proportion.
Equality of proportion permits the Monad, passing through its internal forms, to be restored to its own unity.
Numerical order is not scalar: the same element becomes necessary or harmful according as it constitutes unity or confuses unity already constituted.
Integrity is defined not through the preservation of all parts, but through the preservation of proportion alone; purgation is therefore a form of restoration.
The Monad is a closed system that expands through internal numbers, is transformed by artifice, and nevertheless returns to its first matter.
A valuation of light and darkness is imposed upon the geometric operation, so that formal purity is transferred into a spiritual order.
It must be false that the point always preserves the same essence and function, because the point of the ternary and the point of the quaternary are ordered by opposed values.
The identity between being contained in lines and being a part of lines is false; the point is contained without linear composition.
It must be false that numerical diminution is necessarily substantial diminution, because the removal of the point distinguishes the quaternary more clearly.
External addition cannot confer perfection upon the Monad, because its sufficiency and restoration depend upon its own numbers.
The argument excludes every unity that is immediately posited among lines without a copulative medium.
The argument excludes indiscriminate fullness, in which retaining everything given is preferred to proportionate distinction.
The system admits no extrinsic principle that grounds the order of the Monad, because the Monad is reduced to itself and to its own proper matter.
Binary of lines + common point → united ternary; removal of the point → interruption of unity → quaternary.
Examination of the point's position → distinction between necessary point and superfluous point → preservation of the former, rejection of the latter.
Purified quaternary + proportion of equality → restoration of the Monad to unity and its own matter.
Exclusion of external numbers → numerical autarky → internal expansion and proportional return.
Doubt concerning the absence of the point → supposition of subtraction → conversion of the binary into the quaternary → impossibility of the binary remaining and being dissolved at once.
Necessity of the point of the ternary → negation of linear part → affirmation of a proper hypostasis contained within the binary.
Transition to the quaternary cross → mathematically possible removal → distinction and purification of the quaternary.
Figure A displaying the necessary point / figure B displaying the emptiness of the removed point → the Monad restored through the ternary to the purified quaternary.
The point is reclassified not as a thing simply given, but as an operator whose necessity depends on numerical configuration.
The opposition between addition and subtraction is dissolved: addition of the point can constitute unity, removal of the point can produce clarity.
The quaternary is described not as a mere multiplication of the binary, but as the effect of interrupted unity and as a site of purification.
Proportion is transferred from a quantitative relation to a criterion of inclusion, purification, identity, and return.
Surface — Crosses of two lines and their common or removed point are examined.
Structural — Unity, interruption, part, hypostasis, proportion, and purification order the relation among the binary, ternary, and quaternary.
Metastrategic — Mathematical demonstration is employed to discriminate what is to be retained within the figure and what is to be rejected as superfluous.
Ontological/Temporal — The Monad evolves from its own number, spreads into extension, and through cutting away is restored to its own first matter.
The axioms suffice to reconstruct the necessity of the point in the ternary, its conversion by subtraction into the quaternary, and the purification of the quaternary.

The principal juncture remains in the transition from geometric demonstration to spiritual judgment, because the corruptibility and darkness of the point of the quaternary are not geometrically inferred.

The system coheres so long as the difference between the constitutive point and the confusive point is governed by numerical position; the criterion of this change beyond the configuration itself is not fully determined.
A tension is produced by the fact that the point has its own hypostasis and yet is said to be contained within the linear extensions, without an exposition of the mode of this containment.
A secondary tension is produced by the fact that the Monad is said to be self-sufficient, yet at the same time is described as requiring the craftsman's industry for expansion and restoration.

identity.title: T H E O R. X X.

items.text: Quaeritur quid nova Monadis mysticae commutatio localis revelet, cum corpus eius in membra B, D, C dissecare liceat.
Argumentatio demonstrativa et hermetico-hieroglyphica est: situs, figura, magnitudo et connexio partium pro notis essentialibus accipiuntur.
D et C, ad terram versa et inter se notis figuris manifesta, essentias inferiores, stabiles ac fixas indicant; B autem tertium membrum obscurius et minus determinatum manet.
Natura B per lunam duplicem et crucem elementorum describitur ut gradus existendi et vivendi, elementari artificio tractandus, non ut solaris plenitudo iam naturaliter perfecta.
Ex semicirculis B separatis solaris circulus effici potest, sed effectus est artificialis; ipsa figura B naturaliter laxa, fluxilis et incompleta manet.
Dissectio unius corporis in ternarium non destruit unitatem: membra, ex eadem Monade orta, sympathiam et unionem monadicam mutuam recipere dicuntur.
Partium Monadis situs localis significationem hieroglyphicam et philosophicam mutat.
Figurae D et C a figura B essentialiter distinguuntur.
Directio inferior ad terram, in hac arte, stabilitatem et fixationem significat.
Semicirculus lunae et circulus integer solis hieroglyphica sunt signa.
Duplex figura lunaris B duos primos gradus naturarum creatarum, esse et vivere, designare potest.
Crux B adiuncta elementorum artificium requirit.
Semicirculi separati, arte connexi, circulum solaris plenitudinis repraesentare possunt.
Quod arte ex B componitur non propterea naturaliter in B solidum aut perfectum est.
Minor mensura semicirculorum B disproportionalitatem eius ad D et C indicat.
Membra ex uno corpore Monadis anatomice educta originem communem servant.
Origo communis membrorum sympathiam, attractionem et unionem monadicam fundat.
B non est figura tam manifesta neque tam vulgariter cognoscibilis quam D et C.
B non est naturaliter circulus solaris integer, quia semicirculi eius separati, laxi et dissoluti sunt.
Plenitudo solaris ex B non datur immediate, sed per artem connexionis producitur.
Ex B verum D sperari non potest.
Vera C non fuit primum in natura B; ideo B non est vera luna viva.
Vita et motus B non proprie et naturaliter, sed saltem analogice, attribuuntur.
Theoria non exhaurit mysteria Monadis, sed iter ad ulteriora tantum indicat.
D et C, quia ad inferiora magis vergunt et terram hieroglyphice participant, stabilitatem et fixationem magis quam B significant.
B significat existentiam viventem sub conditione operationis elementaris, non perfectionem solarem iam possessam.
Solaris circulus est terminus possibilis transformationis B, quia semicirculi eius ad punctum commune iam referuntur, licet nondum cohaereant.
Productio figurae E ex B confirmat transformationem eius in characterem Veneris, non in D aut C verum.
Praedicata de B transferenda sunt analogice, dum praedicata propria eius ad figuram arietinam inversam et ad signum elementorum referuntur.
Ternarius B–D–C est articulatio interna unius Monadis, non aggregatum trium rerum extrinsecarum.
Systema perfectionem non ut datum originarium, sed ut effectum artis ordinantis constituit: natura B potentiam praebet, ars plenitudinem formalem efficit.
Ordo ontologicus graduum naturae et ordo figuralis transformationum non coincidunt: signum vivum-lunare potest structuram solarem simul potentia continere et actu carere.
Inferioritas localis D et C non degradationem simplicem, sed maiorem determinationem, stabilitatem et essentialem manifestiam importat.
Unitas monadica non est indistinctio partium, sed vis quae differentias anatomice explicatas in sympathiam reciprocumque nexum reconducit.
Falsum esse debet quod figurae similes eandem essentiam aut eundem gradum perfectionis necessario habeant.
Falsum esse debet quod possibilitas geometrica connexionis iam praesentem unitatem substantialem constituat.
Falsum esse debet quod vita, motus et lunaritas in B proprie praedicentur ex sola specie symbolica.
Falsum esse debet quod dissectio analytica Monadem in res independentes dissolvat.
Systema excludit perfectionem naturalem sine operatione artificiosa: solaritas plena non est status ad manum, sed compositio facienda.
Systema excludit interpretationem omnino exhaustivam: figura est fons mysteriorum indefinite ulteriorum, non obiectum semel clausum.
Systema excludit identitatem immediatam inter visibilem formam et veritatem essentialem, cum B apparere possit lunaris et vitalis sine vera lunaritate vivente.
Commutatio situs Monadis → distributio anatomica in B, D, C → lectura orientationis, figurae et situs.
D et C terram versus ordinata → stabilitas et fixio → essentiae inferiores magis manifeste determinatae.
B cum duplici luna et cruce → esse + vivere + elementorum magisterium → potentia transmutationis.
Semicirculi B separati → connexio artificialis → circulus solaris repraesentatus → character Veneris, non solaritas naturaliter possessa.
Defectus naturalis B → restrictio praedicatorum ad analogiam → distinctio inter proprium B et translata de D ac C.
Unum corpus dissectum → origo communis membrorum → sympathia magnetica → unio monadica absolutissima.
Commutatio localis Monadis → ternarius B–D–C → differentia essentialis D/C et B → analysis naturae B.
Luna duplex + crux elementorum → existentia viva elementis tractanda → semicirculi separati → plenitudo solaris artificialiter componenda.
Inadequatio B ad D et C → negatio verae lunae vivae et solaritatis naturalis → praedicatio analogica → restitutio unitatis per sympathiam monadicam.
Monas non iam figura simplex videtur, sed corpus resolubile cuius partes diversa munera, gradus et modos perfectionis exhibent.
Oppositio naturae et artis reordinatur: ars non creat ex nihilo, sed potentiam incompositam B in formam solarem apparentem disponit.
Solaris, lunaris, elementaris, terrestris et Venerius characteres non species separatae manent, sed effectus positionis, compositionis et mensurae partium fiunt.
Unitas et distinctio desinunt esse contraria: discretio anatomica fit instrumentum manifestandae unitatis magneticae.
Surface — Monas relocata in membra B, D et C dividitur; B per semicirculos et crucem, D per circulum punctatum, C per cornua lunaria legitur.
Structural — Figura, directio, proportio et nexus partium constituunt regulas quibus status naturalis, analogicus vel artificialis discernitur.

Metastrategic — Textus interpretationem hieroglyphicam a recognitione visiva ad operationem disciplinatam transfert: videre figuram non sufficit; oportet scire quid arte effici, quid natura possideri possit.
Ontological/Temporal — Esse et vivere sunt gradus initiales; plenitudo solaris est terminus nondum naturaliter adveniens, quem transformatio artificialis temporaliter interponit.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam conclusionem principalem: B est figura elementaris et lunaris potentiae, solaritatem autem non nisi arte compositam exhibet.
Systema maxime cohaeret ubi figurae, situs inferiores, proportiones et distinctionem naturae ab arte in unam catenam inferentialem coniungit.
Commissura fragilis manet in transitu a proprietatibus graphicis ad essentias, stabilitatem, vitam et veritatem figurarum, quia regula generalis huius transitus hic non demonstratur.
Tensionem constituit quod B dicitur potentiam solaris plenitudinis habere, simul vero nec veram lunam vivam nec verum D in se naturaliter continere.
Unio monadica post dissectionem assertio structuram claudit, sed mechanismus quo sympathia magnetica ex sola origine communi necessario sequatur non plene determinatur.
Restitutio motum textus servat, quia ab relocatione figurali per distinctionem naturalis et artificialis ad unionem finalem procedit, atque mysteriorum ulteriorem indagationem apertam relinquit.
It is asked what the new local transformation of the mystical Monad reveals, when its body may be dissected into the members B, D, C.
The argumentation is demonstrative and hermetic-hieroglyphic: position, figure, magnitude, and connection of the parts are taken as essential marks.
D and C, turned toward the earth and manifest to one another by their figures, indicate lower, stable, and fixed essences; B, however, remains a third member more obscure and less determinate.

The nature of B is described through the double moon and the cross of the elements as a degree of existing and living, to be treated by elemental artifice, not as a solar fullness already naturally perfected.
From the separated semicircles of B a solar circle can be made, but the effect is artificial; the figure of B itself remains naturally loose, fluid, and incomplete.
The dissection of one body into a ternary does not destroy unity: the members, arising from the same Monad, are said to receive mutual sympathy and monadic union.
The local position of the Monad's parts changes their hieroglyphic and philosophical signification.
The figures of D and C are essentially distinct from the figure of B.
Direction downward toward the earth, in this art, signifies stability and fixation.
The lunar semicircle and the complete solar circle are hieroglyphic signs.
The double lunar figure of B can designate the first two degrees of created natures, being and living.
The cross appended to B requires the artifice of the elements.
Separated semicircles, connected by art, can represent the circle of solar fullness.
What is composed from B by art is not thereby naturally solid or perfect in B.
The lesser size of B's semicircles indicates its disproportion to D and C.
Members anatomically drawn forth from one body of the Monad retain a common origin.
The members' common origin grounds sympathy, attraction, and monadic union.
B is not a figure as manifest or as commonly recognizable as D and C.
B is not naturally a complete solar circle, because its semicircles are separated, loose, and dissolved.
Solar fullness is not given from B immediately, but is produced through the art of connection.
From B, a true D cannot be hoped for.
The true C was not originally in the nature of B; therefore B is not a true living moon.
Life and motion are attributed to B not properly and naturally, but at least analogically.
The theory does not exhaust the mysteries of the Monad, but only indicates a path toward further matters.
D and C, because they incline more toward lower things and hieroglyphically partake of earth, signify stability and fixation more than B.
B signifies living existence under the condition of elemental operation, not solar perfection already possessed.
The solar circle is a possible terminus of B's transformation, because its semicircles already refer to a common point, although they do not yet cohere.
The production of figure E from B confirms its transformation into the character of Venus, not into a true D or C.
Predicates concerning B are to be transferred analogically, while its proper predicates are referred to the inverted ram-like figure and to the sign of the elements.
The ternary B–D–C is an internal articulation of one Monad, not an aggregate of three extrinsic things.
The system establishes perfection not as an original given, but as an effect of ordering art: the nature of B supplies potency, art produces formal fullness.
The ontological order of the degrees of nature and the figural order of transformations do not coincide: the living-lunar sign can at once contain a solar structure in potency and lack it in act.
The local inferiority of D and C imports not simple degradation, but greater determination, stability, and essential manifestness.
Monadic unity is not the indistinction of parts, but a force that leads differences anatomically unfolded back into sympathy and reciprocal connection.
It must be false that similar figures necessarily have the same essence or the same degree of perfection.
It must be false that the geometrical possibility of connection already constitutes a present substantial unity.
It must be false that life, motion, and lunarity are properly predicated of B from symbolic appearance alone.
It must be false that analytical dissection dissolves the Monad into independent things.
The system excludes natural perfection without artificial operation: full solarity is not a state at hand, but a composition to be made.
The system excludes a wholly exhaustive interpretation: the figure is a source of indefinitely further mysteries, not an object closed once and for all.
The system excludes immediate identity between visible form and essential truth, since B can appear lunar and vital without true living lunarity.
Transformation of the Monad's position → anatomical distribution into B, D, C → reading of orientation, figure, and position.
D and C ordered toward the earth → stability and fixation → lower essences more manifestly determined.
B with double moon and cross → being + living + mastery of the elements → potentiality of transmutation.
Separated semicircles of B → artificial connection → solar circle represented → character of Venus, not naturally possessed solarity.
Natural defect of B → restriction of predicates to analogy → distinction between what is proper to B and matters transferred from D and C.
One dissected body → common origin of the members → magnetic sympathy → most absolute monadic union.
Local transformation of the Monad → ternary B–D–C → essential difference of D/C and B → analysis of B's nature.
Double moon + cross of the elements → living existence to be treated through the elements → separated semicircles → solar fullness to be artificially composed.
Inadequacy of B to D and C → negation of a true living moon and natural solarity → analogical predication → restoration of unity through monadic sympathy.
The Monad no longer appears as a simple figure, but as a resolvable body whose parts display diverse functions, degrees, and modes of perfection.
The opposition of nature and art is reordered: art does not create from nothing, but disposes B's uncomposed potency into an apparent solar form.
Solar, lunar, elemental, terrestrial, and Venusian characters do not remain separate species, but become effects of the position, composition, and measure of the parts.
Unity and distinction cease to be contraries: anatomical separation becomes an instrument for manifesting magnetic unity.
Surface — The relocated Monad is divided into members B, D, and C; B is read through semicircles and a cross, D through a dotted circle, C through lunar horns.
Structural — Figure, direction, proportion, and connection of the parts establish the rules by which natural, analogical, or artificial status is discerned.

Metastrategic — The text transfers hieroglyphic interpretation from visual recognition to disciplined operation: seeing a figure is not sufficient; one must know what can be effected by art and what can be possessed by nature.
Ontological/Temporal — Being and living are initial degrees; solar fullness is a terminus not yet naturally attained, which artificial transformation temporally interposes.
The axioms suffice to reconstruct the principal conclusion: B is an elemental and lunar figure of potency, but displays solarity only as composed by art.
The system is most coherent where it joins figures, lower positions, proportions, and the distinction of nature from art into one inferential chain.
A fragile juncture remains in the transition from graphic properties to essences, stability, life, and the truth of figures, because the general rule of this transition is not demonstrated here.
It constitutes a tension that B is said to have the potency of solar fullness, while at the same time naturally containing within itself neither a true living moon nor a true D.
Monadic union after dissection, as an assertion, closes the structure, but the mechanism by which magnetic sympathy necessarily follows from common origin alone is not fully determined.

The reconstruction preserves the movement of the text, because it proceeds from figural relocation through the distinction of natural and artificial to final union, and leaves open the further investigation of mysteries.
Theorema quaerit utrum mysteria MONADIS iam exhausta sint et quomodo ex ea adhuc instrumenta artis sacrae deduci possint.
Quaestio in quaestionem novam vertitur: non res extraneae quaerendae sunt, sed nexus MONADIS dissolvendi et partes eius notis distinctae.
Fundamentum argumentationis est compositio formarum, litterarum, vasorum, materiarum et operationum intra idem signorum systema.
Probatio petitur ex symmetria mystica, metathesi locali, homologis geometricis, functionibus vasorum et effectibus artis.
Motus procedit a revelatione selectiva ad decompositionem symbolorum, deinde ad usum operativum et ad interpretationem mysticam.
Argumentatio est reconstructiva, mystagogica et symbolico-operativa, cum implicatione cosmologica.
Mysteria MONADIS nondum exhausta sunt.
Vasa secretiora artis sacrae ex officina MONADIS caute deduci et solis initiatis revelari possunt.
Omnis nexus MONADIS sapienter dissolvi potest, ut singulae partes distinctis notis designentur.
Vas a artificiale ex A et B componitur, utrique commune, cum semidiametro M.
Vas a a prima littera alphabeti Graeci α sola partium metathesi locali differt.
Recta, circulus et semicirculus veram symmetriam mysticam constituunt, quam etiam circulus cum semicirculo ad idem propositum praestare potest.
λ et δ quasi imagines aliorum vasorum sunt, λ vitreum et δ terreum.
λ et δ etiam pistillum ac mortarium significant, quibus lapides artificiales et alia pretiosa in subtilissimos pulveres conteruntur.
ω vas mysteriorum plenissimum est, ex duobus semicirculis constans et a postrema Graeci alphabeti littera sola partium metathesi differens.
α ex artificio spiraculi secretissimo et brevissimo specimen primordiale tyronibus elicit, dum via ad subtiliora praeparanda discitur.
Aer externus et ventus λ in praecipua eius functione magnum damnum afferunt.
ω OMNIUM HORARUM HOMO est.
Fructus artis sacrae ex mysterio duarum litterarum oriuntur, nihil extra MONADEM in medium adducto.
Recta linea quae in α apparet homologiam habet cum parte crucis postremae anatomiae, quae littera M notatur.
Signa haec non solum aphormas sed etiam apodixes praebent iis quorum vigor igneus et origo caelestis est.
Dogma non Μυσικὸν sed Μυστικὸν et Arcanum est; mundus λόγῳ δημιουργῷ methodizatur et homo contemplativus per rectam operationem λόγον mysticum discit.
MONAS non est corpus mysteriorum iam perfecte exhaustum.
Ars sacra non est doctrina omnibus indiscriminatim revelata, sed ad initiatos restringitur.
Formae et materiae vasorum vulgarium in hoc loco explicandae non sunt.
Explicatio nihil extra MONADEM ad argumentum admittit.
Dogma hoc non est Μυσικὸν, id est ad musicam pertinens, sed Μυστικὸν et Arcanum.
Functio praecipua λ sine exclusione aeris externi et venti stabilis non est.
Discrimen inter constructiones geometricas ad finem mysticum usque ad punctum evanescit, cum ad idem propositum recidant.
Dissolutio nexus et notatio partium transformant MONADEM in inventarium symbolorum ex quo vasa distincta componi possunt.
Metathesis localis non est mutatio merae positionis, sed medium quo eadem forma diversa munera mystica et operativa accipit.
Geometria signorum simul est descriptio vasorum, imago instrumentorum et schema operationis materialis.
Ars initiatoria gradatim procedit a specimine primordiali tyronum ad praeparationes subtiliores.
Efficacia artis non separatur a condicionibus materialibus, quia functio λ per aerem et ventum perturbatur.
Correspondentia inter litteram, figuram, crucem et anatomiam efficit ut signa MONADIS originem internam partium demonstrent.
Status ω tam temporalem quam anthropologicam dimensionem signo tribuit, quia vas simul «omnium horarum homo» appellatur.
Signa geometrica, si a subiecto initiato intellecta et operata sint, ex indicibus possibilitatis in testimonia demonstrativa convertuntur.
MONAS fit microcosmus generativus in quo litterae, geometria, materia, instrumenta, corpus, initiatio et cosmologia ad idem principium referuntur.
Cognitio mystica hic non est contemplatio passiva, sed operatio recta qua signum, apparatus et intellectus simul transformantur.
Systema unitatem MONADIS per analysim obtinet: nexus dissolvuntur ut partes discernantur, sed omnes differentiae ad idem propositum mysticum redeunt.
Secreta distributio cognitionis est pars mechanismi argumenti, quia specimen tyronibus, subtiliora initiatis et apodixis subiecto praeparato reservantur.
Tempus et ambitus physicus non sunt adiuncta externa, sed condiciones quae statum et munus signorum determinant.
Auctoritas probationis transfertur a demonstratione communiter verificabili ad aptitudinem initiati, cui signa apodicticam vim praebere dicuntur.
Systema excludit realitatem autonomam quae extra MONADEM causam, materiam vel finem praebeat.
Litterae non sunt signa neutra vel mere alphabetica, sed structurae operativae quae vasa et processus generant.
Scientia non est universaliter communicabilis, quia intellectus eius dependet ab initiatione, dispositione et gradu artis.
Separatio inter formam geometricam, materiam, instrumentum, corpus et mundum non admittitur ut divisio ultima.
MONAS non claudit seriem in finem exhaustivum, quamvis singulas figuras et functiones definiat.
Intellectus mysticus a recta operatione seiunctus non sufficit.
Argumentatio praecludit probationem ab observatore extrinseco qui initiationem, dispositionem et artem non participat.
Possibilitas signum a re significata absolute separandi excluditur, quia figura ipsa munus, materiam et effectum continere debet.
Materia indifferens et ambitus physicus neuter esse non possunt, cum λ ab aere et vento laedatur.
Conclusio definitiva quae omnia mysteria MONADIS clauderet structuram destruere deberet, quia inexhaustio eius principium est.
Publica aequabilitas cognitionis praeclusa est; ordo cognitionis per gradus occultationis et revelationis constituitur.
MONAS inexhausta → nexus universi dissolvuntur → partes litteraliter notantur.
Partes notatae → compositio A et B → vas a cum semidiametro M.
Metathesis localis → distinctio α, λ, δ et ω → distributio formarum et munerum.
Recta, circulus, semicirculus → symmetria mystica → translatio inter figuram, vas et instrumentum.
Instrumentum et materia → conterere lapides artificiales → praeparatio operativa.
Artificium secretum → specimen tyronum → cognitio subtiliorum viarum.
Munus λ → exclusio aeris et venti; munus ω → generalitas temporalium horarum.
Correspondentiae internae → apodixis initiato → doctrina de homine, mundo et λόγῳ mystico.
Mysteria MONADIS inexhausta → revelatio vasorum secretorum → dissolutio nexus → notatio partium.
Notatio partium → compositio et metathesis litterarum → distinctio vasorum, formarum et materiarum.
Distinctio symbolica → functio instrumentalis → gradus initiationis et praeparationis.
Functio materialis et temporalis → correspondentiae anatomicae et cosmologicae → signa ut apodixes doctrinae mysticae.
Primum visibile fit non signum isolatum, sed nexus internus ex quo formae, vasa et functiones generantur.
Litterae denuo classificatae sunt ut figurae geometricæ, vasa artificialia, instrumenta, materiae et indices anatomici.
Oppositio inter mysticum et practicum cadit, quia operatio materialis ipsa fit medium cognitionis mysticae.
Ager strategicus cognitionis describitur ut scala initiatoria: occultatio, specimen, praeparatio subtilior, apodixis.
Tempus et ambitus physicus in tabulam conceptualem inseruntur ut condiciones constitutivae, non circumstantiae externae.
Oppositio inter MONADEM et mundum externum reordinatur, quia mundus, corpus et ars intra productionem MONADIS comprehenduntur.
Surface: Litterae α, λ, δ et ω ut figurae et vasa cum materiis ac functionibus propriis definiuntur.
Structural: Dissolutio nexus, notatio partium et metathesis localis mechanismum differentiationis ac recompositionis constituunt.
Metastrategic: Revelatio gradatim ordinata determinat quis videre, operari et apodixin accipere possit.
Ontological/Temporal: MONAS ut campus realitatis internus ponitur, in quo forma, materia, corpus, mundus et tempus per symbola connectuntur; ω horarum totalitatem et personam humanam coniungit.
Axiomata sufficiunt ad restituendam seriem fundamentalem: inexhaustio MONADIS, dissolutio partium, compositio vasorum, functio materialis et transitus ad doctrinam mysticam.
Firmitas maxima est in nexu inter decompositionem symbolicam, metathesin localem, symmetriam et correspondentias vasorum.
Exacta relatio graphica partium et omnium formarum e figuris adiunctis tantum ex parte determinatur; schema non restituit omnem geometriam.
Locus fragilis est transitus a similitudine figurae ad efficaciam materialem et inde ad vim apodicticam.
Tensio manet inter secretum initiatorum et exhibitionem publicam, inter analysim partium et unitatem MONADIS, inter inexhaustionem et assertionem demonstrativam.
Passus Hebraicus et nonnulla vocabula in fonte illegibilia vel ancipitia manent, unde relatio inter artificium secretum et specimen primordiale plene definiri non potest.
Restitutio motum verum argumentationis servat, sed non potest supplere proceduras occultas quas textus solis initiatis reservat.
The theorem asks whether the mysteries of the MONAD have already been exhausted and how instruments of the sacred art may still be derived from it.
