Repair depends on a preserved common measure: persuasion can reactivate a correct principle, while agreed ends and proportion can restore damaged reciprocity.
Political corruption magnifies individual ethical vulnerability by eroding the justice, friendship, and common activities needed to enact otherwise viable character.
Ethical standing depends on capacities for rational and communal participation rather than on biological motion or imposed social function alone.

Similar pleasure can either fragment or complete agency: its status is determined by whether it captures a particular against reason, repairs a deficiency, accompanies worthy activity, or supplies an incidental ground of love.
Ethical life is a topology of mediation: universal judgment requires an action-governing particular, and reciprocal goodwill requires recognized shared activity.
Human flourishing is distributed actuality rather than private possession because its completion spans character, activity, pleasure, friendship, material conditions, and political commonality.
Virtue stabilizes time by converting correct valuation into repeatable activity, proper pleasure, tested trust, and durable reciprocity.
Defect can be diagnosed by locating the failed interface: corrupted principle, captured perception, inactive disposition, incidental valuation, failed reciprocity, or destroyed common field.
Pleasure functions as feedback rather than an independent good: it intensifies the activity or attachment from which it arises, whether ordered or disordered.
Agency is neither unitary nor isolated; it is a composite internal ordering embedded in reciprocal and political relations that can sustain or impede its exercise.
Corrective intervention is possible only before the generative norm disappears: preserved principle permits ethical cure, and retained common measure permits relational repair.
Politics is not an external application of ethics but the highest-order environment controlling the availability of common activity, reciprocity, justice, and relational flourishing.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Correct principle → action-governing particular → fitting action → proper pleasure → strengthened activity forms the positive intrapersonal loop.
Appetite → affective capture of the particular → action against preserved judgment → regret and persuasion → possible reactivation of principle forms the reparable failure loop.
Virtuous character → love of the other as good → shared activity → proper pleasure and benefit → trust and duration → intensified shared life forms the complete-friendship loop.
Conditional valuation → alteration of pleasure or utility → withdrawal of affection → complaint or dissolution forms the incidental-friendship decay loop.
Common participation → friendship and justice → common benefit → political stability recursively expands the communal field, while private advantage reverses the loop into contraction.
Unimpeded shared virtuous activity is the dominant attractor toward which the reconstructions of knowledge, pleasure, happiness, friendship, and polity converge.
Primary forms classify deficient analogues, while the analogues recursively clarify the conditions that make the primary forms complete.
The principal escalation path is internal cognition → bodily action → pleasure → complete activity → shared life → community → political constitution.
Pleasure becomes a machine at the phase change where it ceases to be treated as a homogeneous object and begins to amplify the activity or relationship generating it.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Finite embodiment plus nonautomatic practical cognition generates the possibility of action against preserved judgment.
Object plus affect plus rational principle plus choice plus enactment generates the classification of individual ethical states.
Preserved measure generates regret and repair; corrupted or absent measure generates resistance to cure or exclusion from ordinary ethical classification.
Separation of pleasure from restoration generates activity-specific pleasure; activity-specific pleasure generates the possibility of pleasant happiness.
Chosen goodwill plus recognition plus shared activity generates friendship as relational actuality rather than private feeling.
Reason for loving generates friendship species; virtuous character integrates goodness, pleasure, utility, trust, and duration into the complete form.
Equality or proportion plus form-specific return generates relational preservation; loss of common measure generates complaint, disparity, or dissolution.
Community plus common benefit generates friendship and justice; their conjunction supplies the political field in which embodied, relational happiness can remain active.

Knowledgeable wrongdoing → layered practical cognition → taxonomy of preserved, absent, and corrupted principle → reconstruction of pleasure as activity → embodied happiness → reciprocal goodwill → friendship species → proportional community → political conditions of relational flourishing.
Correct disposition → vulnerable enactment → activity-specific pleasure → repeated shared life → tested relational stability → communal support → renewed conditions for correct enactment.
The subject is redrawn from a unitary rational chooser into a layered practical system embedded in reciprocal relations.
Moral diagnosis shifts from action type and felt affection to the principle, end, object, choice, and relation that generate them.
Pleasure is reclassified from a homogeneous object of pursuit into an activity-indexed amplifier that can also ground conditional forms of association.
Virtue is relocated from private character into the generative basis of trustworthy, pleasant, useful, and durable shared life.
Self-sufficiency is redrawn as non-remedial dependence: the excellent agent does not need friends as instruments but needs companions for the activity of living well.
Equality is transformed from identical distribution into a plural architecture of truth-governed action, equal reciprocity, and proportional return.
Happiness becomes embodied and relational actuality rather than an invulnerable possession of virtue.
Political constitutions become conditions that expand or contract ethical actuality by organizing common benefit, justice, friendship, and participation.
Ethical reading becomes necessarily temporal: episodic interruption, stable character, tested confidence, separation, and changing circumstances cannot be compressed into static labels.

[Surface level] The explicit field comprises incontinence, self-control, bodily and contemplative pleasure, friendship species, reciprocity, disputes, household relations, and political constitutions.
[Structural level] The same architecture governs both domains: disposition must pass through mediating activity, while object, end, and measure determine the resulting ethical form.
[Metastrategic level] The system intervenes by replacing flat oppositions with primary, qualified, analogical, equal, proportional, curable, and terminal classifications.

[Ontological / Temporal level] Reality is organized as activity emerging from mutable embodied states over time; episodic affect, stable character, repeated association, and political continuity determine whether potentials become actual.

[Methodological / Performative level] Dialectical distinctions repair ordinary ethical appearances, while serial classification performs the expansion from psychic conflict to relational and political order.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Voluntary incontinence remains unstable because responsibility is affirmed precisely where decisive practical cognition is inactive or compromised.
Pleasure oscillates between being identical with unimpeded activity, arising from activity, and strengthening activity; its relational use inherits rather than resolves this ambiguity.
Happiness is called self-sufficient while depending on external goods and companions; the distinction between remedial and constitutive dependence stabilizes but does not eliminate the tension.
Complete friendship joins concern for the other with the lover’s own good without fully demonstrating why these goods cannot diverge.
Proportional equality preserves hierarchy only by presupposing contestable standards of merit, while common humanity limits instrumental domination without abolishing hierarchical structure.
Complete friendship supplies the normative model, but political community requires bonds broader and weaker than complete virtue friendship.

The preserved principle makes the incontinent agent curable, yet the absence of practical wisdom blocks full virtue and therefore leaves the agent’s capacity for complete friendship structurally indeterminate.
Pleasure mutates from an object that captures action into the formal accompaniment and amplifier of activity.
State mutates from individual possession into relational disposition, exposing activity as the necessary actuality of both knowledge and friendship.
Unqualified attribution mutates from delimiting the proper object of incontinence into identifying a normative relational exemplar.
Impediment mutates from affective obstruction of a practical particular into bodily deprivation, separation, failed reciprocity, and political corruption.
Ethical measure mutates from true reason governing appetite into proportional reciprocity governing unequal social relations.
The boundary of ethical standing mutates from rational capacity distinguishing humans from animals into communal capacity resisting the exhaustive reduction of humans to instruments.
Reality appears as a nested coordination machine: rational principle gates practical particulars, virtuous ends gate relations, and communal structures gate reciprocity.
The subject is a composite and permeable node whose internal order can fail episodically and whose completion occurs through embodied shared activity.
Time alternates between interruption and stabilization: affect produces momentary capture, while character, repetition, familiarity, and confidence construct durable ethical form.
Pleasure is the machine’s feedback signal: it can hijack a local action-interface or intensify the worthy activity and relation from which it arises.
Ethical struggle consists not in eliminating affect, embodiment, inequality, or dependence but in restoring correct mediation, shared measure, and unimpeded activity.
Political order is the outer control field: common benefit widens the circuits of friendship and justice, while private advantage contracts them.

The architecture is reconstructively sufficient if it retains five coupled operators: generative ground, state/activity distinction, activity-specific pleasure, reciprocal measure, and communal enablement.
Its strongest integration lies in showing that neither correct cognition nor virtuous goodwill is self-enacting; both require mediated activity.

The exact causal integration of pleasure, character, friendship, and happiness remains underdetermined, especially where pleasure alternates between activity, accompaniment, reinforcement, and reason for attachment.
Coherence is strongest at the level of formal distinctions but weaker where proportional hierarchy depends on compressed assumptions about merit, sex, household authority, and political superiority.

Reconstruction requires sequencing and recursive return: the analysis of psychic failure must pass through pleasure and happiness before friendship can appear as constitutive shared activity rather than remedial utility.
The physiology of affective capture, the thresholds of relational disparity, and the substantive standards of proportional merit remain resistant to axiomatic reduction.
The current-level system is coherent only when friendship is read as the expansion of ethical actuality beyond the individual rather than as an appended topic external to character and happiness.
The system asks how rational activity can become a complete human life when character depends upon pleasure, intimate association, material support, and public formation.

Its governing thesis is that value belongs primarily to excellent activity: friendship is fixed by what it loves, pleasure by what it completes, and happiness by the authoritative activity it sustains.
At this scale the argument becomes a recursive theory of ethical formation, joining rational self-order, shared activity, affective reinforcement, habituation, and law.

The movement is spiral and scale-expanding: disputed exchanges and pleasures are reclassified through activity, activity generates character, character governs judgment, and judgment is reproduced through friends and institutions.
Closure is bifurcated: contemplation supplies the highest end, but the production of agents capable of excellent activity reopens ethics as legislative and political inquiry.
[Persistent] Moral value is indexed to the excellence of an activity or enduring object, not to the intensity of satisfaction, benefit, or desire.
[Persistent] The authoritative person is the rationally ordering element whose activity unifies agency, evaluates pleasures, and determines the highest form of life.
[Mutating] Virtue is both psychic concord and a socially reproduced disposition: it orders desire internally while being stabilized through shared activity, pleasure, habituation, and law.
[Persistent] Happiness is sustained excellent activity chosen for itself rather than a possession, passive state, external product, or aggregate of enjoyments.
[Mutating] Pleasure changes from a sign of ordered character into a supervenient force that strengthens or displaces activity and thereby helps reproduce the character that judges it.

[Mutating] Self-sufficiency means organized dependence rather than isolation: practical happiness requires friends and common life, while contemplation remains only relatively independent because it requires bodily, material, and political support.
[Emergent] Embodied practical excellence is intrinsically relational because its exercise, perception, correction, and reproduction require other persons.
[Attractor] Contemplation is the terminal normative attractor because it most fully realizes the authoritative element through continuous, pleasurable, self-final activity.

[Emergent] Ethical formation is a distributed feedback circuit: activity elicits pleasure, pleasure reinforces repetition, repetition stabilizes character, and character selects future activities and associates.

[Emergent] Formation changes mechanism with scale: reciprocal co-living operates within finite friendship, while law organizes character formation across populations that cannot share complete intimacy.
[Persistent] Practical reason cannot be replaced by a homogeneous metric; it must fit heterogeneous claims by moving between universal classifications and experienced particulars.
[Terminal] Ethical truth reaches practical completion only when embodied in action, habituation, law, and competent political judgment.
[Stable identity] Activity remains the primary bearer of flourishing: social life actualizes virtue through shared action, and contemplation perfects the highest rational activity.
[Escalation] The rational self expands from the source of psychic concord and proper self-love into intellect as the authoritative and quasi-divine principle of complete happiness.
[Mutation] Pleasure shifts from one element coordinated by virtuous self-concord into the formal completion and causal reinforcement of species-specific activities.
[Mutation] Self-sufficiency changes from relational completeness through friendship into the relative independence of contemplation, without ever becoming material or political autarky.
[Displacement] The friend as another self first extends reflexive awareness and then recedes before contemplation, which can approximate completion with fewer co-agents.
[Migration] Co-living migrates from intimate shared perception and imitation into legally organized repetition as the public mechanism of character formation.
[Expansion] Political concord expands from coordinated judgment among already ordered citizens into legislative science concerned with producing and preserving ordered character.
[Recursive inversion] Virtue begins as the condition for good friendship and correct pleasure, then becomes the product of the associations, pleasures, repetitions, and laws it authorizes.
[Absorption] Proportional exchange disappears as a dominant topic after establishing the broader rule that heterogeneous goods and claims require fitting judgment rather than numerical identity.

[Terminal transformation] Proper self-love is elevated from noble practical self-preference to living according to intellect, transforming ethical self-possession into contemplative self-actualization.
[Lower-layer local] Rules governing repayment, benefaction, dissolution, and role-specific obligations remain local adjudicative machinery rather than the cluster’s final architecture.
[Lower-layer local] The temporal completeness and supervenience of pleasure remain a specialized ontology, but they supply the affective mechanism required by the larger formation circuit.

[Scales upward] Classification by friendship-object and classification by completed activity combine into a general rule: ethical evaluation must identify what a relation or affect actually actualizes.
[Scales upward] Rational self-authority organizes psychic concord, proper self-love, pleasure judgment, and the hierarchy culminating in contemplation.
[Bridge] Shared activity and proper pleasure connect interpersonal ethics to character formation because repeated enjoyable co-action makes relational life disposition-producing.
[Bridge] Political concord and legislation join intimate ethics to public formation: common action requires ordered desires, while law produces the habits enabling such action.
[Catalyst] The insufficiency of ethical argument converts descriptive hierarchy into an institutional problem concerning how agents capable of right pleasure and judgment are produced.
[Recoded] The oppositions between self-love and sacrifice, pleasure and virtue, and dependence and self-sufficiency are superseded by distinctions among kinds and levels of rational activity.
The good cannot be represented by one homogeneous scale of pleasure, utility, exchange value, or quantitative return.
Immediate desire and experienced pleasure do not validate themselves, because corrupted character can misidentify both the lovable and the pleasant.
Happiness is neither passive possession nor solitary enjoyment; it requires sustained activity whose human exercise remains socially and materially conditioned.
The person is not a flat aggregate of desires or merely the embodied social compound; normative identity requires the authority of rational activity.
Ethical relation is not exhausted by exact equivalence, enforceable contract, or unrestricted availability to every claimant.
Association, pleasure, and repetition are not morally neutral media because each can strengthen or deform the activities and dispositions it carries.
Knowledge, exhortation, and private choice cannot independently produce stable virtue in agents whose pleasures and desires remain unformed.
External goods are neither the final constituents of happiness nor dispensable accidents; they are subordinate enabling conditions for embodied activity.
Atomistic anthropology must be false: an isolated, preformed individual cannot generate complete friendship, stable character, or fully actualized human happiness.
Aggregative hedonism must be false: pleasures cannot be summed independently of the activities, characters, and relations that give them species and value.
Static substantialism must be false: selfhood, friendship, and happiness exist normatively only through temporally sustained and repeatedly actualized activity.
Procedural universalism must be false: no context-independent algorithm can determine heterogeneous duties, proper pleasures, or competent legislation.
Ethical intellectualism must be false: correct propositions cannot bypass affective habituation, associative reinforcement, and coercively supported repetition.
The separation of ethics from politics must be false: the quality of judgment presupposed by private virtue depends upon social and legal structures capable of reproducing character.
A value-neutral institution must be impossible, because laws necessarily organize repeated actions, pleasures, aversions, and practical perceptions toward some conception of the human end.
The autonomous subject prior to formation is unavailable: the agent who judges correctly is already the outcome of rational discipline, intimate association, affective habituation, and law.
A neutral foundation for normativity remains absent because the virtuous person measures proper pleasure while proper pleasure and habituation help produce the virtuous person.

A complete reconciliation of social and contemplative happiness is unavailable: the highest activity claims relative independence while relying upon the embodied, relational, and political order it ranks as secondary.

Otherness irreducible to evaluative likeness remains structurally inadmissible, because complete friendship is formalized through another self and preserved only under sufficient character similarity.
A spontaneous, noncoercive passage from mass appetite to stable civic virtue is treated as unavailable.
Final practical closure is withheld: contextual obligation lacks fixed weights, coercion lacks a legitimacy threshold, and legislative science requires further comparative inquiry.
Shared activity becomes a pleasure-mediated formation circuit: proper pleasure strengthens the activities friends perform together, and repeated co-activity assimilates their characters.
The virtuous friend functions as an interpersonal extension of the virtuous-person measure by making another excellent life perceptible, enjoyable, and available for imitation.
Law scales the formative function of co-living beyond friendship’s finite circle by organizing repeated activity and affect where reciprocal intimacy is impossible.
Political concord presupposes affective formation: shared practical judgment cannot stabilize unless citizens have first learned to enjoy noble action and reject disgraceful action.
Human self-sufficiency becomes tiered: friendship constitutes practical completeness, contemplation minimizes interpersonal dependence, and both continue to require external support.
Noble sacrifice and contemplation become two forms of rational self-priority, but the hierarchy of happiness subordinates socially sacrificial action to intellectual actualization.
Politics has a double status: it is constitutive of practical virtue because it forms character, yet instrumental to a contemplative end represented as superior to political activity.

External goods are reclassified as relationally allocated conditions of activity: practical judgment governs their distribution, while their value remains subordinate to the excellent actions they enable.

Ethical corruption can cascade across scales: foreign pleasure weakens good activity, repetition stabilizes vice, vice divides the self, and divided agents reproduce defective association and civil strife.
The ethical subject is distributed across nested sites of agency: rational self-order, intimate friendship, shared activity, affective reinforcement, material provision, and legal formation.
Autonomy is an achieved dependence: self-rule emerges only through formative relations and institutions, after which it can exercise a limited independence within contemplation.

Normative authority is recursively reproduced rather than externally grounded: formed agents identify excellent activities, and excellent activities reinforced by association and law form such agents.

Intimacy and legislation are complementary technologies of ethical reproduction: friendship supplies dense reciprocal formation, while law supplies extensive but thinner population-scale coordination.

The system contains three interacting temporalities: pleasure completes the present activity, habituation and friendship accumulate path-dependent character, and happiness is judged across sustained life.
Politics is simultaneously infrastructure and subordinate activity: it produces the character and leisure required by the highest life while being denied the status of primary happiness.

Practical philosophy becomes an architecture of condition-production rather than a set of commands, because action depends upon structured pleasures, relationships, habits, laws, and material supports.
The highest end depends causally upon the lower-order social matrix it normatively demotes, making contemplative superiority structurally reliant on practical and political life.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Rational self-concord enables stable friendship; friendship’s shared activity then reinforces the desires and choices constituting rational self-concord.
Activity generates proper pleasure; proper pleasure strengthens attention and persistence; repetition stabilizes disposition; disposition selects the next activity.
Virtuous character selects virtuous friends, shared life assimilates character, and the resulting character preserves or dissolves the friendship that formed it.
Law forms habits, habits produce reason-responsive agents, and experienced virtuous judgment supplies the legislative expertise by which law is revised.

The principal escalation path runs from disputed goods and feelings to activity-classification, from activity to rational hierarchy, from hierarchy to character, and from character to institutional reproduction.

Activity is the dominant conceptual attractor: friendship, pleasure, virtue, happiness, contemplation, and legislation are each evaluated by the activities they constitute, complete, sustain, or produce.

Self-sufficiency spirals rather than stabilizes: social activity supplies practical completeness, contemplation reduces immediate dependence, and contemplation’s material prerequisites return it to social and political support.
The transition from finite friendship to public law is a phase change from reciprocal participation to asymmetrical institutional formation, not a simple enlargement of intimacy.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Misclassified friendship or pleasure → divergent expectations and judgments → dispute, distraction, or corruption.
Identify enduring object or completed activity → differentiate species → derive the relation’s or pleasure’s proper value.
Establish rational authority → order desire, pleasure, and choice → produce psychic concord and proper self-love.
Psychic concord → extension toward another self → shared excellent activity → reciprocal perception and affective reinforcement.
Repeated activity plus proper pleasure → habituated disposition → stable practical judgment → reproduction or deformation of character.
Finite intimate formation → population-scale insufficiency → legal coercion and public habituation → political concord and legislative expertise.
Excellent activity → practical social happiness → ascent to authoritative intellect → contemplation as primary happiness under material qualification.
Contemplative end plus formative dependency → demand for laws, regimes, and habits capable of sustaining the agents and leisure that contemplation presupposes.
Heterogeneous exchanges, attachments, and pleasures generate conflict when treated as commensurable or self-validating.
Conflict → taxonomic correction by friendship-object, activity-species, character, and relational role.
Taxonomic correction → relocation of value from acquired goods and sensations to excellent activity.
Excellent activity → rational self-order → proper pleasure, stable choice, and capacity for friendship.
Rationally ordered friendship → shared activity → reciprocal moral assimilation and practical social happiness.
Practical social happiness → hierarchy of authoritative activities → contemplation as primary and practical virtue as secondary happiness.
Normative hierarchy → recognition that knowledge cannot form its own receptive subject → habituation and coercive law.
Law-governed formation → legislative expertise → comparative political inquiry as the nonfinal closure of practical philosophy.
Value is relocated from goods possessed and feelings undergone to activities performed, sustained, completed, and reproduced.
The boundary between self and other becomes operational rather than absolute: the friend extends self-perception, while institutions participate in forming the capacities attributed to the self.
Self-sufficiency is remapped from independence to a hierarchy of organized dependencies ranging from intimate reciprocity to contemplative relative autonomy.
Friendship and law become scale-differentiated mechanisms of one formative architecture rather than separate private and public domains.
Politics is reclassified from external administration into the institutional production of agents capable of practical virtue and, indirectly, contemplative life.
Time is differentiated into present completion, cumulative habituation, relational path dependence, and whole-life endurance.

The oppositions pleasure versus virtue, egoism versus sacrifice, and self-sufficiency versus dependence collapse into distinctions among better and worse activities and modes of rational self-realization.
Practical disputes become diagnostic instruments: disagreement over repayment, pleasure, or education reveals deeper errors concerning activity, character, personhood, and formation.
Surface level — The system adjudicates unequal friendship, conflicting duties, self-love, pleasure, happiness, contemplation, habituation, and legislation.
Structural level — Activities organize objects, pleasures, relationships, dispositions, and institutions into recursive circuits of ethical reproduction.

Metastrategic level — Ethical intervention shifts from issuing correct propositions to classifying activities and constructing relational, affective, and legal conditions under which correct action becomes desirable.

Ontological / Temporal level — The person is authoritative rational activity; pleasure completes present activity, habituation accumulates character, friendship extends reflexive life, and happiness requires sustained actualization.

Methodological / Performative level — The inquiry repeatedly converts practical paradoxes into distinctions, then converts those distinctions into formative mechanisms, finally performing its claim that ethical theory must exceed knowledge in action and politics.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: Relational happiness requires virtuous friends, while complete happiness privileges contemplation for requiring fewer co-agents; the hierarchy does not fully reconcile these claims.

The rational self shifts from an integrated practical agent into intellect as the highest self, threatening to demote the embodied and relational activities through which rational character was formed.
The virtuous person measures genuine pleasure, but virtuous character is itself formed through pleasure, repetition, friendship, and law, leaving normative authority partly circular.
Law requires coercive power to form resistant desire, but no criterion separates rational habituation from oppressive enforcement.

Practical judgment remains indispensable but underformalized because no thresholds determine excessive inequality, incurable vice, sufficient material support, or the correct weighting of heterogeneous claims.
Complete friendship loves another as another self while conditioning continuity upon goodness and similarity, leaving radical difference and unconditional personal attachment unintegrated.
Pleasure is said to complete and strengthen activity without being identical to it, but the causal form of this supervenient relation remains unspecified.
Self-sufficiency mutates from socially actualized completeness into contemplative relative independence, then returns to dependence through bodily and institutional prerequisites.
Pleasure mutates from an affect ordered by virtue into a species-specific completion that actively reinforces or displaces the activity producing it.
Political concord mutates from shared judgment among citizens into a problem of legally producing citizens capable of shared judgment.
Proper self-love mutates from choosing noble practical action into identifying oneself most fully with contemplative intellect.
Friendship’s formative function is absorbed into a larger institutional architecture when finite co-living proves incapable of producing virtue at civic scale.
Reality appears as a nested feedback machine: rational ordering operates within the person, reciprocal imitation within friendship, and organized repetition within law.
The subject is not an isolated substance but an authoritative activity-node whose desires, pleasures, associates, and institutions continually stabilize or divide it.
Time is layered: pleasure seals the present act, repeated association sediments character, and happiness names the sustained trajectory of a life.
Ethical struggle consists in controlling formative circuits by selecting activities, companions, pleasures, habits, laws, and material conditions that reinforce rational activity.
Contemplation functions as the machine’s upper attractor, but it remains mounted upon the social, bodily, and political substrate whose activity it claims to exceed.

The cluster is reconstructible from six indispensable structures: activity-indexed value, rational self-authority, affective reinforcement, relational formation, qualified self-sufficiency, and legal-political reproduction.
The architecture is strongest where shared activity, proper pleasure, habituation, and law form a continuous multiscalar account of character production.
The architecture remains underdetermined at the junction between friendship-dependent practical happiness and relatively self-sufficient contemplative happiness.
Coherence is real but qualified: rational activity unifies the system, while the identity of the rational person, the authority of virtue, and the legitimacy of coercion remain unstable.

Reconstruction preserves the actual movement because local disputes progressively disclose psychic order, formative association, activity hierarchy, and institutional necessity rather than merely accumulating topics.

Practical fittingness remains resistant to axiomatic reduction: lived facts, experienced particulars, and situational judgment cannot be replaced by the formal architecture that establishes their necessity.

The central problem is to connect happiness as rationally excellent activity with the formed, socially mediated, and context-sensitive agency capable of selecting and realizing the good in particular circumstances.

The governing thesis is that flourishing is sustained excellent activity generated by the convergence of habituated character, right desire, attributable choice, relational justice, and truth-attaining practical judgment.
At this scale, the argument becomes a civic-teleological theory of practical production and correction rather than either a deduction from first principles or a catalogue of virtues.
Its directional movement is ordered ends → human function → habituated character → voluntary choice → domain-sensitive calibration → justice and institutional mediation → practical wisdom.
Action is the principal relay: it realizes the end, expresses and reproduces character, enters relations of justice, and becomes correct only through perceptive determination of particulars.
Political order is internal to practical excellence because it forms agents, distributes conditions of action, coordinates reciprocal relations, applies law, and corrects universal rules.

The movement is recursively spiral and path-dependent: action forms character, character shapes ends, judgment returns universals to particulars, and institutional correction renews rather than completes the normative order.

Closure is practical and internally circular: the formed prudent agent supplies determinacy, while the criteria of correct formation remain incompletely independent and contemplative superiority reopens the hierarchy of fulfilment.
[Persistent] Practical life is end-ordered, and its non-vain hierarchy terminates in happiness as rationally excellent activity across a complete life.
[Attractor] Action is the generative nexus through which the human good is actualized, character is disclosed and reproduced, relations are ethically structured, and responsibility is transmitted.
[Persistent] Virtue is not possession, capacity, conformity, or isolated success but a stable organization of desire, choice, affect, perception, and activity.
[Emergent] Character is recursively productive and epistemically active: prior conduct forms dispositions that shape how ends appear and thereby condition later desire, judgment, and action.
[Mutating] Practical reason operates by educating appetite into right desire and then integrating that desire with deliberation, perception, and command.
[Persistent] Ethical attribution depends on internal causal contribution, relevant knowledge, voluntary choice, motive, end, and formed state rather than outward deed alone.
[Terminal] Practical universals terminate in perception of particulars because no formula can predetermine every relevant object, relation, circumstance, or exception.
[Emergent] Complete practical correctness requires reciprocal unity between virtue, which makes the end right, and practical wisdom, which truthfully determines and commands its realization.
[Persistent] Human agency is socially formed yet causally attributable: institutions condition character and opportunity without wholly replacing the agent as a source of action.
[Emergent] Justice externalizes character virtue into relation-specific structures of lawfulness, distribution, rectification, exchange, and equitable correction.
[Mutating] Ethical measure is differentiated rather than univocal: qualitative fit, proportional equality, arithmetic repair, reciprocal commensuration, and prudent judgment govern distinct fields.
[Emergent] Law possesses practical authority only as a corrigible universal whose purpose can be restored when unforeseen particulars defeat literal application.
[Mutating] Ethical time is cumulative and asymmetrical: conduct sediments into character, settled character conditions future possibility, and deliberation remains directed toward contingent futures.
[Persistent] External goods and political arrangements condition the exercise and distribution of excellence without becoming intrinsic measures of virtue or happiness.
[Attractor] The good, noble, just, right, and fitting form a linked end-selecting attractor that orients practical calibration without receiving a fully independent specification.

[Terminal] Practical integration completes the account of action within the shared contingent world, but theoretical wisdom retains a superior object and prevents practical flourishing from becoming the final undivided form of rational completion.
[Stable identity → expansion] The good persists as the governing end but expands from terminal happiness into the character-shaped end of wish and the right end that practical wisdom must realize.

[Serial mutation] Virtue moves from functional excellence, to habituated mean disposition, to determinate affective excellence, to complete virtue in relation with others, and finally to reciprocal unity with practical wisdom.

[Functional recurrence → expansion] Activity first constitutes happiness, then produces and reveals character, then acquires relational and institutional consequences governed by justice and practical judgment.

[Mutation] Reason moves from the rational ordering of appetite, through an initially unexplained standard of right reason, into an integrated capacity joining true judgment, right desire, experience, and command.

[Domain migration] The mean migrates from character formation into specific affective fields, then into relational equality and legal correction, and finally into the judgment of the practically wise agent.
[Escalation] Politics moves from architectonic ordering and habituation into the institutional organization of justice, resources, law, judgment, and the conditions of personal prudence.
[Escalation] Particularity develops from a limit on ethical exactness into the determinant of contextual means, exceptions to law, and the terminal object of practical perception.

[Reversal and redistribution] External goods shift from vulnerable conditions of happiness into instruments of virtue, objects of allocation and exchange, and politically distributed conditions of future action.

[Absorption after structural work] Pleasure and pain cease to dominate as named operators after their formative and diagnostic functions are absorbed into right desire, stable character, and practically truthful choice.

[Displacement] Rejection of a separate Good relocates normative authority into function, character, prudent perception, and political order, thereby converting transcendence into an unresolved immanent circularity.

[Terminal transformation] Happiness initially governs the hierarchy as practical excellent activity, but contemplation later introduces a superior object that cannot be fully absorbed into the civic-practical architecture.

[Local] The detailed classifications of force, ignorance, courage, and temperance remain lower-layer analyses; their scalable residue is the conjunction of causal origin, knowledge, selected means, and ordered affect.
[Local] The catalogues of generosity, magnificence, magnanimity, anger, sociability, truthfulness, and wit remain demonstrations of domain-sensitive calibration rather than independent foundations.

[Local] Geometric distribution, arithmetic rectification, monetary commensuration, and rational-state taxonomies remain specialized operators whose differentiation, not whose specific labels, scales upward.
[Scaled] The action–character recursion and the universal–particular recursion scale upward as the two principal engines of practical formation and correction.
[Bridge] The education of appetite into right desire bridges habituation, noble choice, and the practical wisdom that joins correct ends to executable means.
[Bridge] Political formation scales into justice because institutions do not merely habituate individuals; they organize reciprocal relations, distribute goods, and administer corrigible universals.
[Catalyst] The underdetermination of right reason and true appearance generates the demand for practical wisdom as experienced perception, deliberation, judgment, and command.
[Superseded] Virtue as a generic mean state is recoded into a differentiated architecture requiring right end, relational fit, voluntary choice, institutional location, and prudent determination.
[Superseded] Evaluation by visible deed or outcome is replaced by reconstruction of motive, knowledge, control, desire, character, relation, law, and formative history.
[Terminal boundary] Contemplative superiority scales upward as a limit on practical completion but remains insufficiently integrated to reorganize the preceding civic-ethical machinery.
Happiness cannot be an instrumental possession, passive state, external reputation, isolated success, or episodic enjoyment.
Ethical normativity cannot be grounded in a separate universal Good, a single arithmetic mean, or any rule detached from heterogeneous practical domains.
Correct action cannot be generated by theoretical knowledge, verbal instruction, formal cognition, or instrumental calculation without habituated desire and perception.
Moral status cannot be read directly from outward conduct, magnitude, success, injury, conformity, or possession.
Character can be neither a fixed natural substance nor the product of an unconditioned, self-originating choice.
Virtue does not eliminate appetite, pleasure, pain, fear, anger, or desire; it organizes their objects, degrees, relations, occasions, and ends.
Flourishing cannot be private or atomistically self-sufficient because formation, justice, exchange, law, and political association enter its conditions of realization.
Agency cannot be reduced either to freedom from all conditions or to passive determination by appetite, institutions, pressure, fortune, and social position.
No exhaustive legal or decision procedure can abolish the remainder generated by contingent particulars.
External goods, wealth, honor, office, and recognition cannot confer virtue even though they condition its scope and exercise.
The architecture excludes ethical intellectualism and formalism: practical truth cannot exist independently of formed desire, experience, and perceptual access to particulars.
It excludes behavioralism and surface consequentialism because ethical identity depends on causal and motivational structures invisible in the material description of a deed.
It excludes a synchronic model of the subject because character, capability, responsibility, prudence, and flourishing are effects of cumulative temporal formation.
It excludes private moral atomism because the agent’s ends, opportunities, relations, resources, classifications, and corrective practices are politically mediated.
It excludes sovereign legalism and pure conventionalism alike: law binds, yet its authority remains answerable to natural, proportional, purposive, and equitable correction.
It excludes ethically neutral instrumental reason because efficient selection of means becomes practical wisdom only when character supplies a genuinely good end.
It excludes universal commensurability: goods, virtues, persons, relations, and rational activities cannot be reduced to one homogeneous scale without destroying their operative distinctions.
It excludes a self-sufficient practical monism because political action and contemplation remain distinct modes of rational completion with no frictionless reduction of one to the other.
The deepest absent object is an independent criterion of the good, noble, fitting, just, and right after normative authority has been relocated into formed character and prudent judgment.
A fully self-grounding origin of the practical agent is unavailable because habituation, law, experience, character, choice, and practical wisdom presuppose one another.
A neutral standpoint outside habituated desire, affect, political formation, and character-shaped appearance is unavailable to practical judgment.
An invulnerable human good is unavailable because flourishing remains embodied, temporally extended, materially conditioned, relationally distributed, and politically exposed.
A perfectly exhaustive common measure is unavailable: no metric simultaneously orders intrinsic excellence, distributive merit, heterogeneous goods, political status, and contemplative rank.
A complete legal closure is impossible because contingent action preserves an irreducible zone that no prior universal can fully classify.
Universal reciprocal personhood remains unavailable because the architecture’s fullest justice presupposes a political boundary that excludes dependent household relations.
A final unity of practical and contemplative fulfilment is unavailable because practical wisdom completes action without governing the superior object of theoretical wisdom.

Because happiness consists in excellent activity and general ethical structure terminates in particulars, practical wisdom is not an auxiliary virtue but the operational condition for realizing the chief good.

The action–character loop becomes an adaptive calibration system: activity forms dispositions, dispositions select ends, and prudent perception varies execution without abandoning rational orientation.
Political order becomes a distributed normative ecology that forms agents, structures relations, allocates enabling goods, applies law, repairs universals, and administers attribution.
Conditioned agency remains attributable only if social formation and institutional mediation shape but do not exhaust the agent’s causal contribution.
Justice is the relational externalization of flourishing: character excellence becomes complete toward others only through differentiated equalities and law-governed association.
Practical truth is itself an ethical-political achievement because the perceiver capable of seeing the right end and fitting means must have been formed through prior activity and institutions.
Distribution and exchange mediate the realizability of happiness by organizing access to resources, recognition, association, and future opportunity without determining intrinsic excellence.

Complete-life flourishing and practical judgment share an asymmetrical temporality: a sedimented past shapes present perception, while deliberation and institutional provision organize contingent futures.

The circularity of the standard intensifies across the architecture: good character discloses the true good, practical wisdom depends on good character, and political order is judged through agents whose formation it governs.
Practical completion remains structurally non-final: civic excellence realizes happiness in action, yet contemplation introduces a superior object that practical reason cannot subsume.
Human flourishing is a dynamically stable civic-practical circuit in which excellent activity reproduces the character, judgment, relations, and institutions required for its continuation.
Practical truth is not detached representation but a formed capacity to align real ends, right desire, contingent means, relational obligations, and executable command.
The ethical subject is a diachronic causal history and relational node: formed before mature choice, active in reproducing its character, and embedded in institutions that classify its actions.
Freedom becomes conditioned practical authorship: the capacity to originate attributable action from formed desire while remaining corrigible through reflection, law, and experience.
Ethics and politics become internally distinct but inseparable operations: ethics forms and directs character, while politics organizes the relational and material world in which character can act.
Corrigibility becomes a condition of normative authority: rules, habits, and judgments remain valid only insofar as they preserve orientation toward the good through changing particulars.
Material distribution is ethically indirect but structurally decisive because it controls the field of possible excellent activity without constituting excellence itself.
Vice is an epistemic-practical deformation: malformed character distorts the apparent end, while instrumental intelligence may then optimize the realization of that distorted end.

Rational fulfilment possesses a bifurcated architecture: practical excellence integrates embodied and political life, while contemplation preserves an object whose superiority destabilizes practical finality.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Happiness requires excellent activity → excellent activity requires virtue → activity forms virtue → formed virtue sustains the activity constituting happiness.
Action → character → appearance of the good → wish → deliberation → practical command → action forms the expanded agency loop.
Pleasure and pain → habituated desire → apparent end → practical reasoning → choice → renewed pleasure and pain joins affective formation to prudential action.
Universal norm → unforeseen particular → perceptual or equitable correction → restoration of normative purpose → renewed non-exhaustive universal forms the correction loop.
Political law → habituated citizen → prudent judgment → legislation or equitable application → preserved political order → renewed formation forms the agent–polity loop.
External resources → allocation and exchange → opportunities for action → virtuous or vicious use → altered association and future distribution forms the material-relational loop.
Ranked ends → happiness → function → virtue → habituation → attributable choice → relational justice → practical wisdom marks the principal escalation from teleology to civic-practical intelligence.
The good–noble–just–right–fitting complex is the central attractor around which function, affect, mean, law, equality, deliberation, and action converge.
Repeated conceptual division marks phase change: apparently unified terms are differentiated by domain and relation, then recomposed through the judgment capable of navigating those distinctions.

sections.name: Formal Generative Schema of the Whole Book

items.text: Plural purposive practices → hierarchy of ends → terminal governing good → happiness.
Distinctive human function → rational activity → excellent performance → need for virtue capable of sustaining activity across a life.
Natural receptivity → repeated affectively reinforced conduct → stable disposition → character-shaped appearance of ends.
Apparent good → wish → deliberation over contingent means → rational choice → attributable action.
Heterogeneous fields of action → excess and deficiency → qualitative calibration → differentiated character virtues.
Character virtue extended toward others → justice → differentiated equalities → institutional mediation of shares, injuries, and exchange.
Universal law + irreducible particular → misfit → equity → restored legislative purpose.
Right end supplied by character + experienced perception + deliberation + judgment + command → practical wisdom → correct choice.
Correct action → realization of the good + reproduction or correction of character + relational consequence + political attribution.
Sustained excellent activity under material and political conditions → qualified practical happiness → contemplative horizon that exceeds practical integration.
Purposive action → ordered ends → chief human good → happiness.
Happiness → rational function → excellent activity → demand for an account of virtue.
Natural receptivity → habituation → affective reinforcement → stable character → attributable choice.
Character virtue → heterogeneous domains → contextual calibration → concrete excellent action.
Social relation → justice → differentiated equality → distribution, rectification, exchange, and law.
Universal law → exceptional particular → equitable restoration of normative purpose.
Indeterminate right reason → differentiated rational capacities → practical wisdom → correct choice and command.
Sustained civic-practical excellence → recursive reproduction of agents and institutions → qualified happiness → unresolved contemplative superiority.
The good is reclassified from a detachable object into the governing end immanent to function, character, practical judgment, and sustained activity.
Virtue is reclassified from private self-command into a civic-relational organization of desire, perception, choice, action, and judgment.
Action is reclassified from a transient deed into an operator that realizes ends, manufactures character, enters justice relations, and carries responsibility across time.
The subject is reclassified from an isolated chooser into a formed causal history embedded in affective, legal, economic, and political relations.
Practical reason is reclassified from a homogeneous faculty or detachable rule into integrated right desire, experienced perception, deliberation, judgment, and command.
Politics is reclassified from external administration into the production, coordination, material enablement, correction, and attribution of practical agency.
Law is reclassified from final command into a purposive universal whose authority includes equitable correction by particulars.
Freedom is reclassified from independence from influence into informed, character-mediated causal contribution within conditioned relations.
Ethical time is redrawn as sedimented formation opening onto contingent futures rather than a sequence of independent and reversible decisions.
Moral reading becomes causal-relational reconstruction: visible conduct must be interpreted through formative history, desire, motive, knowledge, control, institutional location, and end.
[Surface] The system determines happiness, virtue, voluntary agency, courage, temperance, calibrated conduct, justice, law, equity, rational states, and practical wisdom.

[Structural] Hierarchies of ends, recursive habituation, character-shaped appearance, differentiated relations, institutions, and practical judgment form one distributed mechanism of excellent action.

[Metastrategic] Ethical intervention shifts from transmitting propositions or commands to forming desire, reconstructing agency, differentiating relations, distributing conditions, and correcting universals.

[Ontological / Temporal] The human being is an embodied, social, path-dependent cause acting within contingent futures, while rational reality also includes necessary objects exceeding practical governance.

[Methodological / Performative] The system performs its doctrine by beginning with rough universals, dividing terms by domain and relation, testing them against particulars, and returning closure to trained judgment.

sections.name: Internal Tensions, Mutation Points, and Fault Lines

items.text: The good agent discloses the true end, yet good agency is identified by correct orientation toward that end; practical wisdom and political order inherit rather than eliminate this circularity.
Political and educational formation precedes mature choice, yet responsibility requires the formed subject to remain an originating cause rather than an institutional product.
Happiness and virtue possess intrinsic worth, yet their exercise depends on fortune, resources, recognition, distribution, office, and political stability.
Contextual variability resists universal decision procedures, yet intrinsically bad acts, natural justice, and the objectively noble impose boundaries not generated by context alone.
Law must bind as a universal while equity must depart from its letter; the architecture supplies purposive correction but no final criterion governing every conflict between rule and exception.
Justice completes virtue toward others while restricting full reciprocal jurisdiction to a politically qualified class, making universality depend on prior exclusion.
Developed virtue and practical wisdom are mutually necessary, but their reciprocal dependence leaves the developmental emergence of either incompletely explained.
Practical wisdom is indispensable to human flourishing and political order, yet theoretical wisdom remains superior in object and incompletely integrated with practical completion.
The good mutates from terminal end, to functional excellence, to character-shaped appearance, to the right end jointly validated by virtue and practical wisdom.
Virtue mutates from excellent activity and habituated mean state into relational justice and reciprocal unity with practical wisdom.
The mean mutates from context-relative affective calibration into relation-specific equality and finally into experienced practical judgment.
Reason mutates from the ordering of appetite into an unexplained standard and then into a differentiated practical capacity integrating truth, desire, particulars, and command.
Politics mutates from architectonic coordination and habituation into the institutional infrastructure of justice, distribution, legal correction, and personal prudence.
External goods mutate from vulnerable conditions of happiness into instruments, distributable shares, media of association, and constraints on future practical possibility.
Completion mutates from complete-life happiness into complete virtue toward others and complete practical wisdom, before being destabilized by contemplative superiority.

Reality appears as a civic-teleological self-correcting feedback machine: ends orient action, action sediments character, character selects ends, institutions stabilize relations, and judgment repairs universals.
The subject appears as an embodied, habituated, desiring, perceiving, deliberating causal node that is neither sovereign over its formation nor passive within its institutional environment.
Time appears as sedimented yet open: character condenses prior action, present judgment inherits that formation, and deliberation navigates futures no rule can exhaust.
Possible navigation consists in habituating desire, preserving attributable choice, calibrating relations, correcting law, and sustaining right ends under material and political vulnerability.

The global axioms are sufficient to reconstruct the meta-cluster engine: chief good → excellent activity → habituated character → attributable choice → relational calibration → institutional justice → practical wisdom → recursive correction.

The architecture remains underdetermined concerning the independent content of the noble and right end, distributive merit, the best political order, and the genesis of the already formed prudent agent.
Coherence is strongest where action simultaneously realizes the good, reproduces character, enters social relations, and becomes corrigible through practical judgment.

Reconstruction depends on sequencing and recursive return because happiness requires virtue, virtue requires habituation, habituation requires attribution, relational action requires justice, and justice requires practical wisdom.
Situated perception remains indispensable and resistant to axiomatic reduction because it supplies the final discrimination among particulars that no extracted universal can perform.

The reconstruction preserves the actual movement only if social formation and responsibility, objective good and character-dependent appearance, universal law and equitable exception, material dependence and intrinsic excellence, and practical completion and contemplative superiority remain unresolved but operative.

identity.title: Ne L1 01
identity.context: Chapters 01–06 · Book I · Book II · Book III · Book IV · Book V · Book VI

items.text: The governing problem is how embodied agents can acquire, enact, sustain, and reproduce excellent activity when correct cognition and goodwill are neither self-enacting nor self-forming.

Flourishing is reconstructed as sustained excellent activity rather than disposition or possession, but such activity requires psychic mediation, fitting pleasure, companions, material support, and political order.
The architecture is recursively causal: character enables activity, activity elicits pleasure, pleasure reinforces repetition, and repeated relational or institutional activity reproduces character.
Classification by object, end, activity, principle, and measure converts apparent sameness among actions, pleasures, relations, and exchanges into hierarchically differentiated ethical forms.
Pleasure becomes the central feedback operator: it can capture action, complete worthy activity, stabilize association, or sediment vice according to the activity and character it reinforces.
Friendship and law are scale-differentiated mechanisms of ethical actuality: friendship supplies dense reciprocal co-activity, while law supplies extensive population-level habituation.

Self-sufficiency is repeatedly recoded as organized dependence: practical excellence requires shared life, while contemplation reduces immediate interpersonal dependence without escaping bodily and political support.

The dominant movement is spiral and scale-expanding: intrapersonal coordination becomes relational actuality, relational actuality becomes formative reproduction, and formative reproduction becomes institutional condition-production.
Closure is bifurcated and recursive: contemplation is installed as the highest activity, yet its dependency upon formed agents, leisure, goods, and law returns the terminal hierarchy to politics.
[Persistent] Ethical actuality belongs primarily to sustained excellent activity; a correct disposition, goodwill, or capacity remains incomplete while inactive.
[Persistent] Ethical species and value are determined by generative object, end, principle, activity, and measure rather than by surface action, affective intensity, or quantitative return.
[Mutating] The distinction between state and exercise expands into a formation circuit: dispositions govern activity, but repeated pleasurable activity also produces the dispositions that govern it.

[Mutating] Pleasure has no independent ethical valence; it operates as activity-indexed feedback capable of capturing, completing, strengthening, displacing, or reproducing the activity from which it arises.
[Emergent] Virtue is both cause and effect: it coordinates practical cognition and relation while being stabilized by proper pleasure, friendship, habituation, and law.
[Emergent] Rational self-rule is an achieved organization of embodied and relational dependence, not the spontaneous sovereignty of an isolated subject.
[Persistent] Heterogeneous impulses, persons, goods, and claims require fitting mediation by truth, proportion, role, and experienced practical judgment rather than mechanical sameness.

[Emergent] Embodied practical excellence is intrinsically relational because companions are co-agents, perceptual extensions, affective reinforcers, and formative influences rather than merely external aids.

[Emergent] Friendship and law belong to one multiscalar formative architecture but operate through different mechanisms: reciprocal participation at intimate scale and asymmetrical habituation at civic scale.

[Mutating] Self-sufficiency means freedom from merely remedial dependence within an organized field of constitutive dependence; even contemplative relative independence remains materially and politically conditioned.

[Terminal] Politics is constitutive condition-production: it distributes the goods and common activities needed for ethical actuality and forms the pleasures, habits, and judgments needed for ethical agency.
[Persistent] Practical truth reaches completion only through context-sensitive enactment; neither theoretical correctness nor universal classification can replace experienced judgment of particulars.

[Attractor] Activity is the system’s dominant attractor: virtue, pleasure, friendship, happiness, politics, and contemplation are ordered by the activities they enable, complete, sustain, reproduce, or constitute.

[Terminal] The hierarchy culminates in contemplation as the most continuous and self-final rational activity, but this culmination cannot terminate practical inquiry because its agents and conditions must be politically produced.
[Stable identity] Activity remains the primary bearer of ethical actuality from embodied action and shared life through practical happiness and contemplation.
[Stable identity] Classification by generative ground persists across psychic states, friendship species, pleasures, exchanges, and forms of happiness.
[Functional recurrence] The state/activity distinction migrates from inactive knowledge and friendship into character formation, where exercise not only actualizes but recursively produces the state.
[Mutation] Pleasure moves from captor or accompaniment of action to a causal feedback force governing attention, repetition, association, and character.

[Recursive inversion] Virtue begins as the stabilizing condition of excellent action and complete friendship, then returns as the sedimented product of pleasurable activity, co-living, habituation, and law.
[Expansion] Friendship expands from constitutive shared actuality into a technology of perception, imitation, affective reinforcement, and character assimilation.
[Migration] Co-living migrates from reciprocal intimate activity into legally organized repetition once friendship’s finite reach proves inadequate for population-scale formation.

[Escalation] Politics moves from the outer field enabling justice and shared activity to the formative mechanism that produces agents capable of practical judgment, and then becomes infrastructure for contemplation.

[Terminal transformation] Self-sufficiency changes from constitutive companionship without remedial need into contemplative relative independence, only to return to dependence through embodiment, leisure, goods, and institutions.
[Escalation with instability] The rational self moves from the ordering principle of a composite, permeable agent to intellect as the agent’s highest and quasi-divine identity.
[Absorption] Proportional exchange ceases to dominate after establishing the general requirement that heterogeneous goods and relations be governed by fitting, nonnumerical judgment.

[Displacement] Friendship-centred practical completion is displaced but not eliminated by contemplation; it survives as part of the formative and material substrate required by the supposedly more independent activity.

[Lower-layer local] The universal judgment–perceptual particular–bodily motion mechanism remains the local explanation of incontinence; the scalable proposition is that correct states require mediating interfaces to become action.
[Lower-layer local] Friendship species, repayment rules, benefaction disputes, and role-specific obligations remain local relational taxonomies rather than the final architecture.
[Lower-layer local → Scales upward] Pleasure’s specialized ontology remains local, but its activity-specific completion and reinforcement become the affective mechanism of ethical reproduction.
[Scales upward] The nonidentity of disposition and exercise becomes a general account of actuality, vulnerability, and formation across cognition, friendship, character, and happiness.
[Bridge] Proper pleasure links enactment to formation because it both completes worthy activity in the present and increases the probability of its repetition.
[Bridge] Friendship connects individual excellence to public formation by converting virtuous activity into shared perception, imitation, reinforcement, and durable character.
[Transition catalyst] The insufficiency of self-control, correct propositions, and private goodwill forces the shift from ethical instruction to the production of receptive desires and stable habits.
[Recoded] Politics changes from external support for ethical activity into the institutional reproduction of the capacities presupposed by ethical activity.
[Superseded] The autonomous, already formed chooser is replaced by a recursively produced agent whose rational authority depends upon prior affective, relational, and legal formation.

[Current-level terminal] Contemplation introduces a hierarchy not reducible to the formation circuit: it ranks the most relatively independent rational activity above the relational-practical matrix while continuing to depend upon that matrix.
Ethical actuality is not inferable from overt action, professed knowledge, goodwill, pleasure, or possessed character considered apart from enactment.
Correct knowledge and exhortation cannot independently command action or form stable desire.
Pleasure neither validates itself nor supplies a homogeneous measure of goodness; corrupted and excellent activities can both be affectively reinforced.
No common quantitative currency can determine heterogeneous ethical objects, benefits, obligations, activities, or pleasures.
Happiness is not a private possession, passive satisfaction, or solitary rational state insulated from embodiment and shared life.
Self-sufficiency is not autarky, because both practical and contemplative excellence require enabling bodily, material, relational, and political conditions.
Friendship, association, repetition, and law are not neutral containers; each reinforces a determinate organization of desire, action, and character.
Politics is not an external application of completed ethics, since it conditions present enactment and reproduces future agents.
Contemplative superiority does not entail causal independence from the practical order it normatively demotes.
Automatic rational sovereignty must be false: knowledge cannot govern action without practical mediation, and rational judgment cannot reproduce itself without formation.
Atomistic anthropology must be false: neither flourishing nor the agent capable of flourishing can be generated outside relational and institutional conditions.
Static substantialism and moral externalism must be false: ethical identity depends upon temporally sustained generative principles and activities rather than visible conduct or possessed properties.
Hedonistic monism must be false because pleasure derives its species and value from activity, character, and relation while recursively intensifying them.
Ethical formalism and procedural universalism must be false: no proposition, rule, contract, or algorithm can replace fitting judgment and habituated responsiveness to particulars.
Value-neutral mediation must be impossible: companions, pleasures, practices, and institutions necessarily form some pattern of desire and activity.
Atemporal excellence must be false because interruption, repetition, confidence, habituation, institutional continuity, and whole-life endurance alter what ethical states become in actuality.
A strict separation between ethics and politics must be false: private excellence depends upon public conditions, and public order depends upon the character it produces.
Seamless conversion is unavailable: no uninterrupted passage exists from knowledge to action, virtue to activity, goodwill to shared life, or law to good character.
A neutral origin of normative authority is absent: correction presupposes a surviving measure, while the agents capable of applying that measure are themselves products of norm-governed formation.
The preformed and autarkic subject is unavailable; agency exists only as vulnerable embodiment organized through prior relations, pleasures, habits, and institutions.
A universal ethical metric is unavailable because the system preserves irreducibly heterogeneous goods, relations, temporalities, and standards of fittingness.
Complete reconciliation between relational-practical and contemplative happiness is unavailable: the highest activity claims relative independence while relying upon the order it ranks below itself.

Radical otherness remains structurally unassimilated: complete friendship coordinates self-good and other-good through likeness without deriving their final identity or accommodating difference beyond shared evaluative form.
Spontaneous population-scale virtue is unavailable; civic formation requires organized repetition and coercive law where reciprocal intimacy cannot operate.
Final practical closure is withheld because no fixed procedure determines proportional merit, coercive legitimacy, sufficient support, or the correct weighting of heterogeneous claims.
Ethical dispositions are simultaneously preconditions and sedimented effects of activity: they must already guide enactment, yet they become stable only through repeated enactment.
Pleasure converts local action-quality into path-dependent character: what first interrupts or strengthens a present activity becomes, through repetition, a mechanism of future practical perception.
Friendship is both a constituent of flourishing and a formative regulator because companions co-enact excellence while making excellent life perceptible, enjoyable, and imitable.
Politics governs both sides of ethical actuality: it controls the conditions under which existing character can act and the processes through which future character is produced.
Repair becomes recursively conditioned: correction requires a preserved measure, but the capacity to retain and apply that measure depends upon the prior formation being corrected.
Human autonomy is achieved dependence: relational and institutional formation produces the self-governing agency later represented as relatively independent.
Ethical time is layered across momentary capture, present completion, cumulative habituation, relational duration, institutional reproduction, and whole-life judgment.
Law scales the formative function of friendship only by changing its mode from reciprocal co-participation to asymmetrical and potentially coercive organization.

Institutional corruption can create a multiscalar vice cascade: distorted public conditions organize defective pleasures and repetitions, which produce divided agents and reproduce defective association.
Contemplation is a dependent summit: its relative independence is causally generated by the embodied, relational, material, and political matrix it normatively subordinates.
Practical judgment becomes the irreducible operator connecting psychic truth, proportional reciprocity, allocation of external goods, and legislative competence.
The identity of the agent splits between a composite relational node and authoritative intellect, leaving uncertain whether the highest life perfects or abstracts from the formed human whole.

Ethical causality is circular but stratified: disposition governs activity, activity generates pleasure, pleasure drives repetition, repetition stabilizes character, and institutions organize the circuit’s future conditions.
Agency is a topology rather than a single locus, distributed across practical cognition, embodiment, companions, pleasures, material supports, and institutions.
Autonomy is not an initial power but the successful recursive closure of formative dependencies into stable rational self-government.
Practical philosophy becomes condition-production: intervention must organize the activities, affects, relations, habits, goods, and laws through which correct action becomes available and desirable.
Ethical defect can propagate between scales: failure at a perceptual or affective interface can sediment into character, association, institutional practice, and political disorder.
Ethical time is path-dependent: present pleasures alter future dispositions, durable relations alter practical perception, and institutions transmit these alterations beyond individual lifetimes.
Normative authority is immanent and recursively reproduced rather than externally secured, making its practical force dependent upon successful formation and vulnerable to circularity.

Contemplative superiority is infrastructurally dependent: the terminal end is not self-producing but requires lower-order practical and political systems to generate agents, leisure, and material support.

Effective repair must identify both the failed interface and the operative scale, since persuasion, companionship, habituation, institutional redesign, and political reform address different levels of the same distributed system.

sections.name: Recursive Loops, Escalation Paths, and Conceptual Attractors

items.text: Correct principle → fitting practical perception → excellent action → proper pleasure → repetition → stabilized character → renewed correct perception forms the primary enactment-formation loop.
Affective capture → defective action → reinforcing pleasure → repetition → divided character → defective association → institutional reproduction forms the principal escalation path of corruption.
Surviving measure → regret or dispute → persuasion and proportional correction → restored activity → renewed confidence forms the reparable-order loop.
